Experiments on software engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, and instruction following show that \texttt{PROBE} attains a coverage rate closer to the target level with tighter predictive bounds than a calibrated baseline.

papers.title: An Adaptive, Context-Aware, and Stacked Attention Network-Based Recommendation System to Capture Users' Temporal Preference
papers.abstract: Recommendation systems have become more important since the widespread use of the Internet. The large amount of information means that it is difficult for users to discover they really need. However, users' preferences can change over time because of the age and the impact of social networks. Recommendation systems must capture users' preferences and recommend suitable items, which is a difficult challenge. This study proposes a novel recommendation system that adapts to the changing preferences of users. By learning and adapting to users' changing preferences better recommendations are provided. This study uses context factors as additional information to model users' preferences more precisely. For the proposed recommendation system, the context is based on users' interaction items within each defined time interval. This study proposes two novel attention mechanisms for the recommendation system. The contextual item attention module captures contextual information, changing pattern in users' preference and the importance of items. The multi-head attention module extends the diversity of users' preferences and adapts to changing preferences. The recommendation performance is improved using additional item's temporal information to model the contextual item's representation. Experiments compare the proposed algorithm with several state-of-the-art recommendation methods using three real-world datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed context-aware recommendation model outperforms traditional methods and demonstrate the effectiveness with which contextual information is captured by the attention mechanism.

papers.title: Variance-Reduced Stochastic Hessian-Driven Nesterov Acceleration with Adam-Style Preconditioning
papers.abstract: Stochastic first-order methods use sampled gradients to reduce per-iteration costs, but estimation errors can slow convergence and, in some settings, cause divergence. To improve gradient accuracy while retaining acceleration, we develop scalar and diagonal versions of VR-Adam-SHANG for smooth stochastic convex optimization. The methods combine STORM-type recursive estimation, Adam-style preconditioning, and SHANG's accelerated interpolation and correction, using at most two stochastic gradient evaluations per iteration without full-gradient refreshes. Under unbiased sampling, bounded variance, and mean-square smoothness of gradient noise, polynomial steps with prescribed initialization yield $O(1/K)$ mean-square gradient-estimation error and expected objective-gap bounds combining $O(1/K^2)$ initial-energy decay with an $O(1/\sqrt K)$ stochastic term after $K$ iterations. These guarantees require neither monotonicity of the preconditioner nor a uniform positive lower bound on its eigenvalues. The analysis also establishes polynomial-step convergence of projected nonrecursive Adam-SHANG-s, filling a gap in its original theory. Experiments compare the methods at matched sample-gradient budgets. In every tested setting, at least one of the two versions achieves the lowest mean terminal objective gap among all compared methods.

papers.title: Strain Controlled Hydrogen Interstitial Site Preference and Hydride Phase Suppression in Epitaxial Vanadium
papers.abstract: Understanding hydrogen behavior in transition metals is crucial for energy storage and sensing technologies. Here we combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations with in-situ electrical measurements to reveal how epitaxial strain governs hydrogen interstitial site selection and phase stability in vanadium. Our calculations demonstrate a robust thermodynamic preference for tetrahedral (T) over octahedral (O) sites, with the energy difference modulated by lattice anisotropy through strain-tunable H 1s-V 3d orbital hybridization. Experimentally, epitaxial V films on MgO(001) exhibit a critical thickness-dependent crossover: 50 nm films show characteristic first-order alpha-beta hydride transitions, while 10 nm films display continuous solid-solution behavior with complete transition suppression. This crossover is governed by the progressive relaxation of epitaxial strain with increasing film thickness: the 10 nm films retain strong coherent strain that flattens the free-energy landscape and suppresses hydride nucleation, whereas the 50 nm films approach the strain-relaxed bulk limit where long-range elastic interactions restore first-order phase behavior. Finite-size truncation of elastic fields and interfacial electronic reconstruction further reinforce this dimensional crossover. Our work establishes a unified framework connecting atomic-scale orbital physics to mesoscopic phase thermodynamics, providing design principles for strain-engineered metal-hydride systems.

papers.title: WiFo-R: Wireless Foundation Model with Recurrent Channel Representation
papers.abstract: Wireless foundation models learn transferable channel state information (CSI) representations across heterogeneous wireless systems. However, conventional grid-aligned representations couple feature sequence length to CSI dimensions, restricting the allocation of representation capacity to different propagation conditions and task requirements while increasing inference overhead. This paper proposes WiFo-R, a wireless foundation model that learns progressive channel representations with selectable capacity. A channel-query cross-attention encoder aggregates spatial, temporal, and spectral CSI information, while parameter-shared recurrent updates refine existing channel features and introduce additional latent tokens. Multi-mask, multi-depth self-supervised pretraining equips intermediate states with strong reconstruction capabilities, followed by task-aligned post-training for channel estimation and CSI feedback. WiFo-R supports temporal and frequency-domain channel prediction, channel estimation, and variable-rate CSI feedback, and transfers to localization and LoS/NLoS classification. Experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution channel configurations demonstrate accurate reconstruction, progressive performance improvements, and strong transferability. A single feedback encoder--decoder supports six payload lengths at fixed quantization precision, while cross-attention and selectable recurrent depth improve the accuracy--complexity trade-off for large-scale CSI observations.

papers.title: Zero Replacement and Latent Profiles in Short Media Diaries: Checking Recording Status Before User Segmentation
papers.abstract: Short media diaries contain many zeros because many activities go unrecorded during the observation period. Log-ratio analysis of time allocation requires these zeros to be replaced with small positive values; as a result, all respondents who did not record an activity receive nearly the same value. We examined how such zero replacement affects classification in latent profile analysis and propose checks to perform before profiles are interpreted. Three-day diaries of 8,089 adults from the 2025 Korea Media Panel Survey were converted into nine-part time-use compositions. Gaming was not recorded by 88.9% of the respondents, and in every model with two to eight profiles and a covariance matrix held equal across profiles, respondents who recorded gaming and those who did not were classified into different profiles. Even when the replacement value equaled the minimum recording unit (5 min/day), the two-profile classification largely matched gaming recording status, and the two groups separated more sharply as the replacement value decreased, until the separation was complete. Before naming profiles, researchers should therefore check the proportion of respondents who did not record each activity and its replacement value, the same proportion within each profile, and the distribution of usage time among those who recorded the activity.

papers.title: Task-adaptive anonymisation enables privacy-preserving sharing of clinical speech data
papers.abstract: Clinical speech is increasingly used for disease screening and clinical assessment, but directly distributing speech recordings poses privacy risks because they contain both speaker-identifying voiceprints and sensitive spoken content. Existing speech anonymisation approaches are primarily developed for general speech applications or task-specific clinical speech and overlook that different clinical tasks rely on distinct speech characteristics, necessitating task-adaptive anonymisation strategies to protect patient privacy while preserving clinical utility. Here we introduce CASA, a clinically adaptive speech anonymisation agent that transforms anonymisation from a fixed processing procedure into a task-guided optimisation process, dynamically tailoring voiceprint and content anonymisation to task-specific privacy and clinical utility requirements. Through recursive self-improvement (RSI), CASA iteratively evaluates and refines anonymisation strategies against task-specific privacy and clinical utility requirements, while learning from these outcomes to guide more efficient planning in subsequent clinical tasks. CASA is validated across 14 clinical tasks encompassing five languages, diverse elicitation paradigms, and mental health, cognitive and voice disorders. CASA preserved disease-related classification performance while meeting speaker-anonymisation requirements across all clinical tasks, versus only 8/14 for the strongest fixed method. Assessments of resistance to speaker re-identification by external attackers and identification and redaction of sensitive personal information in clinical speech further demonstrated CASA's dual protection of speaker identity and sensitive spoken content. Clinical expert assessments further supported the preservation of clinically relevant information and the acceptability of anonymised speech for controlled research sharing.

papers.title: BiRefNet-V2: Rethinking Bilateral Reference for High-Resolution Dichotomous Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: Dichotomous image segmentation requires pixel-accurate foreground-background separation while preserving fine structures such as thin filaments, sharp edges, and intricate textures. BiRefNet addressed this challenge through bilateral references, combining image patches and gradient information, but its inward reference loses local spatial structure and lacks semantic guidance, while its outward reference relies on single-channel gradient attention. We recast this paradigm as controlled information recovery - locality determines what spatial information survives, semantic selectivity what information enters, and focused boundary supervision where refinement occurs - and propose BiRefNet-V2 to implement it: (1) locality-preserving and semantically guided detail injection through space-to-depth transformation, overlapping patches, and a Semantically Guided Gate; (2) a learned boundary stream with focused supervision that generates full-channel residual attention without requiring boundary annotations; and (3) a dual-branch decoder integrating depth-wise boundary convolutions with large-kernel attention. A modernized framework - LayerNorm, GELU, the Lion optimizer, and a DINOv3 backbone - cuts training from 600 to 50 epochs. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on DIS5K, camouflaged object detection, and high-resolution salient object detection across all 13 evaluation sets. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet-V2.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Stability of Weakly Asymmetric Burgers Vortices: A Circulation-Independent Asymmetry Threshold and Optimal Decay
papers.abstract: Burgers vortices are stationary solutions of the Navier--Stokes equations in a background straining flow and serve as a model for vortex tubes in three-dimensional turbulence. In this paper, we consider weakly asymmetric strains and establish the local nonlinear asymptotic stability of the corresponding Burgers vortices against small three-dimensional perturbations for arbitrary circulation. Our proof exploits the specific axial structure of the linearized operator, combining a two-dimensional resolvent analysis with decay estimates for axial derivatives to control the full three-dimensional evolution. A first-moment decomposition isolates the slow modes, and Gaussian resolvent bounds are transferred to polynomially weighted spaces. This yields nonlinear stability with the endpoint exponential decay rate $(1-\lambda)/2$, where $\lambda$ denotes the strain asymmetry, without any additional polynomial factor in time. An exact nonlinear first-moment law demonstrates that this rate is optimal over the full admissible perturbation class, including at zero circulation.

papers.title: Onsager--Machlup Theory and Transition Pathways for Degenerate Stochastic Systems with Multiplicative Noise
papers.abstract: Noise-induced transitions between metastable states are central to many nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems, and most probable transition pathways provide an effective means of revealing the underlying transition mechanisms. In this work, we develop an Onsager--Machlup framework for degenerate stochastic dynamical systems driven by multiplicative Gaussian noise. We first derive the Onsager--Machlup action functional for the additive-noise case using the Girsanov transformation, and then extend the result to multiplicative noise through a Lamperti-type transformation. The resulting functional provides a variational characterization of the most probable transition pathway, from which we derive the associated Hamilton--Pontryagin boundary value problem. We further recast the variational problem as an equivalent optimal control problem and propose a neural-network-based numerical method for computing the most probable transition pathways. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the theoretical framework and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed computational approach.

papers.title: Finite torsion in Hodge--Witt cohomology groups
papers.abstract: For a bounded coherent complex of graded modules over the Raynaud ring $R$, we compare three descriptions of finite torsion: Ekedahl's pieces $A_f^2$ and $A_{\SSpart}^1$ of the biduality filtration, the nilpotent and semisimple parts of the torsion of the Illusie--Raynaud c\oe ur, and the corresponding parts of the finite torsion $t^1$ of Ekedahl's diagonal cohomology. We show that finite torsion in bidegree $(0,i+1)$ measures the failure of the $i$th flat Artin--Mazur formal group to be smooth; we deduce that all flat Artin--Mazur formal groups of a Mazur--Ogus variety are smooth. For a smooth projective surface, we identify the three possible dual pairs in terms of the $p$-primary torsion of the geometric N\'eron--Severi group and the local-local and local-\'etale parts of the finite Picard quotient.

papers.title: Parametrizations of the solutions of Love equations and their momenta
papers.abstract: The Love equation is a paradigmatic example of a Fredholm integral equation of great interest in mathematics and physics, where its applications range from electrostatic problems to exactly solvable models for one-dimensional systems. In this work we propose a method to approximate the normalized solutions of Love equations of the first and second kind via a parametrization obtained by Hermite interpolation at Chebyshev nodes. Following the same approach, we also obtain approximations for the second, fourth and sixth momenta of the solution of the Love equations. We focus in particular on one-dimensional quantum gases described by the Lieb-Liniger and the Gaudin-Yang models. For these models, the solutions of Love equations correspond to the normalized densities of pseudorapidities. We show that remarkably accurate results can be obtained using the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation with a number of points as low as 17+2. In the case of the Lieb-Liniger model, we also propose a very accurate closed-form estimate of the dimensionless ground state energy valid for all values of the dimensionless interaction parameter incorporating known results for small and large couplings supplemented by the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation for intermediate couplings. As an application of this result, we compute the dimensionless local two-particle correlation function and the black soliton solutions of the Lieb-Liniger model.

papers.title: Theory of spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy with topological insulator tips
papers.abstract: Topological insulators have enabled a new class of spin-sensitive scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) probes based on helical boundary states. However, how these probes generate a net spin-polarized tunneling current remains unclear. We present a theory of spin-polarized STM with topological insulator tips and show that asymmetric tunneling-contact geometry and spin dephasing enable helical boundary states to generate a spin-polarized tunneling current. Within the standard Landauer-B\"uttiker formalism, we demonstrate this mechanism for a quantum spin Hall (QSH) insulator tip: asymmetric contacts make the two counter-propagating helical edge states, which carry opposite spins, traverse path lengths that differ by $\Delta L$, and spin dephasing induces backscattering that reduces the conductance more strongly for the longer path. For a representative asymmetric contact and weak spin dephasing, the QSH tip exhibits a tunneling spin polarization of $P_s=-17.2\%$ under positive bias, whose magnitude can reach $50\%$ for larger $\Delta L$, and which remains robust against Rashba spin-orbit coupling. Crucially, this polarization, dominated by helical edge transport rather than by bulk states, naturally reverses sign with the bias polarity owing to spin-momentum locking. Our findings are consistent with recent STM experiments using topological tips.

papers.title: ErosionBench: Probing Alignment Decay in Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: As enterprises delegate consequential work to multi-agent LLM systems, benign-looking requests can escalate into unsafe actions as they propagate across sessions through poisoned shared state, long-context documents, and trusted peer messages: no single message is malicious, yet the assembled tool action is. Prior benchmarks isolate a single agent under prompt injection or score multi-agent attacks by their final output, leaving cross-session erosion of shared state out of scope. We introduce ErosionBench, an environment-grounded benchmark that executes such attacks and verifies alignment decay at the process level, scoring the realized tool call against authorized intent and provenance with deterministic contracts, not output text. Each scenario is authored as a deterministic state graph before any prose is rendered, so every state change traces to a known cause. It spans four enterprise domains and four decay mechanisms across 1,728 scenarios with matched benign controls, labeled against the OWASP Top-10 for LLM Applications, plus 198 image-based attacks, each paired with a text equivalent, so a defense must survive the same attack in either channel. Perimeter defenses suppress attacks only by over-refusing 54-92% of legitimate work, so a low attack-success rate can conceal severe over-refusal. As a reference defense, we propose a calibrated Meta-Auditor pairing synchronous state checks with asynchronous trajectory monitoring; on a family-disjoint 906-scenario held-out split it reaches 98.5% recall at a 2.9% false-positive rate. Since it monitors trajectory, not surface content, its detection is channel-invariant: the strongest auditor flags image-delivered attacks about as reliably as their text equivalents (recall gap $\leq$2 points per model). Across GPT, Gemini, and Claude auditors, calibration keeps false positives low while recall tracks model capability, strongest for Claude.

papers.title: DuSS-PET: Self-Supervised Low-Dose PET Reconstruction Using Pseudo-Dual-Domain Consistency Without Paired Data
papers.abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) is pivotal in medicine and healthcare, but requires high radiation doses for quality imaging. Although deep learning has shown promise for low-dose PET reconstruction/enhancement, existing methods primarily rely on fully supervised learning, which requires paired low- and full-dose scans that are clinically impractical to obtain. To overcome this fundamental limitation, we propose DuSS-PET, a novel self-supervised PET reconstruction framework that operates without any paired low- and full-dose data. Our method is built upon a computational Noisier2Noise (Nr2N) paradigm, featuring a Bernoulli corruption strategy that serves as an image-space approximation to emulate low-count noise patterns in image-derived pseudo-sinogram representations. The DuSS-PET framework integrates three core components: an adaptive Swin transformer for pseudo-sinogram restoration, a plug-and-play module for image enhancement, and a consistency-constrained SSL strategy that enforces agreement between the pseudo-sinogram and image representations. Extensive experiments on multi-center datasets demonstrate that DuSS-PET achieves superior reconstruction performance, outperforming state-of-the-art SSL methods and achieving comparable or even better results than fully supervised approaches across various dose levels. In particular, it exhibits exceptional generalization across different scanner vendors. This work is among the first self-supervised low-dose PET reconstruction framework that enforces consistency between reconstructed images and pseudo-sinograms, where the pseudo-sinogram generated in the image space serves as a solid computational consistency constraint for enhanced imaging without full-dose training scans. The source code will be publicly available at https://github.com/ladderlab-xjtu/DuSS-PET.

papers.title: The geometry of anisotropic propagation for multidimensional reaction-diffusion equations in shifting habitats: A zero-sum stopping game approach
papers.abstract: We study the propagation geometry of multidimensional reaction-diffusion equations in shifting habitats. Using geometric optics techniques and viscosity solution theory, we prove that the associated rate functions converge locally uniformly to the unique viscosity solution of a variational inequality with singular initial data. We identify this limit as the value of a zero-sum stopping game whose zero set determines the Wulff shape. This zero set coincides with that of the positive part of the value function of an unconstrained optimal control problem if and only if Freidlin's condition holds. When Freidlin's condition fails, we derive a pointwise characterization of the stopping-game zero set, yielding a convex hull representation. These results then yield explicit Wulff shapes and directional spreading speeds for all habitat speed. As the habitat speed increases, the Wulff shape evolves from a large ball to a truncated ball. It then develops conical, cylindrical, and paraboloidal boundary components attached to spherical parts, before eventually becoming a smaller ball. Some of these geometric transitions occur while both axial spreading speeds remain unchanged. Moreover, by characterizing the optimal trajectories, we distinguish two mechanisms of nonlocal speed selection and show that such selection can occur in oblique directions even when it is absent in both axial directions.

papers.title: Beyond Node Attributes: A Controlled Evaluation and Ablation of Local Interaction Statistics for Ethereum Phishing Detection
papers.abstract: Methods for detecting phishing accounts on Ethereum are usually evaluated as complete pipelines that differ in features, architecture, and training protocol, which makes the contribution of interaction information hard to isolate. This paper evaluates the Unlabeled Feature Extension (UFE), a block of 12 local interaction statistics computed from each account's incoming and outgoing call and transfer edges without reading class labels. UFE is appended to the 14 source features of HEIG-Phish and tested with six model families: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, LightGBM, Graph Attention Network, GraphSAGE, and Meta-IFD. Within each pair of Baseline and Plus variants, the data partition, model configuration, random seed, decision threshold, and sampled neighborhoods are identical; only the input feature block changes. Across 20 predetermined stratified partitions of the same 2,763 labeled externally owned accounts, UFE increased test Macro-F1 by 1.0 to 9.1 percentage points across the six models. Every pair improved on all 20 partitions, all Nadeau-Bengio corrected 95% confidence intervals lie above zero, and the false-positive rate decreased for all six models. An exact-edge Random Forest ablation over 10 predetermined partitions associates most of the gain with the incoming transfer-edge sum attribute; once this feature is present, an incremental contribution of the remaining 11 UFE columns was not established. The results support reporting feature-augmented baselines alongside graph models, but they show stability under re-partitioning of one static, transductive benchmark rather than temporal or cross-dataset generalization.

papers.title: Beating the Probabilistic Bound for Hashing and Improving Lower Bounds for Trifferent Codes
papers.abstract: We improve the probabilistic lower bounds on the rates of hash codes and list-recoverable codes. For perfect $q$-hashing, we prove $R_q>B_q$ for every $q\geq 3$. Our main result concerns non-perfect hashing. For every $q\geq 4$, we prove $R_{q,3}>B_{q,3}+\frac{1}{250000}.$ In particular, the case $q=9$, combined with the Tetra code, strictly improves the K\"orner-Marton lower bound $R_3\geq \frac14\log(9/5)$ for trifferent codes. We also extend the method to $(p,2,3)$-list recovery. For every $q\geq 4$ and $0\leq p B_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)$. For every fixed $0\leq p<1/18$, the rate improvement is bounded below by a positive constant independent of $q\geq 4$. The same holds for every fixed $0\le p<1/12$ when $q$ is sufficiently large.

papers.title: Chatter Attack: Resource Consumption Attack for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: LLMs are powerful but incur substantial inference cost, which can be exploited by malicious users to induce overly long outputs, increasing latency and operational expense. Prior resource consumption attacks either coerce repetition or suppress the end-of-sequence token by lowering its logit value. However, with autoregressive, sampling-based generation, the search space grows exponentially with length and small deviations or unstable trajectories can derail optimization, limiting attack effectiveness and stability. To address this issue, we introduce Chatter Attack, a novel class of resource consumption attacks that optimize adversarial prompts to induce predefined short target phrases, thereby avoiding search-space explosion while still eliciting long responses. Specifically, Chatter Attack triggers self-doubt using short doubt-inducing phrases as the target, and sustains this state throughout generation via inference attention loss and global entropy loss. To extend to black-box settings, we further propose a novel Bayesian Prompt Optimization (BPO) method, which models the objective function globally by constructing a discrete token kernel, efficiently exploring the entire search space using prior information. Extensive experiments across multiple models and datasets show that our method outperforms baselines, with maximum response length increases to 31.5$\times$, and revealing practical resource-depletion risks for real-world LLM inference services.

papers.title: Primitives and Paths: Predicting What Post-Training Can Do from What the Base Model Already Has
papers.abstract: Does reinforcement learning teach language models new capabilities, or merely amplify ones acquired during pre-training? The literature offers evidence for both: pass@$k$ studies suggest RL reweights latent behaviours while some controlled composition studies demonstrate gains beyond simple amplification. We argue that this question has no answer independent of the capability state of the base model, and propose a two-dimensional state space for post-trainability. The first axis, \emph{effective full-solution support}, measures whether successful trajectories can be sampled under a feasible exploration budget. The second axis, \emph{atomic primitive coverage}, measures whether the constituent skills of a solution can be executed when the burden of composition is removed. Together, these dimensions motivate three regimes -- amplification, composition-limited, and acquisition-limited -- each predicting a distinct empirical signature and calling for a distinct intervention. We propose a prospective measurement protocol and investigate the framework using synthetic composition tasks across three small language models. We find that primitive mastery alone does not guarantee that RL can learn a composition. Checkpoints that execute every primitive reliably can fail to improve when complete solutions are never sampled during training, whereas modest composition supervision that establishes nonzero support enables substantial RL gains. The framework reframes mid-training as preparation for post-training: its role is to move models into states from which RL can operate effectively.

papers.title: Support enumerators of two-row grids and comb posets
papers.abstract: We enumerate lattice points of preorder polytopes by support size for two-row Ferrers posets and recursively defined comb posets. For two-row posets, the order-ideal inequalities give a reflected-walk model in the nonnegative quadrant. Its transfer operators have a rank-one commutator, from which we derive an identity with five independent parameters. A matching-parameter specialization factors into the enumerators of a Motzkin excursion and a Motzkin bridge and proves the conjectured product of type~A and type~B Narayana polynomials for a two-row grid with its maximum removed. The general identity also records the two row supports separately. For combs, maximum ideal excess leads to a scalar recursion and a cubic generating function with independent spine and tooth weights. This proves a compositional-inverse conjecture of Athanasiadis and Chapoton and gives explicit $\gamma$-coefficients by Lagrange inversion. We prove $\gamma$-positivity for all two-row Ferrers cell posets and for the combs. The truncated-grid enumerators have simple negative zeros.

papers.title: Auto-GlaKG: Automated Biomarker Reasoning for Explainable Glaucoma Detection
papers.abstract: Interpretable glaucoma detection requires a transparent connection between fundus images, clinically meaningful biomarkers, and diagnostic predictions. Knowledge graph (KG) reasoning provides this structure, but performance measured using annotated biomarkers does not establish performance when only images are available. We present Auto-GlaKG, an automated framework that combines image-based biomarker prediction with fixed clinical-prior rules. A ResNet50 network predicts the cup-to-disc ratio (CDR) and six morphological signs using biomarker supervision, and a KG reasoner aggregates their signed rule contributions into a glaucoma score. On 689 fundus images evaluated using stratified, group-aware five-fold cross-validation, Auto-GlaKG achieves a pooled area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.951 (95\% confidence interval: 0.931--0.969), with sensitivity of 0.970 and specificity of 0.779. The matched image classifier also achieves an AUC of 0.951, while the rule stage adds 0.2~ms per image. Replacing predicted CDR with its annotation increases fold-mean AUC from 0.953 to 0.995. The framework provides an explicit rule-level account of image-based predictions and identifies CDR estimation as a priority for validation using independently measured biomarkers.

papers.title: Learning calibrated probabilistic forecasts using Koopman mode decomposition and the continuous ranked probability score
papers.abstract: Well-calibrated forecasting for non-linear dynamical systems is essential in science and engineering applications such as fluid dynamics and weather prediction. We present a forecasting method combining probabilistic machine learning with the structured linear dynamics of Koopman mode decomposition. Within this framework, the observation, linear dynamics, and state reconstruction operators are constructed using standard machine learning architectures, producing predictive distributions via the pushforward of injected noise samples. The model is trained using a proper scoring rule, the continuous ranked probability score, to directly target calibrated, accurate forecasts. The approach is validated on two non-linear ordinary differential equation examples and two partial differential equation examples, vortex shedding and cavity flow, using both large and small, noisy datasets. Results demonstrate that known Koopman eigenfunctions and spectra can be identified and used for accurate forecasting. The model can also produce multi-modal predictive distributions, demonstrated for a trajectory initialised on the boundary between two basins of attraction. Uncertainty is captured by the sample ensemble spread, with spread--skill ratios close to one over the training horizon in several experiments, although for extended rollouts and noisy datasets, the ensemble may become under- or over-dispersed. In low-noise experiments, temporal rollout is generally accurate for at least twice the training horizon, and up to twenty times in some cases. Approximation quality is comparable to a deep ensemble approximation over the training horizon, but at a reduced computational cost and with better robustness in identifying Koopman eigenvalues.

papers.title: Engineering ferroelectric nanocapacitors through interfacial phonon bias
papers.abstract: As ferroelectric devices approach the nanometer scale, their behavior becomes increasingly sensitive to boundary conditions. In perovskite oxide nanocapacitors, epitaxial strain and electrostatic screening are well-established control parameters. Then, while expected to contribute to the epitaxial stabilization of ferroelectric ultrathin films, the lattice-dynamical state of the electrodes has not been isolated as an independent tuning knob. Here we call this poorly explored coupling interfacial phonon bias, whereby the electrodes' phonon energy landscape reshapes that of the adjacent ferroelectric across their shared interface. Using first-principles-accurate machine-learned interatomic potentials and molecular-dynamics simulations, we examine this mechanism in symmetric BiFeO${}_3$ nanocapacitors in contact with a metallic perovskite oxide. By independently controlling the orientatio and amplitude of the electrodes' octahedral-tilt landscape, while keeping conventional elastic and electric boundary conditions fixed, we show that the electrodes' phonon energy landscape can modify the stability of competing BiFeO${}_3$ phases. In particular, this allows us to shift the ferroelectric transition temperature and even induce antiferroelectric-like switching at ambient conditions. We thus showcase interfacial phonon bias as a complementary and powerful strategy to modify and optimize the properties of ultrathin epitaxial films.

papers.title: Chaos Growth in a Generic 2D Hamiltonian System
papers.abstract: We examine the geometric mechanism controlling the transition from local to global chaos in a generic 2D Hamiltonian system, the generalized H\'{e}non-Heiles system. Using Poincar\'e sections and invariant manifolds, we show that the chaotic fraction grows through abrupt transitions associated with the destruction of invariant barriers. We introduce an index that gives the time required for the first penetration of a local chaotic domain into the global chaos. This index increases sharply and tends to infinity as a critical energy is approached. The set of lobes generates heteroclinic connections, while multiple unstable periodic orbits exhibit a global manifold structure characterised by repeated loops and lobes. However, in special chaotic cases close to the integrable H\'{e}non-Heiles potential, where two asymptotic curves extend to infinity, the manifold topology differs qualitatively from the generic case, as the asymptotic curves no longer form closed structures surrounding the periodic orbits.

papers.title: Probing the Supersymmetric Grand Unified Theories with Anomaly Mediation at the Future Proton-Proton Colliders and Hyper-Kamiokande Experiment
papers.abstract: With the grand desert hypothesis, we investigate the Supersymmetric (SUSY) Grand Unified Theories (GUTs) with the minimal anomaly mediated supersymmetry breaking (AMSB) as a continuation of our program of studying SUSY GUTs at the future 100 TeV proton-proton Collider such as $\rm FCC_{hh}$ and SppC as well as proton-decay experiment such as Hyper-Kamiokande experiment. We show that for the GUT scale $M_{GUT} \ge 0.84 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, the upper mass bounds on the gluino and first two generation squarks are 8 TeV and 6 TeV, respectively. Therefore, the gluino and first two generation squarks can be probed at the $\rm FCC_{hh}$ and SppC. In addition, we discuss the mass spectra for the colored sparticles, sleptons, pseudo-scalar Higgs and electroweakinos. We also shed light on the possible search strategies of gluino and winos at the future 100 TeV colliders. Moreover, for $\rm M_{\rm GUT} \le 0.84 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, the proton lifetime for dimension-six proton decay via heavy gauge boson exchange is less than or around $5 \times 10^{34}$ years, and thus we can probe it at the Hyper-Kamiokande experiment. To be concrete, we present a couple of benchmark points representing the above two mentioned GUT conditions on $\rm M_{\rm GUT}$.

papers.title: Effect of Correlation on the Pressure-Induced Insulator to Metal Transition in Complex Spin-Orbit Coupled Double Perovskite La$_2$CoIr$_{1-x}$Ti$_x$O$_6$
papers.abstract: We study the effect of electron correlation ($U$) and hydrostatic pressure on the electronic properties of double perovskites La$_2$CoIr$_{1-x}$Ti$_x$O$_6$ for $x$ = 0, 0.5, and 1, using first-principles electronic structure calculations within density functional theory (DFT). At ambient pressure, we systematically vary the electron correlation, i.e., on-site Coulomb interaction to study its effect on band gap and structural parameters. Increasing the value of $U$ enhances the band gap of all three compositions while producing only a slight variation in structural parameters. The effect of hydrostatic pressure is also studied for the same compositions. The estimated band gap values at ambient pressure closes at approximately 39, 42, and 53 GPa for $x$ = 0 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 5 eV and $U_\mathrm{Ir}$ = 2 eV), 0.5 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 5 eV and $U_\mathrm{Ir}$ = 2 eV), and 1 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 4 eV), respectively, indicating pressure-induced insulator-to-metal transitions. These results show that electron correlation stabilises the insulating state, whereas hydrostatic pressure favours the metallic state by closing the band gap. These findings highlight the tunability of correlated oxides through electron correlations and pressure, offering insights for materials design.

papers.title: ALETHEIA: A Multi-Frequency Eddy Current Pulsed Thermography Dataset for Neural Operator Learning in Nondestructive Testing
papers.abstract: Learning neural solvers for spatiotemporal partial differential equations (PDEs) under real-world constraints remains a key challenge in scientific machine learning, especially for inverse tasks with sparse and noisy boundary observations. We present the Aletheia dataset, the first 3D benchmark for learning data-driven solvers in the context of nondestructive testing (NDT). The dataset simulates eddy-current-induced heating in conductive solids and models the resulting transient heat propagation governed by the heat equation. Aletheia contains over 4,700 high-resolution samples across 10 excitation frequencies (1-100,kHz), each providing volumetric heat source and temperature fields over time. It supports both forward prediction of temperature evolution and inverse reconstruction of internal heat sources or defects from surface infrared measurements. Real infrared thermography data from cracked rail specimens are included for calibration and comparison. We define four canonical tasks on both regular and irregular grids and benchmark them using various neural operators. Aletheia establishes a unified platform for evaluating neural PDE solvers under realistic NDT conditions, enabling progress in reliable, data-driven inverse modeling. The dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/sherlock-0327/ALETHEIA.

papers.title: The Outer Eshelby Problem in Amorphous Solids with Odd Dipole Screening
papers.abstract: The so-called "2-dimensional Eshelby problem" was defined by JD Eshelby, where a circle is cut out of an elastic sheet, deformed into an ellipse, and forced back into the material. This creates a quadrupolar response which turned out to be very relevant for describing plastic deformations in amorphous solids. Moreover, the resulting strain field has been used to describe how elasto-plastic models respond to external strains. It is thus important to examine carefully the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids, especially when anomalous elasticity is at play. Here we solve the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids with both even and odd dipole screening and a complete analytical result is obtained for the displacement and strain fields. The analytical results are crucial for understanding the anomalous responses in displacement fields measured directly from experiments and numerical simulations. The computation of strain fields clearly demonstrates the deviations from their classical counterparts for perfectly elastic solids. The decomposition of the displacement field shows the excitation of higher-order Fourier modes. The presence of higher excitations other than the imposed Eshelby geometry therefore suggests the possible nonlinear mode coupling that can influence and modify the anomalous responses.

papers.title: Rayleigh's conjecture in dimensions four and five
papers.abstract: We prove Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate in dimensions four and five. In fact, we obtain a sharp comparison with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: on every open set of finite positive measure, the first plate eigenvalue is at least the square of the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiplied by the ratio attained on a ball. The proof uses a homogeneous transformation of a trial function and its gradient. Two divergence identities reduce the comparison to positivity of a quadratic form in the Hessian. We establish the required Bessel inequalities by rational estimates for entire profiles and their remainders. An exact defect identity accounts for regular nodal sets, so the argument allows trial functions of either sign and imposes no boundary regularity. The domains may be disconnected or unbounded. We characterize equality up to sets of zero Sobolev capacity. We also obtain quantitative stability with the optimal quadratic power of the Fraenkel asymmetry.

papers.title: Understanding When and Where Self-Supervised Speech Models Learn Phonemes and Prosodic Cues through Layer-Wise and Time-Resolved Probing
papers.abstract: Self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) encode a rich hierarchy of acoustic, prosodic, and phonetic information, yet when and where it emerges during pretraining remains unclear. We train frozen-encoder probes on every Transformer layer across pretraining checkpoints of two matched models: HuBERT-Base, whose stage 2 is a separately initialized model trained on new pseudo-label targets, and single-objective wav2vec 2.0-Base. Our five tasks span an acoustic-to-abstract gradient: absolute pitch (F0), speaker-relative pitch, lexical stress, phoneme boundaries, and 38-way phoneme identity. Acoustic-prosodic cues and phone boundaries are decodable from the earliest checkpoints and barely shift across layers, whereas phoneme identity is constructed during pretraining, re-localizing to upper-middle layers under HuBERT's stage-2 targets at a matched update count. Acquisition order therefore tracks abstraction from the acoustic surface, not the segmental/suprasegmental distinction, extending to prosody an account established for phonetic, lexical and syntactic structure; the no-switch wav2vec 2.0 shows no comparable re-localization.

papers.title: FESOM2.8 in single precision: climate fidelity over six decades and performance on CPUs and GPUs
papers.abstract: Halving the floating-point precision of an ocean model can make it substantially faster, but whether the rounding errors stay negligible over climate time scales has rarely been tested. We implement single precision in the global ocean-sea-ice model FESOM2 and compare 60-year hindcasts with double-precision controls. A first implementation lost salt steadily, accumulated a heat-content deficit of 129 ZJ, and shifted major ocean fronts. Controlled experiments trace the drift to the tracer update: small increments added to a large salinity value are rounded away, and the increments themselves are biased. Accumulating tracer tendencies and layer thicknesses in 64 bits, and carrying the rounding error of each tracer update into the next, removes the drift for at most 8% additional runtime. Single- and double-precision simulations then differ in heat content and mean state about as much as two double-precision runs with slightly perturbed initial conditions, sea ice differs by at most 0.2%, and he salinity difference is four orders of magnitude smaller than before. In the coupled model AWI-ESM3, single precision adds no detectable heat source or sink over 60 years. Single precision speeds up the 60-year hindcasts by a factor of 1.35, and the model by up to 1.66 on meshes of up to 5 km resolution; on GPUs, a C++/Kokkos version runs up to 1.27 times faster and needs 43% less memory. Whether reduced precision is safe for climate integrations is decided by long-term budgets, not by short tests.

papers.title: On the monotonicity of amenable category for geometric 4-manifolds and their connected sums
papers.abstract: We show that the amenable category is monotone with respect to the domination relation for geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums.

papers.title: Direct Light-Cone Reconstruction of the $B$-Meson Shape Function in HQET
papers.abstract: The $B$-meson shape function encodes the nonperturbative residual-momentum dynamics of the heavy quark within heavy quark effective theory (HQET). From a Wilsonian perspective, HQET provides a natural framework for lattice calculations when the heavy quark mass is comparable to or exceeds the inverse lattice spacing. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a $B$-meson quasi-shape function directly in HQET and calculate its one-loop matching to the light-cone shape function, avoiding an intermediate matching step involving a full-QCD light-cone distribution. We determine the one-loop renormalization kernels and matching coefficients in both the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ and regularization-independent momentum-subtraction (RI/MOM) schemes for the quasi-shape function, while keeping the light-cone shape function in the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme. The matching coefficients are obtained at leading power in the large-$v^z$ expansion and are independent of the infrared regulator. Our results provide the perturbative ingredients for a direct lattice HQET determination of the $B$-meson shape function.

papers.title: Hardware-Efficient Continuous-Variable Quantum Computation: Finite-$N$ Non-Gaussian Gates in a Floquet-Engineered Cavity-BEC
papers.abstract: Continuous-variable (CV) quantum computation in bosonic modes offers a hardware-efficient route toward fault tolerance, yet synthesizing deterministic, macroscopic non-Gaussian gates with Wigner negativity remains challenging. Here, we establish two physical breakthroughs and two tensor-network innovations using a single-cavity 87Rb Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) as a macroscopic bosonic logical mode. Physically, building on our orthogonal optical dual-driving architecture, we propose deterministic, unitary Floquet-engineered Two-Axis Twisting (TAT) non-Gaussian gates without post-selection, and introduce a paradigm shift from quantum metrology to CV quantum computation: via a normal-ordered Holstein-Primakoff expansion and non-perturbative spin simulations, we show that the over-squeezed regime ($t>t_{opt}$, where Wineland squeezing $\xi_R^2$ degrades) harnesses finite-$N$ Bloch-sphere curvature - manifesting at $O(1/S)$ as cubic shearing and quartic Kerr $(a^\dagger a)^2$ interactions - to deterministically generate Wigner negativity. Methodologically, we formulate an exact automaton Matrix Product Operator in the compact SU(2) spin basis with an $N$-independent Liouvillian bond dimension ($D_L=6$), bypassing Fock cutoff errors ($N_{max}$) and $O(N^3)$ permutational-invariant scaling. Finally, we decouple $4^N$-dimensional Lindblad evolution from collective observation via an Exact Bilateral Dynamic Programming Dicke Projector with log-gamma normalization, extracting the $(N+1)\times(N+1)$ symmetric projection $\tilde{\rho}_{n_L,n_R}$ without moment truncation while tracking symmetry retention $p_{sym}(t)$. Our proof-of-principle $N=50$ benchmark resolves deep Wigner negativity ($W_{min} \approx -0.214$ at $t=2.00\mu$s, after $\xi_R^2 \approx 0.124$ at $t_{opt} \approx 0.64\mu$s), establishing a scalable architecture for $N \sim 10^3-10^5$ macroscopic BEC processors.

papers.title: Harmonic and Monogenic Representations of White Noise and its weighted harmonic Bergman estimates
papers.abstract: Continuing Feichtinger's generalized stochastic process theory, we analyze harmonic and monogenic representations of white noise in Euclidean spaces. We define its convolution with square-integrable functions. Using the weighted Sobolev regularity of the white noise, we establish a high-dimensional Sokhotski-Plemelj formula for the white noise density. Furthermore, we embed these representations into new weighted Bergman spaces, proving that the weighted Bergman norms of the harmonic representations are bounded by the white noise's weighted Sobolev norms.

papers.title: Saidzoda-Tajik-EmbeddingGemma-300M: Knowing Every Letter Is Not Reading Tajik
papers.abstract: EmbeddingGemma-300M is a small open embedder whose tokenizer represents every Tajik letter, and as released it is weak at Tajik retrieval: on our Tajik law test the right passage is in its top ten results for 49.3% of questions, on tax documents for 45.9%, and on the human-written Belebele Tajik set for 69.8%, against 98.6% on the Russian version of the same set. We present Saidzoda-Tajik-EmbeddingGemma-300M, the same model fully fine-tuned for one epoch on 235,140 question and passage pairs written by our own Tajik language model for laws, tax documents, Wikipedia and web text, with the same mined hard negatives, English and Russian replay, loss, global batch, learning rate and epoch as our earlier Saidzoda-Tajik-E5-Large (arXiv:2611.00592) and BGE-M3 models. After training, law reaches 92.4% and tax 91.7%; on Belebele, the one test written by people, recall@10 rises from 69.8% to 92.6% and the first result is right for 76.6% of questions instead of 51.7%. A checkpoint at step 100 of 466 already holds 88% of the law gain at recall@10. At recall@10 the result is no more than 2.8 points below the two 560M models trained on the same pairs on law, tax and Wikipedia, within the intervals, with 768-dimensional vectors and about half their parameters; at recall@1, for which we have no intervals, it stays 7.0 points behind the E5 model on Belebele. The cost is a drop of 3.0 and 2.8 points in Russian and English recall@1, larger than for the two earlier models. We also report that, according to our run notes, a bfloat16 test run produced a non-finite loss at step 3 which the training framework logged as zero, so training was done in fp32. Our generated test questions come from the same model as the training questions, so we treat those scores as an upper limit until questions written by Tajik speakers exist.

papers.title: DeepSoMo: Deformable Object Motion Estimation under Proprioceptive Partial Observability via Predictive Latent Dynamics
papers.abstract: Estimating the motion of deformable bodies in soft robotics from proprioceptive sensing is challenging due to partial observability, as internal observations provide only indirect access to global motion, contact, and shape evolution. In such settings, instantaneous observations are insufficient, and accurate estimation requires temporally consistent latent representations. This paper studies deformable motion estimation under proprioceptive partial observability from a latent dynamics perspective. We argue that a key requirement for long-horizon estimation is latent temporal consistency, where latent states remain predictive of future observations. To this end, we present DeepSoMo, a learning-based framework that enforces predictive structure in latent dynamics through a self-supervised latent prediction constraint. We evaluate the approach in a canonical deformable dynamics setting using high-fidelity finite-element simulation as a controlled source of ground truth. Results demonstrate consistent improvements in trajectory estimation, orientation recovery, shape reconstruction, and contact inference over architecture-matched recurrent baselines.

papers.title: An $SU(5)$ GUT with non-holomorphic modular $S'_4$ symmetry: fermion masses, mixing and leptogenesis
papers.abstract: A non-supersymmetric $SU(5)$ grand unified model is constructed based on the non-holomorphic modular $S'_4$ flavor symmetry, supplemented by a global Peccei--Quinn $U(1)_{PQ}$ symmetry that constrains the Yukawa couplings. Constructed from polyharmonic Maa{\ss} forms, these couplings allow the model to reproduce the observed charged-fermion masses and mixing as well as the neutrino oscillation parameters for both normal ordering (NO) and inverted ordering (IO), with all Pull values satisfying $|\mathcal{P}| < 0.8$. The model further yields specific predictions for yet-unmeasured parameters, including the absolute neutrino masses, the Dirac CP phase, the Majorana phases, and the effective Majorana mass $m_{\beta\beta}$. We then study thermal leptogenesis by solving the density matrix equations. For a given benchmark point, the final baryon asymmetry depends solely on the single free parameter $b$ that sets the right-handed neutrino mass scale, and an appropriate choice of this parameter reproduces the observed value $\eta_B \simeq 6.12 \times 10^{-10}$. Finally, the correlation between this scale parameter and specific low-energy observables provides a potential bridge between the fermion flavor structure and early-Universe cosmology.

papers.title: Stretched near-groups
papers.abstract: We study stretched near-group fusion categories over $\mathbb{C}$ of type $G+k|G|$ for abelian groups $G$ and positive integers $k$, describing the structure of the double including fusion rules, modular data, and Frobenius--Schur indicators under a variety of assumptions. For cyclic $G$, when enough invertible objects exist in the double, we describe all associated de-equivariantizations which connect the existence of stretched near-group fusion categories to the existence of other stretched quadratic categories. All of our results apply to the case $k=1$. In particular, the known existence of $C_{m^2}+m^2$ near-group categories for all positive integers $m$ implies the existence of Haagerup--Izumi fusion categories for all cyclic groups. As a further application, we provide a general conductor bound severely restricting the existence of stretched near-group categories, and for infinitely many abelian groups $G$ of square order, among them $C_4\times C_2^{2j}$ with $j\geq2$, we show that a near-group fusion category $G+k|G|$ exists if and only if $k=0$.

papers.title: A Layer-wise Study of How Style Rewriting Breaks the Calibration of Zero-Shot LLM Fake-News Detectors
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly asked to judge whether a news article is true, and their stated confidence is often taken at face value. We test what happens to that confidence when an article's writing style, but not its facts, is manipulated, as in recent \emph{style attacks} on fake-news detectors. Tracing how the prediction and its confidence form layer by layer inside the network, we study three model families (LLaMA-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B) on three fake-news benchmarks, and find the same three patterns in every model--dataset pairing. First, on the original articles the models are competent and largely honest judges: they settle on an answer, briefly become overconfident, and then correct their confidence in the final layers. Second, style-rewritten articles break this self-correction: the models become far less accurate, under the strongest attack, worse than random guessing, yet remain just as confident, so they are \emph{confidently wrong} precisely when a warning is most needed. Third, nearly all of the damage comes from rewriting into sensational or emotionally charged styles, while sober, neutral rewrites leave the models' honesty largely intact. The practical implication is that an LLM's confidence about veracity cannot be trusted as a safety signal when an article's style may have been manipulated.

papers.title: FRESCO: A Novel Consistency Control for Asynchronous Pipeline Parallel Training
papers.abstract: Asynchronous pipeline parallelism can accelerate distributed model training, but suffers from instability caused by inconsistent gradient computations. We identify a fundamental source of this inconsistency: error signals are coupled to forward-time features, not just parameter states. This means that parameters may evolve as long as they preserve forward-equivalence. Leveraging this insight, we introduce FRESCO, which frames asynchronous updates as a constrained optimization problem: it finds the minimal update modification that acts trivially on the activation subspace. We demonstrate that FRESCO consistently outperforms representative asynchronous baselines in LLM pre-training, with the gains most pronounced under deep pipelines and high inconsistency levels: at pipeline depth 32, it reaches the same loss as the strongest baseline with 43% fewer iterations and 30% less wall-clock time, while requiring 8~921$\times$ less memory overhead. Moving beyond the current limitations, FRESCO establishes a new foundation for high-utilization pipeline parallel training, providing a scalable path for large-model development on diverse, resource-constrained systems.

papers.title: Precision Fragmentation Functions from Modern COMPASS SIDIS Data
papers.abstract: We present a comparative account of three global determinations of collinear fragmentation functions (FFs) for charged pions, charged kaons, and unidentified charged hadrons. The HAPS-PiFF1.0, HAPS-KaFF1.0, and HAPS-hFF1.0 analyses combine single-inclusive $e^+e^-$ annihilation with charge-separated semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS), including the 2025 COMPASS proton-target measurements and the revised 2026 isoscalar-target results. Flexible neural-network parametrizations, Monte Carlo replicas, and NLO/NNLO perturbative setups are employed. The proton and isoscalar samples sharpen the flavor sensitivity of SIDIS, while gluon fragmentation remains comparatively weakly constrained. We discuss the effects of perturbative accuracy, the principal limitations, and prospects for future measurements.
authors: Maryam Soleymaninia (On behalf of HAPS Collaboration)

papers.title: Algorithms for Soft Tree Containment on Tree-Child Networks
papers.abstract: Phylogenetic networks generalize evolutionary trees by allowing lineages to merge. The Tree Containment problem asks whether a network $N$ displays a tree $T$ on the same taxa. When the polytomies of $T$ reflect uncertainty rather than simultaneous divergence, the relevant notion is soft display, in which $N$ may refine the polytomies of $T$. We take it in its asymmetric reading. Soft Tree Containment is NP-hard on reticulation-visible networks even at reticulation indegree three, and it was open for a non-binary tree and a tree-child network with multifurcating tree nodes or reticulations of indegree above two. We solve this case. A cluster characterization reduces soft display to realizing all clusters of $T$ by one switching, and in a tree-child network the vertices that can realize a cluster lie on a single chain. The per-cluster requirements then form a constraint network of width one, which arc consistency decides without search, and a $2$-SAT instance when $N$ is binary. This yields, to our knowledge, the first polynomial-time algorithm for soft Tree Containment on single-labelled tree-child networks of arbitrary reticulation indegree, and a linear-time algorithm when $T$ is binary. The same method decides the symmetric variant of the problem, in which the polytomies of $N$ may be resolved as well.

papers.title: Continuity of solutions to nonlocal nonlinear diffusion equations
papers.abstract: We establish an explicit modulus of continuity for locally bounded weak solutions to nonlocal porous medium type equations with measurable kernels. The nonlocal tail is only assumed to be integrable in time. The result lays a solid foundation for the intrinsic Harnack estimates of these equations.

papers.title: LoMASA: A Local Multi-Agent Sales Assistant with Confidence-Gated Delegation for B2B Quoting
papers.abstract: Frontline sales staff spend much of their day re-coordinating quotes after customers change quantities, ask for discounts or new payment terms, or costs move. We present LoMASA (Local Multi-Agent Sales Assistant), a training-free multi-agent system that runs entirely on one desktop computer. A 35B mixture-of-experts model (System-1) makes each decision in a single forward pass and reads its confidence from the probabilities of the answer options. A 27B dense model (System-2) writes customer replies and escalation briefs and is consulted when System-1 is unsure. Code computes every price, margin and option, and hard pricing rules cannot be overridden. On a test split of 500 simulated episodes with 1512 decisions built from public supply-chain data, the salesperson has to decide only 19.5% of decisions: 38.0% are settled automatically, with a median latency of 2.67 seconds, and 42.5% are escalated to a manager by the hard rules. On the automatically settled decisions LoMASA is as accurate as a rule baseline (0.894 vs.\ 0.894) and makes fewer commitments whose margin later falls below the floor (2.61% vs 4.53%); the price is additional escalations to the manager. Option probabilities are well calibrated without any training, unlike confidence stated in words by the same model. We also report where the design does not help: the 27B model rarely changes a decision.

papers.title: Joint Poisson Reconstruction for Prompt-Gamma-Enabled 68Ga/18F Dual-Isotope Quantitative PET Imaging
papers.abstract: Objective:To enable simultaneous quantitative 68Ga/18F PET imaging despite low prompt-gamma triple-coincidence counts and random-triple contamination. Methods: We developed an expectation-maximization reconstruction method (PNR-EM) that jointly estimates pure-emitter, non-pure-emitter, and random-triple components using a Poisson model of prompt double, prompt triple, and delayed triple measurements. A consistent-delay strategy estimates random triples while preserving true-pair temporal correlations. Prompt doubles additionally constrain the non-pure component, and total variation regularization suppresses reconstruction noise. The method was evaluated with quantitative and Derenzo phantoms, a nine-well separation phantom, and tumor-bearing mice. Results: Phantom quantitation showed strong linearity (r2>0.99) and a maximum relative deviation below 9.9% relative to single-isotope references. The separated images largely preserved rod resolvability relative to their corresponding single-isotope references. The best PSNR, SSIM, and RMSE were 33.72 dB, 0.975, and 0.0206 for 18F, and 34.86 dB, 0.955, and 0.0181 for 68Ga in the 9-well phantom. The 68Ga RMSE was 41.4% lower than that of the best image-domain separation baseline. Tumor-bearing mouse imaging demonstrated in vivo separation of 68Ga-DOTA-NOC and 18F-FDG distributions. Conclusion: Joint estimation improved dual-isotope separation under the evaluated low-count conditions. Significance: To our knowledge, this study provides the first experimental demonstration of simultaneous 68Ga/18F PET separation using prompt-gamma coincidences, supporting simultaneous imaging of complementary metabolic and receptor-targeted tracer distributions.

papers.title: TLRS-DPO: Token-Level Risk Scoring for Better Direct Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a simple and widely used alternative to RLHF for aligning large language models (LLMs), but its sequence-level objective cannot precisely locate or suppress the local patterns that make an otherwise acceptable response unsafe or undesirable. We propose TLRS-DPO (Token-Level Risk Scoring for Better Direct Preference Optimization), which augments DPO with fine-grained token-level control while remaining fully offline and reference-based. TLRS-DPO introduces a token-level robust compensation term that converts the policy-reference log-ratio on rejected responses into localized risk scores, a curriculum-style schedule that gradually increases the strength of this compensation during training, and a risk-adaptive screening mechanism that selectively penalizes only high-risk tokens instead of entire sequences. This design bridges sequence-level preference fitting and token-level behavior control, and can be implemented as a drop-in modification to standard DPO trainers. Empirically, TLRS-DPO improves alignment quality and safety-relevant behavior with minimal impact on helpfulness compared to strong DPO baselines.

papers.title: Nonlinear Interference Estimation in Coherent Optical Systems: Principles and Applications
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of nonlinear interference (NLI) is important for monitoring and optimizing coherent optical networks. This invited paper reviews the main techniques proposed for receiver-side NLI estimation, with particular focus on longitudinal power monitoring (LPM). We discuss the principles, advantages and limitations of LPM-based NLI estimation, including recent experimental demonstrations. We then experimentally investigate the impact of the spatial step size and the number of averaged constellation blocks on estimation accuracy. The results show that accurate NLI estimation does not necessarily require a highly accurate power profile, with limited improvements obtained by increasing the number of averaged blocks. Finally, we discuss the main practical limitations and applications of NLI estimation, with particular attention to end-to-end and span-wise optical power optimization.

papers.title: An elementary observation on the Robin problem for NLS
papers.abstract: We present an infinite set of explicit solutions of the integrable focusing NLS equation on the half-line that are rapidly decaying and satisfy a homogeneous Robin condition but have very different behaviors on the wall $x=0$. We then argue that a similar phenomenon exists for a small non-homogeneous perturbation of the Robin problem. This renders a potential application of the unified transform method to non-linearizable Robin problems impossible.

papers.title: GFM Control Automatic Compliance Toolbox
papers.abstract: The increasing penetration of converter-interfaced generation reduces system inertia, short-circuit strength, and voltage support. European grid codes, including the ENTSO-E Network Code on Requirements for Generators and the ACER Demand Connection Code, now define disturbance-based validation procedures for grid-forming (GFM) generation and converter-based demand. Commercial RMS tools, however, lack an integrated workflow aligned with these recent requirements. This paper presents an automated Python-PowerFactory compliance toolbox and an RMS test bench for a co-located system comprising a 1 MW GFM photovoltaic (PV) plant, a 0.3 MW GFM battery energy storage system (BESS), and a 1 MW converter-interfaced dynamic load at a 20 kV point of common coupling fed from a 110 kV grid. Extended virtual synchronous machine models and a DCC-oriented load model are tested in batch, with results automatically extracted and plotted for assessment. Results show compliant RMS performance for the slower, electromechanical tests, while the paper identifies which tests require complementary electromagnetic transient (EMT) verification.

papers.title: Welfare in Envy-free Contracts: When Agents Have Sparse Interests
papers.abstract: We study welfare maximization under envy-free contracts, where a principal assigns tasks and offers success-contingent payments to heterogeneous agents with hidden effort. For unit-demand agents, we establish a sharp complexity boundary: the problem is polynomial-time solvable when each agent is interested in at most two tasks, but NP-hard with at most three interests. Our algorithm analyzes tree-structured dependencies among forced assignments and reduces optimization to maximum-weight independent set in a perfect graph. When agents may receive multiple tasks, no polynomial-time constant-factor approximation exists unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. Finally, with homogeneous success probabilities and rewards, we establish a welfare- and revenue-preserving equivalence between unit-demand contract design and envy-free pricing. This yields polynomial-time welfare maximization without restricting interests, while revenue maximization remains NP-hard.

papers.title: Regulating pedestal pressure profile by microtearing modes in the EAST tokamak
papers.abstract: The pedestal pressure profile plays a critical role in determining the overall confinement of tokamak fusion plasmas. This letter reports the first evidence on regulating pedestal pressure profile by microtearing modes (MTMs) via limiting the pedestal gradient, which was thought to be limited by kinetic ballooning modes over the last decades. This is observed in an ITER-baseline-like target plasma in the EAST tokamak. MTMs arrest the recovery of pedestal electron temperature (and hence pressure) by clamping its gradient at a critical value while leaving the density profile essentially unaffected. Global fluid and local gyrokinetic simulations confirm the excitation of MTMs when the pedestal electron temperature gradient exceeds a threshold value in this experiment. This finding reveals MTMs as an alternative electromagnetic micro-instability that imposes an additional constraint in determining the pedestal structure in tokamaks.

papers.title: MCSA: Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation in SO(3) Equivariant GNNs for Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs) based on Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs) have achieved remarkable progress in atomistic modeling. However, accurately representing atomic interactions across different spatial scales remains challenging. In this work, we investigate the radial spectral properties of SO(3)-equivariant message passing and establish that the cutoff radius controls the characteristic spatial-frequency scale of radial interactions. Based on this analysis, we propose Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation (MCSA), a plug-and-play module that aggregates radial kernels with different cutoff radii to enrich multi-scale geometric representations. To achieve efficient implementation, we exploit the compact support of radial kernels to fuse cutoff-dependent radial weights before angular tensor-product operations, avoiding redundant angular computations while preserving rotational equivariance. Extensive experiments across representative EGNN backbones demonstrate consistent improvements in energy, force, and stress prediction, as well as enhanced accuracy in higher-order properties, including phonon dispersion and lattice thermal conductivity. Further evaluations on layered materials with distinct interaction scales demonstrate the effectiveness of physically motivated cutoff selection. Code is available at: https://github.com/JF-Tan/MCSA.

papers.title: Electron cooling mediated by transverse optical phonons in doped SrTiO$_3$
papers.abstract: Soft transverse optical (TO) phonons in doped SrTiO$_3$ couple to electrons through the polarization field, quadratically in the paraelectric phase and, additionally, linearly in the polar phase due to the onset of spontaneous polarization. We investigate heat flow between a three-dimensional electron gas and soft TO phonons. For two-TO-phonon scattering, the heat flow of hot electrons crosses over from $T^5$ to $T^3$ at the Bloch-Gruneisen temperature. In the polar phase, an additional one-TO-phonon channel emerges, yielding a softer temperature dependence of the heat flow, $T^3$ at low and $T$ at high temperatures, with the spectral weight set by the spontaneous polarization. This channel may dominate at low temperatures and leads to a nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the heat flow in the vicinity of the polar transition.

papers.title: Do Feature Interactions Break Explainability? Provable Explanations for Any-Order Neural Additive Models
papers.abstract: Post-hoc explanation methods for neural networks are often heuristic and lack provable guarantees. A common alternative to such methods that was studied in recent years is to compute a cardinally-minimal subset of input features that is provably sufficient to determine the model's prediction. For general neural networks, however, finding such explanations is computationally intractable. In contrast, recent work showed that this problem becomes more tractable for a particular family of neural networks, namely neural additive models (NAMs), though standard NAMs are highly restrictive because they exclude feature interactions altogether. In this work, we study the computation of provably minimal and sufficient explanations for neural networks with restricted feature interactions, bridging the gap between fully general neural networks and purely additive models. We first prove that even with constant-order interactions, the problem is $\Sigma_2^P$-hard, implying that worst-case exponential complexity is unavoidable. We then identify two provably tractable settings: one based on sparsity in the interaction structure and another based on a stronger interaction-aware notion of sufficiency. Under either of these settings, we develop algorithms that compute provable explanations for neural networks with any-order interactions while retaining much of the computational efficiency of additive models. Empirically, we show that these explanations are significantly smaller and faster to obtain than those produced by standard algorithms, while being derived from models that achieve much higher accuracy than standard NAMs. Overall, our results help expand the class of neural networks that admit efficient provable explanations, while clarifying the fundamental role of feature interactions in shaping their complexity.

papers.title: SGA-Sparse: Training Native SwiGLU Gates for Activation-Sparse and Low-Bit LLMs
papers.abstract: Activation sparsity can reduce FFN weight traffic during single-user LLM decoding, but active channels must be identified early enough to avoid fetching unused weights. In pretrained SwiGLU models, training-free routing with the native gate performs substantially worse than routing with the up activation at high sparsity. We show that this ordering reverses after sparsity-aware training. Based on this insight, we introduce SGA-Sparse, which converts pretrained SwiGLU LLMs into fixed-budget activation-sparse models by training the existing gate projection directly as a top-k router. SGA-Sparse updates all model parameters end-to-end while preserving the original SwiGLU activation and introducing no auxiliary router parameters. After approximately 30B training tokens, LLaMA models from 1B to 8B achieve uniform per-token 75-85% FFN channel sparsity while remaining within 0.2-2.7 pp of their original dense checkpoints in average zero-shot accuracy. Because post-training quantization degrades sparsity-trained checkpoints, we further study two complementary quantization-aware training (QAT) recipes: continued-QAT largely recovers performance at 4-bit weight quantization, while joint-QAT performs better for the more aggressive sub-4-bit target. To compare activation sparsity with dense low-bit quantization, we translate the sparsity-induced reduction in weight traffic into an equivalent bit-width. Under this unified weight-traffic metric, our 2.5- and 1.5-bit-equivalent models establish a new accuracy-traffic Pareto frontier: the 2.5-bit-equivalent models match dense 3-bit QAT accuracy, while the 1.5-bit-equivalent models approach dense 2-bit models and outperform dense ternary models by 1.3 pp on average. These results establish native-gate training as a practical approach for combining high FFN sparsity with low-bit weights.

papers.title: Support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains
papers.abstract: We study the spatial support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains. Under a local nondegeneracy condition, additive noise gives full distributional support at every fixed positive time. For the Dirichlet problem with nonlocal multiplicative noise, we prove that the solution is either identically zero or has full support; excluding the zero state requires a separate non-hitting assumption. For a Neumann model, nonzero initial mass excludes the zero state and yields full support. The proofs combine Galerkin approximation with terminal Malliavin estimates. Numerical results illustrate the propagation mechanisms.

papers.title: Grid-forming Control of Offshore Wind through a Diode-Rectifier HVDC System: a 2 GW Case Study
papers.abstract: Diode-rectifier-unit (DRU)-based high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission considerably reduces the volume and weight of the offshore converter platform for remote wind farms and, hence, its cost, but shifts the task of forming and regulating the offshore AC network to the wind-turbine converters. This paper examines which grid-forming control strategy is the most suitable for DRU power transfer. The DRU commutation relationship shows that the delivered active power depends on the offshore voltage magnitude (but not on the converter voltage angle), so the angle-based active-power loop of virtual synchronous machine control is not closed through the rectifier.
