A $P-V/Q-{\omega}$ grid-forming architecture, which regulates active power via the voltage magnitude and derives frequency from the reactive power error, is therefore adopted. Electromagnetic transient simulations of a 1GWaggregated grid-forming turbine on a 66 kV collector network with a $\pm$525 kV bipolar DRU link show that the commanded power is delivered over 800 to 1000MW with the offshore voltage held near nominal. The paper also examines how grid-forming operation changes the allocation of control duties within the Type-4 turbine: once the grid-side converter forms the network, DC link regulation must move to the machine-side converter, which limits the achievable bandwidth of the DC-link control. Extending the system to 2 GW with two 500 MW grid-following units achieves full power transfer in simulation, but with the grid-forming converter loaded beyond its continuous rating and a steady-state offshore frequency deviation of approximately 1.8 Hz.

papers.title: EbbFlow: PINN-Inspired Progressive Curriculum for MeanFlow Training
papers.abstract: MeanFlow learns interval-average velocity for few-step generation, but its fixed temporal sampler mixes diagonal and interior supervision throughout training. We interpret temporal coordinates as collocation points: diagonal samples provide a stochastic boundary target, whereas finite intervals supply a differential-consistency target. The diagonal fraction controls how often the consistency component appears, while interval length enters its gradient through an explicit factor. Motivated by this distinction, EbbFlow uses Temporal Supervision Allocation (TSA) to schedule the diagonal fraction and interval geometry. It starts with diagonal supervision, then admits interior samples and expands their maximum interval; a left-anchored interval law preserves coverage across time. The per-sample loss, target, backbone, and inference procedure remain unchanged. In matched class-conditional ImageNet $256\times 256$ runs without classifier-free guidance (DiT-B/2, one training seed per method, 400k updates), EbbFlow achieves 50k-sample FID of 39.65 at one network evaluation and 36.02 at two-evaluation ODE sampling, versus 44.82 and 39.86 for MeanFlow. Gradient probes show a mid-training difference in component geometry. Ablations support allocation scheduling and left-anchored intervals, although a fixed full-horizon variant performs better at one evaluation. These results suggest that temporal sampling is a useful training control whose benefits depend on the inference protocol.

papers.title: A Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs and a $3$-Design Obstruction for Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the doubly extended Reed--Solomon code with parameters $[q+1,k,q-k+2]_q$, where $q\ge3$ is a prime power and $2\le k\le q$. We prove a conjecture of Wu and Zhou by showing that the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_k$ do not form a $q$-ary $3$-design when $2\le k\le q-1$. Using shortening, we extend this obstruction to every nonempty weight class with $3\le w<q+1$. We also establish that each individual nonempty positive-weight class of $\mathcal{C}_k$ forms a $q$-ary $2$-design if and only if $\gcd(k-1,q-1)=1$. Consequently, every nonempty positive-weight class below full support has exact $q$-ary design strength $2$ when this coprimality condition holds, and $1$ otherwise.The three-design obstruction follows by applying a classical subset-product character identity to a marginal covering count for three prescribed nonzero symbols. The comparison between weights rests on a covering-count formulation of the classical MDS coset-weight relations. For every linear $[n,k,d]_q$ MDS code with $2\le k\le n-1$, this formulation shows that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at any one nonempty positive weight is equivalent to the same property at every nonempty positive weight.More generally, for $2\le t\le\min\{k,d\}$, we prove that the $q$-ary $t$-design property at any $t-1$ distinct nonempty positive weights forces it at all nonempty positive weights.

papers.title: Edge Computing for Computer Vision in IoT: Feasibility and Directions
papers.abstract: The convergence of decentralized architectures integrating Machine Learning, Computer Vision and Low Power Wide Area Networks is increasingly becoming an integral part of our daily existence. Internet of Things serves as a real-time data conduit enhancing decision making via embedded technology and continuous data exchange. This paper explores the feasibility of Edge Computing as a foundational pillar in this evolving landscape. We experiment under real world, dynamic conditions, evaluate the technological aspects, strategies, process flows and key observations under the broad Edge Computing domain. Research pathways include Multi-access Edge topologies in future 6G networks, model quantization, and satellite-enhanced communication platforms. Additionally, a discussion is added supporting the advanced AI functionalities, including zero-shot learning, multi modal perception, and decentralized generative AI, thereby broadening the scope of intelligent applications across various domains. The significance and research objective of this study are threefold: (1) evaluation of LoRaWAN and satellite IoT communication strategies, (2) analysis of CV workloads on edge hardware and (3) future research directions where Edge Computing can support low-latency, energy-efficient and socially impactful IoT applications. By explicitly addressing these aspects, we aim to establish a clear link between the technological feasibility, ultimately with a practical and socioeconomic relevance.

papers.title: scBIG++: Learning Across Genes and Cells to Predict Single-Cell Perturbation Responses
papers.abstract: Predicting single-cell transcriptional responses to genetic and chemical interventions supports gene-function discovery and regulatory analysis. Existing studies often focus only on highly variable genes, restricting the expression changes available for downstream analysis. Cells exposed to the same intervention can also show heterogeneous expression responses, with coordinated gene programs active to different degrees. We propose scBIG++, a full-gene perturbation prediction framework that models this heterogeneity by connecting expression-adaptive gene modules with population-conditioned generation. To preserve shared gene structure while accommodating cellular variation, Gene-Relation Clustering organizes genes into common windows, within which Dynamic SoftSub learns expression-dependent submodule memberships. This shared organization enables Set-GCAE to exchange information about corresponding gene groups across control cells, placing individual representations in their source-population context. The cell representations initialize a latent flow, while their pooled summary and the perturbation representation condition response generation. Generated states are decoded into expression profiles covering all assayed protein-coding genes retained after preprocessing, supporting comprehensive analysis of perturbation-induced expression changes. Experiments across six genetic and chemical settings spanning 6,539--19,451 genes demonstrate competitive perturbation-effect recovery and full-gene expression reconstruction under unseen targets and combinations, cross-cell-line transfer, and held-out compounds. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/ttruan2426-dot/scBIG.

papers.title: Replay Fidelity in LLM Agent Evaluation: Randomness, Hidden State, and Test Oracles in AppWorld
papers.abstract: Reproducibility in large language model (LLM) agent evaluation depends on replay fidelity: which parts of an execution trace are reconstructed, controlled, and compared. This matters for agent debugging, failure analysis, and counterfactual evaluation of stateful tool use. We audit all 71 unsuccessful executions in a fixed historical AppWorld corpus using 284 isolated fixed-code replay attempts. Reconstructed declared settings admit 42 cases under printed-output, pre-oracle database-delta, and native-verdict/test-count checks; resetting the random-number generator before each interaction admits 68. The 26-case gap contracts to four under database/oracle checks, with one endpoint unknown. Mechanism studies identify four materialized-state discrepancies despite matching outputs and verdicts. In one admitted endpoint pair, an identical API call yields matching responses but different row effects; common future Python RNG removes that deterministic difference in two paired repetitions. A separate JWT credential-equality program and alignment controls expose authentication/write differences, with missing repetitions retained. For all 10 affected post-oracle export cases, native export from retained output trackers restores the reference comparison without changing original cached contents. A purposeful 12-case BFCL pilot shows no discrepancy under its tested public-state, return, and verdict checks. We preserve resource censoring and infrastructure deviations. The contribution is a bounded empirical characterization of replay eligibility, hidden state, and test-oracle integration, without estimating debugger accuracy, repair gains, or method-ranking distortion.

papers.title: Spot Markets for AI Inference: Dynamic Capacity Allocation and Pricing on a Shared Accelerator Fleet
papers.abstract: Inference providers size their accelerator fleets for the interactive peak and sell spare capacity through fixed discounts, such as batch tiers at half price. However, inference differs from conventional cloud capacity in four respects: capacity depends on the latency tier through batching, moving weights between models is slow and costly, spot demand can wait until its deadline, and power can bind. In this paper, we develop a framework for dynamic capacity allocation and pricing of AI inference on a shared accelerator fleet. We consider a provider that serves several models under a power cap and sells each model in an interactive tier with a speed promise and in a spot tier for preemptible work with a deadline. In each period, the provider chooses how many replicas of each model to keep loaded and what spot price to quote. We show that one interactive token displaces a fixed number $\rho_m>1$ of spot tokens, and that the optimal spot price lies midway between the interactive price and the effective cost of capacity in the deadline window, which is close to the prevailing half price only when the fleet is slack. We further show that a spot tier raises the optimal reliability of the interactive tier, and that placement should follow persistent demand shifts while prices absorb transients. Building on these results, we design a model predictive controller based on a linear program with explicit approximation bounds, which solves each period in milliseconds. Numerical experiments on a simulated week with a measured daily demand profile, a flash crowd, and a grid curtailment show that the controller raises profit by 7.4% over fixed half-price practice, captures 93% of the gain available with perfect forecasts, keeps the interactive promise through both events, and leaves spot buyers better off.

papers.title: Disentangling Where and When:Factored Spatio-Temporal Explanations for Video Action Recognition
papers.abstract: Post-hoc explanation methods for video action recognition typically conflate spatial appearance and temporal dynamics into a single saliency or importance map. We propose a perturbation-based framework that disentangles these contributions into a spatial appearance mask ($M_a$) and a temporal motion mask ($M_m$). The two masks are jointly optimized against a frozen action recognition model through factored perturbation architecture, with nearest frame replacement to identify important temporal dynamics. A separation penalty discourages the appearance mask from spending budget on frames that the motion mask has already discarded. A ReLU-based area constraint penalizes explanations larger than an assigned budget. To evaluate these explanations, we introduce a separation protocol that sweeps spatial pixels and temporal frames independently, backed by proofs characterizing the proposed method. Across EPIC-Kitchens-55, EGTEA Gaze+, and Something-Something V2, our method attains the lowest deletion AUC against leading baselines while producing masks roughly five times sparser.

papers.title: NumericalDiff: Numerical Program Differencing via Value-Based Trace Alignment and Intervention
papers.abstract: Numerical programs implementing the same computational task can exhibit different numerical behavior because of their execution stacks, program representations, or program logic. Source text and final outputs alone provide limited diagnostic information: numerical differences can propagate through corresponding computations, while distinct executions can produce equal outputs. We present NumericalDiff, an execution-based method that records assignment-level numerical events, aligns traces using a tolerance-aware longest common subsequence independent of variable names and source locations, and optionally reexecutes after replacing one intermediate value with its counterpart. Among the original and all single-intervention executions, it lexicographically maximizes matched events and minimizes unmatched events. NumericalDiff supports code comparison across language and framework front ends, currently including NumPy, PyTorch, JAX, C, C++, Fortran, and Octave. We evaluate NumericalDiff on 36 controlled cases comprising 675 pair/input instances: 36 execution-stack, 588 program-representation, and 51 program-logic instances. All 24 operator-injection instances expose trace differences, including three with tolerance-equal final outputs, while complete trace alignment is achieved for all 441 canonical cross-representation instances. Within the 51 program-logic instances, intervention improves 24 alignments and raises macro-average matching coverage from 0.4210 to 0.6513. The results show that value-based trace alignment and reexecution can delimit propagated numerical differences across heterogeneous implementations.

papers.title: Deterministic Narrative Gravity: Bridging Theory of Mind and Historical Simulation through ABM-LLM Architectures
papers.abstract: Historical social simulation faces a fundamental reproducibility challenge: the stochastic nature of large language models (LLMs) introduces a digital butterfly effect that prevents exact replication across multi-turn runs. Furthermore, the inability to control low-level server parameters in commercial LLM hosting environments severely limits reproducibility. To overcome this opacity, we present a deterministic multi-agent framework coupling LLMs to an Agent-Based Modelling (ABM) pipeline grounded in Theory of Mind (ToM) and Cognitive Archaeology, and validate exact artifact identity within local, pinned execution environments using SHA-256 hashing. Run locally at temperature zero with clean per-call model reloads, the system injects differentiated cognitive states per turn through dissonance-driven behavioural modes and gated internal voices. Evaluating seven model configurations spanning 4B to 31B parameters against an ablated baseline reveals clear operational boundaries. Small models ($\leq$8B) suffer from context capacity overload, producing repetitive, specular dialogue loops. However, at $\geq$12B parameters, the ABM scaffolding breaks the monotonous response patterns seen in ablation. Crucially, these scaffolded models exhibit spontaneous diegetic expansion: they coherently expand scenario lore through tactically motivated, anachronism-free details rather than escalating into aggression. By resisting the structural pull toward premature scene closure, scaffolded sessions sustain an open terminal Narrative Vector ($V_N = \mathrm{Open}$ in 12/21 overall; 9/9 in official $\geq$12B configurations) whereas unscaffolded ablation never does (0/21). This framework provides a transparent, auditable benchmark architecture for virtual archaeology, with the full pipeline released as open-source software to enable independent replication.

papers.title: The first-order phase transitions and gravitational waves from an effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models
papers.abstract: First-order phase transitions in the early Universe can generate stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds in frequency bands targeted by proposed deci-Hz observatories. We study the gravitational-wave consequences of the right-handed gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2)_{R_1}\times SU(2)_{R_2}\to SU(2)_R$ in a Pati-Salam effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models. The ultraviolet construction fixes the gauge structure and particle multiplicities, while the scalar masses and quartic couplings are treated as renormalized inputs below the supersymmetry-breaking scale. Using a one-loop finite-temperature potential with ring resummation, we follow a strongly supercooled transition at the few-TeV scale through nucleation, percolation, completion, and reheating. The leading-order friction diagnostic does not support a runaway wall, so sound waves dominate the gravitational-wave signal, with turbulence as a sub-leading contribution; the finite acoustic lifetime suppresses the peak. For the fast-wall reference case, the spectrum peaks at $f_{\rm peak}=0.611$ Hz with $h^2\Omega_{\rm GW,peak}=1.232\times10^{-11}$, in the deci-Hz band targeted by DECIGO and BBO. We present its dependence on the wall speed, renormalization scale, and thermal screening, together with a noise-only comparison for several proposed detector configurations.

papers.title: DynOLAT: OLAT Video Prediction for Controllable Dynamic Full-Body Relighting
papers.abstract: Accurate lighting response is essential for realistic dynamic human relighting, because shadows, highlights, and color changes should follow the target illumination in both direction and relative strength. Current learning-based relighting methods can generate visually plausible videos, but they often exhibit imprecise lighting responses: shadows and highlights may drift away from the target direction, and the output brightness may not faithfully follow the relative intensities in the target environment, making the result closer to appearance harmonization than controllable relighting. To address this issue, we propose DynOLAT, a generalizable OLAT video prediction framework for dynamic full-body humans. Instead of directly synthesizing a single relit appearance, our method predicts temporally consistent One-Light-At-a-Time (OLAT) basis videos from flat-lit inputs, and then linearly combines the predicted bases according to the target environment map. This OLAT-based formulation makes the directional response explicit in the predicted bases, while the relative lighting strength is determined by the linear weights derived from the environment map. We further introduce a dynamic capture pipeline and the first large-scale dynamic full-body OLAT dataset, comprising over 24 million frames from 224 identity-outfit combinations, where different outfits of the same person define separate combinations. Experiments show that DynOLAT responds more faithfully to variations in target lighting direction and relative intensity than the tested baselines, enabling controllable video relighting while preserving fine appearance details and temporal coherence. The dataset and processing tools will be publicly released to foster future research.

papers.title: Viscot-steer: Disentangling and Transferring Visual Chain-of-Thought via Activation Steering
papers.abstract: Visual chain-of-thought (visual-CoT), also known as "thinking with images", equips LVLMs with the ability to locate and use key visual evidence for reasoning. However, acquiring such visual-CoT capabilities requires costly post-training and tightly couples them to a specific backbone, making transfer to other LVLMs difficult. Existing cross-model transfer methods typically treat visual-CoT as a monolithic capability, using a unified representation that ignores the functional distinction between grounding and reasoning and introduces stage-irrelevant interventions. To address this problem, we propose Viscot-steer, a training-free activation steering framework for transferring visual-CoT capabilities across heterogeneous LVLMs. Specifically, Viscot-steer first disentangles visual-CoT into grounding and reasoning vectors and extracts them from the source-model layers associated with the corresponding capabilities. It then aligns the vectors with the activation space of the target model and steers the grounding and reasoning layers during bounding-box prediction and reasoning-trace generation, respectively. Across benchmarks covering high-resolution visual understanding, general visual perception and reasoning, and mathematical visual reasoning, Viscot-steer transfers capabilities from different visual-CoT models to architecturally diverse LVLMs and outperforms the strongest capability-transfer baseline by an average of 1.86 percentage points on the primary evaluation metrics.
authors: Ningning Wang (University of Science and Technology of China)
Beier Zhu (University of Science and Technology of China)
Kaiyun Yang (University of Science and Technology of China)
Xun Yang (University of Science and Technology of China)

papers.title: Multi-Granularity Communication-Computing Resource Mapping for User Association in MEO-Assisted LEO Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: Low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite networks are evolving into spaceborne communication-computing infrastructures. Their user association must jointly account for the radio link and the CPU, GPU, NPU, memory, cache, storage, energy, queue, and thermal states that determine executable service capacity. This paper studies a MEO-assisted LEO architecture in which medium-Earth-orbit (MEO) regional state aggregators collect and relay time-stamped telemetry, the network operation control center (NOCC) maintains the global logical resource view and makes the final association decisions, and LEO satellites provide access and onboard execution. We develop a multigranularity representation and service-primitive-driven mapping that converts a service-level request into a target-LEO-dependent quantized resource vector. The integer formulation, exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) reference, and a capacity-aware primal-dual algorithm share the same mapped objective. Experiments use real-world service bandwidth traces, a 1584-satellite LEO shell, multiple traffic seeds, controlled load and mapping error, delayed telemetry, and temporal sessions. Relative to static mapping, the proposed method improves realized utility by 10.64% and lowers end-to-end outage by 5.70 percentage points. Target quantization reduces signaling by 19.84% with negligible utility loss. Additional load, delay, temporal, runtime, and exact-MILP audits delimit the operating region and remaining mapping uncertainty.

papers.title: On the K\H{o}nig-Egerv\'{a}ry theorem for $k$-trees
papers.abstract: The famous K\H{o}nig-Egerv\'{a}ry theorem is equivalent to the statement that a graph is bipartite if and only if the matching number equals the vertex cover number for every induced subgraph. Bessy, Ochem, and Rautenbach (J. Graph Theory 91 (2019) 73-87) generalized this theorem to $k$-paths by introducing the class $\mathcal{G}_k$ of graphs where, for every induced subgraph, the maximum number of disjoint paths of order $k$ equals the minimum number of vertices intersecting all such paths. They provided complete structural characterizations of graphs in $\mathcal{G}_k$ for $k \in \{3, 4\}$, and for odd $k$ when no cycle of order less than $k$ is present. Inspired by this nice work, we extend the K\H{o}nig-Egerv\'{a}ry theorem to $k$-trees (i.e., trees with exactly $k$ vertices). We define the class $\mathcal{J}_k$ of graphs where, for every induced subgraph, the maximum number of disjoint trees of order $k$ equals the minimum number of vertices intersecting all such trees, and provide complete structural descriptions of graphs in $\mathcal{J}_k$ for all $k \ge 3$.

papers.title: Synergizing CKM and ISAC for Environment-Aware Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Channel knowledge map (CKM) and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) have emerged as two key technologies for sixth-generation (6G) and beyond wireless networks, enabling a new paradigm toward environment-aware system design. CKMs provide static or stochastic wireless environment information a priori by learning location-dependent mappings from transceiver positions to channel knowledge of various types, whereas ISAC exploits wireless signals to sense environmental objects in real time. CKM and ISAC have primarily been studied separately in prior works, while their integration offers a promising approach for enhancing the environment awareness of 6G networks and further improving both sensing and communication capabilities. On the one hand, sensing can support CKM construction by providing location-tagged measurements and richer environmental observations, while also enabling real-time CKM refinement in dynamic environments. On the other hand, CKM can enhance sensing by offering prior environmental information for clutter mitigation, and CKM and sensing information can be jointly leveraged to improve communications. This article provides an overview of the complementary interactions between CKMs and ISAC, with particular emphasis on three design approaches: sensing-assisted CKM construction and refinement, CKM-assisted sensing, and joint CKM- and sensing-enhanced communications. We also discuss future research directions for achieving environment-aware wireless networks.

papers.title: Independence number and odd dominating models
papers.abstract: A dominating $K_t$-model, introduced by Illingworth and Wood [J. Graph Theory, 2025], is a sequence $(T_1,\dots,T_t)$ of pairwise vertex-disjoint subtrees of $G$ such that every vertex of $T_j$ has a neighbour in $T_i$ for $1\leq i 0.51075n/\alpha(G)$. This qualitatively extends the results of Fox [SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2010] and Balogh and Kostochka [Discrete Math., 2011]. An odd dominating $K_t$-model is a dominating $K_t$-model with an assignment of one of two colours to each vertex of $V(T_1)\cup\dots\cup V(T_t)$, such that every edge of each $T_i$ is bichromatic and, for $1\leq i<j\leq t$, some edge between $T_i$ and $T_j$ is monochromatic. Let $\text{had}_{\text{od}}(G)$ denote the maximum order of such a model. Our constant-factor improvement of the Duchet-Meyniel bound relies on our next result: every claw-free graph $G$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{od}}(G)\geq 2\chi(G)/3$, generalising a result of Chudnovsky and Fradkin [J. Graph Theory, 2010]. The factor 2/3 is asymptotically best possible. For $t\geq2$, we prove that every $n$-vertex graph with no odd dominating $K_t$-model has independence number at least $(n+t-1)/(2t-2)$. For the stronger notion in which every vertex of $T_j$ has a neighbour of the same colour in $T_i$, we prove the analogous results with $(n+t-1)/(2t-2)$ replaced by $(n+t-1)/(3t-3)$.

papers.title: Not Yet in the Profile: Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic User Profiling by Learning from Future Interactions
papers.abstract: On the Web, user profiling builds compact user representations from interaction histories for efficient personalization, and dynamic user profiling updates them as users' behavior and preferences change. However, new user behavior can be ambiguous, and its interpretation differs across users. To address this, we introduce Uncertainty-aware Adaptive Profile Manager (UAPM), which separates the claims in a user profile from interpretations of new behavior that are not yet confirmed, through a Profile, a Buffer, and a Rulebook. UAPM records user-specific interpretation and update rules in the Rulebook, keeps ambiguous evidence in the Buffer outside the Profile as evidence for later decisions, and writes supported general and situational characteristics to the Profile. We train UAPM with Privileged On-Policy Distillation with Dual Specialization (POPD-DS), which learns from recorded future interactions during training without access to them at deployment. Its first stage, Dual Specialization, distills a stronger model into a current-only Student and a future-informed model that becomes the Teacher. In the second stage, privileged on-policy distillation (POPD), only the fixed Teacher receives future interactions and guides the Student's own management decisions alongside task rewards. Experiments on three Web personalization tasks show that UAPM outperforms multiple baselines under the same downstream input budget, improving on the best same-budget baseline by up to 5%.

papers.title: Weak Dissolution of Groups for Rearrangement
papers.abstract: Suppose that $k$ of $n$ classrooms are to be dissolved and their students moved to the other classrooms so that the numbers of students in any two remaining classrooms differ by at most $d$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on the numbers of students for this to be possible whichever $k$ classrooms are dissolved. Moreover, we determine how small the largest classroom can be when this is possible. In particular, when all classrooms have different sizes, the smallest possible size of the largest classroom is $d+\lceil (n-d-1)(n-d)/(2k)\rceil$ if $k<(n-d-1)/2$, and it is $n$ or $n+1$ otherwise. This extends the results of Siriseriwan and Sripatak, who studied the case $d=0$.

papers.title: Holographic dissociation of tetraquark and hybrid meson in the spinning plasma
papers.abstract: We explore the dissociation of the tetraquark \(Z_c\) and the hybrid meson \(\pi_1\) in a spinning quark-gluon plasma described by the planar limit of a spinning Myers-Perry black hole. Both states are treated within one holographic framework, using a non-quadratic dilaton profile whose parameters are fixed by the \(Z_c\) and \(\pi_1\) mass spectra. Spectral functions are computed in the longitudinal and transverse channels. The boost parameter and temperature both lower the peak height and broaden the width, and the effect is stronger in the transverse channel. In both channels, the heavier 2S states melt before the 1S states. Furthermore, the two exotic channels display distinct dissociation behaviors within the same effective framework. This provides a unified holographic approach to compare how different exotic states behavior, without requiring a dynamical calculation of their binding energies.

papers.title: When Self-Consistency Hurts: The Hidden Cost of Majority Voting in Small Language Models
papers.abstract: We study prompted chain-of-thought (CoT) with self-consistency (SC), i.e. sampling N traces and plurality-voting, on small language models, a regime where per-query compute budgets are tight yet SC is commonly applied with a fixed sample budget inherited from large-model practice, regardless of instance difficulty. Across two model families (Qwen-2.5-0.5B, Gemma-3-1B) at FP16 and MLX-Q4 (4-bit quantisation in Apple's MLX framework), on GSM8K and MATH-500, we run 8 per-task and 4 task-pooled experiments at n=200-400 with 1,000x paired-bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs). Our first result is an upper bound: an oracle gate deciding per prompt whether to invoke SC reaches 109-174% of always-SC's accuracy at 23-30% of its compute in all 12/12 cases, so at N=5 always-SC is dominated everywhere on our grid. That margin is exactly the rate at which SC flips correct greedy answers to wrong, here 3-10.5% of prompts, which on Qwen-Q4 x MATH-500 exceeds the wrong-to-right rate and leaves always-SC 3 pt worse than always-greedy. Our second result is a deployable approximation: a gate over greedy-pass signals skips 45-99% of SC calls, with bootstrap CI half-widths under 5 pt, removing 36-79% of always-SC compute. Accuracy retention at those operating points has point estimates of 98.1-98.8%, which we report as point estimates because their CIs are wide (lower bounds 76-86%) over an SC accuracy of only 15-36%. The evidence covers N=5 on two <=1B families and two math benchmarks, which is the scope we claim. Code is available at https://github.com/heywanrong/SiftSC.

papers.title: Source-Anchored Visual Autoregression for Extreme Image Compression
papers.abstract: In the extreme-low bitrate range below $0.01$ bpp, image compression becomes a constrained generation problem: the reconstruction depends on inferring plausible missing details while staying close to the input image. Autoregressive token models provide an efficient coarse-to-fine prior for this setting, but the transmitted early-scale tokens often leave object identity and texture underdetermined, which can lead to source-inconsistent reconstructions. We introduce Source-Anchored Visual Autoregression (SAVAR), a generative codec built on Visual Autoregressive (VAR) modeling. SAVAR transmits early-scale tokens and a compact caption. The tokens provide image-specific layout information, while the caption supplies global semantics. SAVAR reconstructs a partial VQ-VAE latent from the retained scales, maps it to the start-of-sequence initialization, and uses the same latent to condition the caption embedding before adaptive layer normalization, separating two roles that are typically driven by a shared condition in VAR-style generation. On the Kodak and CLIC2020 datasets in the extreme-low range, SAVAR reduces perceptual distortion relative to matched ARPC retained-scale operating points, lowering LPIPS by about $8$--$9\%$ and DISTS by up to $22\%$ at a lower bpp. It reconstructs a $512 \times 512$ image in about $218$ ms on one NVIDIA L20X GPU, retaining fast autoregressive decoding in the evaluated setting.

papers.title: Decidability of Elementary Modal Logics is Undecidable
papers.abstract: We study the decidability of modal satisfiability over classes of Kripke frames defined by universal first-order sentences. Although some such classes yield undecidable satisfiability problems, decidability is guaranteed for wide families of frame conditions, including universal Horn sentences and universal sentences implying transitivity. A more than decade-old open problem asks a natural question: can decidable and undecidable cases be distinguished algorithmically? We prove that this is impossible, already for equality-free universal frame conditions over a single binary relation. More precisely, there is no algorithm that, given such a condition, decides whether its associated local modal satisfiability problem is decidable. We first establish the result for conditions with equality and then eliminate equality by passing to quotients of worlds with identical incoming and outgoing edges.

papers.title: On the sharpness of a Liouville exponent in a competitive elliptic Schr\"odinger system
papers.abstract: We identify $p_*(n)=(n-1)/(n-3)$, $n\geq 5$, as the sharp exponent for Liouville theorems concerning a two-component elliptic Schr\"odinger system with self-focusing interactions and repulsive intercomponent coupling. We consider the strictly copositive regime, in which the repulsion strength is smaller than the geometric mean of the two self-interaction strengths. Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) established a Liouville-type nonexistence result in the range $1<p<p_*(n)$. For every $p_*(n)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct bounded, nontrivial, nonnegative entire solutions whenever the repulsion strength approaches the copositivity threshold from below. The construction combines a compact variational functional, a periodic spectral gap, and uniform exterior estimates that remove a truncation. Our result gives a negative answer to the open question posed by Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) of whether strict copositivity implies nonexistence of nontrivial nonnegative entire solutions throughout the Sobolev subcritical range when $n\geq 5$.

papers.title: Dhara: Evidence-Oriented Retrieval for Indian Knowledge Systems
papers.abstract: Relevant evidence in Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) collections may be distributed across passages in different parts of a work, including verses, translations, and commentaries. Locating it requires matching natural-language questions and partially remembered verse fragments to source passages. We present Dhara, a retrieval engine combining hybrid search, chapter- and book-level Entity Notes (EN), Fuzzy Verse Retrieval (FVR), and neural reranking. Five comparisons on the 325 questions in Dhara Bench examine retrieval representations against BM25, EN's contribution, reranker quality and computation time, FVR, and Gemini. BGE-M3 single-vector retrieval exceeds BM25 in nDCG@10, Recall@20, and MRR@20 across all categories. Its scores are broadly comparable to ColBERTv2, with mean retrieval times of 0.108 s and 0.962 s under the same hardware configuration and a smaller memory footprint for chunk storage on disk. Adding EN to a direct branch with a matched candidate count improves nDCG@10 in all twelve categories with Qwen and ten with BGE; the combined ranking is capped at the same candidate count. Qwen improves nDCG@10, Precision@5, and MRR@20 over BGE in every category, at approximately 6.72 times the overall estimated serial computation time. FVR increases Verse-category nDCG@10 by approximately 20 percentage points with either reranker. Gemini is evaluated after source mapping and manual review with relevance annotations visible. The Qwen pipeline with EN and FVR has higher Recall@20 than Gemini in ten categories and stronger complete-evidence retrieval in Multi-hop questions, while Gemini retains early-relevance advantages in several categories. The results inform retrieval choices according to evidence requirements and resource budgets.

papers.title: Optimal Dividends and Voluntary Liquidation under Omega-Type Regulatory Termination
papers.abstract: We study a joint optimal dividend and voluntary liquidation problem for a company whose surplus follows a spectrally negative L\'evy process and is subject to Omega-type regulatory termination. Dividend payments are modeled as a singular control, while voluntary liquidation is an optimal stopping decision with a state-dependent liquidation payoff. When the surplus falls below a regulatory solvency threshold, an Omega clock accumulates the time spent in distress and may terminate the firm before voluntary liquidation occurs. Under dynamic programming and continuity assumptions for an auxiliary Markov subproblem, we characterize its value as the smallest controlled stochastic supersolution of the associated quasi-variational inequality. We prove that any regular stochastic solution with a dividend barrier coincides with the value function over all admissible dividend and liquidation policies, and hence is unique within this class. Using $\omega$-scale functions, we construct single-band, singleton, and no-liquidation candidates, establish sufficient conditions for global optimality, and give conditions under which these candidates supply the unique regular barrier stochastic solution. Brownian and Cram\'er--Lundberg examples illustrate how regulatory parameters affect dividend and liquidation boundaries and generate transitions between policy regimes.

papers.title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact K\"ahler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely generated must factor through a hyperbolic Riemann orbifold. As applications, we derive several new restrictions on the structure of quasi-projective groups.

papers.title: Monotonicity of Wang's recursive sequence and logarithmically complete monotonicity of the reciprocal of the inverse tangent
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a sequence $b_n$, posed by Fei Wang, which is defined by $b_1=\frac13$ and a convolution-type recursive relation. We derive the generating functions of $nb_n$ and of $b_n$, the latter of which is $\ln\frac{\operatorname{arctanh}x}{x}$, and represent $b_n$ as a moment integral over $[0,1]$ with a positive density. From this representation we prove that the sequence $b_n$ is positive and logarithmically convex, that the sequence $nb_n$ is strictly decreasing, and that the ratio $\frac{b_{n+1}}{b_n}$ is strictly increasing in $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with limit $1$, which answers Wang's problem. We also give a determinantal expression and closed-form formulas for $b_n$ involving Stirling numbers of the first kind and partial Bell polynomials. Finally, we prove that the function $\frac1{\arctan x}$ is logarithmically completely monotonic on $(0,\infty)$.

papers.title: Infinite dimensional Gaussian limits for the giant component of inhomogeneous random graphs
papers.abstract: We prove Gaussian limits for the type measure of the giant component in sparse inhomogeneous random graphs. Countable types yield convergence in a weighted Hilbert space under boundedness, irreducibility, supercriticality, and a uniform tail condition on the empirical type weights. For types on a finite dimensional closed Riemannian manifold, smooth kernels yield convergence in a negative Sobolev space for any Borel type distribution. We allow deterministic types and first order kernel perturbations; independent type sampling adds an independent Gaussian term. The proof combines a seeded exploration identity, Hilbert space martingale limits, tail estimates, and inversion of the branching operator outside the giant. Finite types with random parameters are covered. A heat kernel example gives explicit variances for all spectral modes.

papers.title: Beyond Code Translation: Agentic Android-to-HarmonyOS Migration
papers.abstract: Migrating Android applications to HarmonyOS is an important yet challenging software engineering task. Existing large language model (LLM)-based migration approaches primarily translate code at the method or file level, overlooking project-wide dependencies and workflow coordination. Moreover, ArkTS, the primary language for HarmonyOS, is relatively low-resource, and migrated applications often lack sufficient tests for reliable verification, making end-to-end migration error-prone. We present A2HTrans, an agentic framework for end-to-end Android-to-HarmonyOS application migration. Rather than performing isolated code translation, A2HTrans decomposes applications into functionality-aware migration tasks, prioritizes them through dependency analysis, and orchestrates translation, validation, and iterative repair within a unified execution workflow. To improve migration reliability, A2HTrans employs a tool-augmented verification strategy that combines compiler-based syntax checking with LLM-based semantic validation and automated repair. We evaluate A2HTrans on 14 Android applications spanning diverse sizes and domains using Claude-Sonnet-4.6 as the underlying migration model. Compared with Claude Code, A2HTrans preserves 8.3% more functional completeness, improves behavioral correctness by 8.0%, and reduces migration time by 28.8%. These results demonstrate that structured agentic execution substantially improves the reliability and efficiency of project-level cross-platform software migration.

papers.title: Token graphs of stars
papers.abstract: The $k$-token graph $F_k(G)$ of a graph $G$ has as vertices the $k$-subsets of $V(G)$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. Let $S_n$ be the star with $n$ leaves. Since every edge of $S_n$ is incident with the center, $F_k(S_n)$ is the inclusion graph of the $(k-1)$- and the $k$-subsets of the leaves. We use this identification to determine its diameter, radius, girth, Wiener index and number of spanning trees, and to decompose $F_k(S_{n+1})$ into $F_k(S_n)$ and $F_{k-1}(S_n)$ joined by a matching; the parameters of $F_k(S_n)$ that are already known, such as its connectivity, independence number, automorphism group and spectrum, are collected in an appendix. The two parameters that the identification does not settle are the domination and the packing numbers. For the domination number we prove, for fixed $k \ge 3$, that $(1-\frac{k-2}{k-1}\pi_k-o(1))\binom{n}{k-1} \le \gamma(F_k(S_n)) \le (1-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{k-2}{k-1})^{k-2}+o(1))\binom{n}{k-1}$, where $\pi_k$ is the Turan density of the complete $(k-1)$-uniform hypergraph on $k$ vertices; for $k=3$ both constants are equal to $\frac{3}{4}$, so that $\gamma(F_3(S_n))=(\frac{3}{4}+o(1))\binom{n}{2}$, and the upper bound takes the exact form $\gamma(F_3(S_n)) \le \binom{n}{2}-\lfloor (n+1)^2/8 \rfloor$, which is attained for all $3 \le n \le 10$. For $k=4$ we improve the upper bound to $(\frac{17}{27}+o(1))\binom{n}{3}$, which matches the lower bound if Turan's conjecture $\pi_4=\frac{5}{9}$ holds. We show that the packing number of $F_k(S_n)$ equals the maximum size $A(n+1,4,k)$ of a binary constant-weight code, and we characterize when the packing and the domination numbers coincide, namely, for $2 \le k \le n-1$, exactly when $n=2k-1$ and a Steiner system $S(k-2,k-1,2k-1)$ exists; in that case both parameters equal the Catalan number $C_k$.

papers.title: On Rankin Invariants of Ideal Lattices
papers.abstract: The Rankin constant $\gamma_{n,k}$ measures the largest discriminant of a densest rank $k$ sublattice of a lattice in $\R^n$ over all such lattices of rank $n$ and their exact values are mostly open. For a general lattice $L\subset \R^n$ of rank $n$, the problem of determining its Rankin invariant $\gamma_{n,k}(L)$ is to find the discriminant of such a densest sublattice. There are no general formulas to compute the discriminant of any arbitrary rank $k$ sublattice. This paper specializes to the case of ideal lattices arising from ideals of number fields, and provides two approaches to study Rankin constants: first, we propose a systematic approach to approximate the minimum discriminant by introducing subideal lattices and proving a closed-form formula to compute $\gamma^{ideal}_{n,k}(L)$, the ideal Rankin invariant of the ideal lattice. Subsequently, we establish necessary conditions on the underlying number field for the existence of an ideal lattice admitting an optimal subideal lattice with a prescribed minimum discriminant. Secondly, we consider ideal lattices with arbitrary sublattices. We compute $\gamma_{9,2}$ and improve the current known bounds of the Rankin constants $\gamma_{5,2}$, $\gamma_{7,2}$ and $\gamma_{9,3},\gamma_{9,4}$, and provide an algebraic construction of the lattice that was used in dimensions $5$ and $7$.

papers.title: TEAM: Topology-Aware, Semantic-Sensitive, General Transformer for Multimodal-Attributed Graphs
papers.abstract: Multimodal-Attributed Graphs (MAGs) organize heterogeneous data in graphs whose nodes are characterized by modalities such as text and images rather than traditional unimodal attributes. However, many representative MAG methods organize propagation around node-level states and topology-defined neighborhoods, which can obscure fine-grained modality contributions: a bounded neighborhood may contain semantically weak evidence, while compatible context need not be confined to it. To address both limitations, we propose TEAM, a modality-centric framework that constructs and encodes graph context with node-modality tokens rather than treating each node as a single interaction unit. Concretely, TEAM unfolds the local topology into a Modality Encoding Tree and performs tree-anchored semantic evidence acquisition, organizing local structural context while expanding the accessible evidence space outside the constructed local Tree. We further introduce the Modality-Source Context Transformer (MSCT), which encodes the selected node-modality tokens and coordinates interactions among modality-source groups. By retaining textual and visual attributes as separate interaction units until readout, it supports fine-grained cross-node cross-modal exchange without first collapsing them into whole-node features. Across the evaluated baselines, TEAM attains the highest reported mean on all graph-learning metrics, all three G2Text metrics, and both G2Image metrics. On Toys, it surpasses the strongest baseline by 3.37 and 2.93 percentage points in Accuracy and Macro-F1, respectively.

papers.title: Heavy tails in Gaussian-process surrogates: process-level profiling degeneracy versus observation-level identifiability
papers.abstract: In this article, we study heavy-tailed alternatives to Gaussian-process surrogates, namely Student-$t$ processes, $\alpha$-stable processes and Gaussian processes with heavy-tailed noise. These are Gaussian scale mixtures, and the position of the mixing variable decides whether the tails can be learned from a single realization. For process-level mixtures with a free amplitude, the profile likelihood of the mixing law is data-free and is maximized by the Gaussian law, the plug-in predictive is a data-free transformation of the Gaussian-process predictive, and no estimator can be consistent for the mixing law over the model along one path. For observation-level mixtures with symmetric $\alpha$-stable noise, the tail index is identifiable. Further, for one-dimensional inputs under fixed-domain asymptotics with $\alpha_0<2$ and compact hyperparameter sets, a cross-fitted plug-in estimator and the Laplace marginal-likelihood estimate computed at the global posterior mode attain the efficiency bound of the model with a known regression function, also for Mat\'ern-$5/2$ sample paths. We also characterize small-sample failures of the Laplace approximation as folds of a posterior-mode branch and give a diagnostic. Finally, in a repeated Bayesian optimization study, observation-level tails reduced regret under gross outliers, as did Student-$t$ noise, and no degradation was detected under Gaussian noise.

papers.title: The $(t-1)$-chromatic Ramsey number of cycles for three colours
papers.abstract: For integers $t\ge 2$ and $\ell\ge 3$, let $R^t_{t-1}(C_\ell)$ be the least integer $n$ such that every colouring of the edges of $K_n$ with $t$ colours contains a cycle of length $\ell$ whose edges use at most $t-1$ colours. Buci\'c and Khamseh determined the analogous number for paths and asked for its value for cycles. We answer this question for three colours: we show that $R^3_2(C_\ell)=\ell+\lfloor(\ell+1)/6\rfloor$ for every $\ell\ge 11$, and we determine the values for $3\le \ell\le 10$.

papers.title: Fefferman-Stein Type Distribution Function Inequalities on Product Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish on $R^n\times R^m$ a Fefferman--Stein type distribution function inequality in which the nontangential maximal function of the product Poisson extension is controlled by the Lusin area integral function: \[ |\{N>\lambda\}|\le C\left(|\{A>\lambda\}|+\lambda^{-2}\int_{\{A\le\lambda\}}A^2\,dx\right). \] The central idea is to establish a local $L^2$ estimate for the radial maximal function. This yields a new proof of the corresponding one-parameter inequality, avoiding Green's formula and the treatment of sawtooth regions, and extends to the multiparameter setting.

papers.title: On Proximity Subgroups of Groups
papers.abstract:
By a $	extit{proximity subgroup}$ of a group $G$ we mean a norm $
u$ on $G$ valued in a complete lattice $L$ equipped with a binary sum (an additive counterpart of a multiplicative structure). The idea is that the smaller the value $
u(y)$ is, the closer $y\in G$ is to the subgroup of $G$ defined by the equation $
u(x)= ot$, where $ ot$ is the bottom element of $L$. We test whether this notion is a suitable substitute for the usual notion of a subgroup (recovered by taking $L=\{ ot,	op\}$ with join as the sum), by showing that the form of proximity subgroups is noetherian. Intuitively, this means that proximity subgroups are as well suited for formulating and proving isomorphism theorems and homological diagram lemmas for groups as the usual subgroups are. We study several questions in relation to this, including what makes the noetherian form of usual subgroups special among all of these noetherian forms, and in fact, all noetherian forms of the category of groups.

papers.title: Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
papers.abstract: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.

papers.title: Testing Conditional Moment Restrictions in Networks
papers.abstract: Parametric models of network formation, such as dyadic logit models, are increasingly popular, but few tools exist to test their specification. This paper develops a specification test for conditionally independent dyad (CID) models based on the probabilities that these models assign to subgraphs, the patterns of links among small groups of agents. Given the agents' characteristics, a parametric CID model determines not only the probability of each link but also the probability that a group of agents forms a triangle, a star, or any other subgraph. Under correct specification, the expected frequency of each subgraph among agents with given characteristics equals its model-implied probability. This forms the basis of the testable conditional moment restrictions. The test statistic is the weighted integrated squared distance between a nonparametric kernel estimate of these probabilities and the probabilities implied by the estimated parametric model. I derive its asymptotic distribution under the null hypothesis.

papers.title: Exactly integrable field theory in $(2+1)$-dimensional space-time: the spectral equations
papers.abstract: The primary object in quantum field theories is the one-step relativistic evolution operator. In this paper we consider the evolution operator defined on the auxiliary Kagom\'e lattice with the $q$-oscillator algebra of observables, the local ingredient of the evolution operator is the $q$-oscillator $R$-matrix of the Zamolodchikov tetrahedron equation. We construct explicitly the complete system of equations (which can be seen as a specific form of nested Bethe Ansatz equations) defining the spectrum of the evolution operator. This system of equations is valid for an arbitrary initial data (occupation numbers), and the thermodynamical limit is well defined for this system.

papers.title: A Multistage Extension of Witsenhausen's Counterexample with Linear Signaling
papers.abstract: We study a multistage scalar extension of Witsenhausen's counterexample in which controller 1 observes the initial state exactly, whereas every subsequent controller observes only a local noise-corrupted state and does not inherit its predecessors' observations, so that every nonterminal action both regulates the state and shapes the signal available to the next controller. Restricting the signaling controllers to linear policies while leaving the terminal controller unrestricted, we compute the exact value within this class and reduce the optimization to a deterministic dynamic program in a single propagated variance. The optimal intermediate gains are shown to have a shrinkage form, and the value functions of that program are concave. For two stages, the benchmark admits a closed form on a matching locus, where for small effort weights it has two distinct minimizers, and at the standard parameter instance on that locus a two-point nonlinear policy strictly improves upon it. For three stages, numerical continuation at a reference instance reveals three distinct local minima, and two values of the initial variance at which the lowest of the three changes abruptly. Under the terminal-cost normalization we further prove, for every finite horizon, that the optimal linear value becomes asymptotically equal to the signaling-idle benchmark as the initial variance tends to infinity.

papers.title: Coherent Conversion of an Interacting Dark-State-Polariton Condensate into a Photonic Bose-Einstein Condensate
papers.abstract: An interacting condensate can retain an observable imprint of its preparation after the interactions are switched off. For light, accessing this regime requires separating the formation of a photon condensate from the material medium that redistributes its energy. We investigate a multimode-cavity scheme in which an interacting dark-state-polariton condensate is coherently converted into a confined photonic Bose-Einstein condensate as the atom-cavity coupling is removed. The polariton mass, matter fraction, and particle number control the condensate occupation during preparation. Remarkably, changing the mass also modifies the condensate's response to repulsion through the spatial overlap of its orbitals, even when the entire single-particle spectrum is held fixed. Ideal mode-preserving conversion conserves the full natural-orbital occupation spectrum, while finite-time few-body calculations show that additional occupation changes during transfer are much smaller than those established during interacting preparation. Once decoupled from matter, the photons evolve under the free cavity Hamiltonian while retaining correlations acquired in the interacting gas. Interference between cavity modes produces oscillations in the photon density, while resonant pair correlations persist after interaction removal and distinguish the resulting photon state from a quadratic thermal state with the same one-body density matrix.

papers.title: Guidance at Pure Noise Erodes Speaker Similarity in Few-Step Token-Conditioned Flow-Matching TTS
papers.abstract: Text-to-speech systems built from a language model and a flow-matching mel decoder now run the decoder with two to four Euler steps instead of the official ten or more. At two steps the word error rate (WER) is unchanged, but speaker similarity (SIM) drops by one to six points. This paper shows that most of this loss comes from classifier-free guidance on the first step. At pure noise the network can only return the conditional mean, so guidance shifts every trajectory by nearly the same vector. Later steps do not remove this shift, and its size grows with the length of the first step, so it is negligible with ten or more steps and accounts for most of the loss with two. Two training-free samplers are derived from this analysis. First-step unguided sampling (FSU) leaves the first step unguided and recovers $84$--$91\%$ of the two-step SIM loss on CosyVoice~2/3 with no significant WER increase. FSU-Mid replaces the two Euler steps by one midpoint step with an unguided first evaluation, recovers $77$--$85\%$ on IndexTTS-2 and matches the ten-step teacher on CosyVoice~2 and GLM-TTS. Both use three network function evaluations, one fewer than the official two-step sampler, and FSU-Mid gives the highest mean recovery among eight published guidance rules re-run at two steps on four decoders.

papers.title: Deep Learning-based Quantitative Ultrasound (DeepQUS) for Multiparametric Hepatic Steatosis Assessment
papers.abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) has shown promise for liver fat quantification in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Incorporating multiple parameters has demonstrated the potential to outperform single QUS parameter measures. Here, we propose a deep learning-based multiparametric QUS framework that learns effective integration of multiple features from QUS measures to estimate pixel-wise hepatic fat fraction, enabling the detecting of heterogeneous fat accumulation within the liver. We developed a U-Net based network architecture to predict local fat fraction percentages, which takes 2D QUS maps as input and is trained with magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) as the ground truth. We extracted 2D QUS maps (H-scan frequency, at-tenuation, Nakagami, and RF/envelope/log-compressed data) and tested various input configura-tions consisting of different combinations of the QUS parameters. We enrolled 30 patients with healthy livers or suspected/confirmed MASLD, and acquired ultrasound RF data, and validated our approach using the patient data. Among all tested input configurations, the model combining H-scan, attenuation, and Nak-agami parameters achieved the best performance, with a Spearman correlation coefficient (Rs) of 0.92 and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.98. The predicted fat fraction maps exhibited color changes concordant with the gradual increasing in MRI-PDFF, from normal liver to 45% fat ac-cumulation. These findings demonstrate that deep learning can integrate multiparametric QUS in-formation in a fully data-driven manner, providing a localized fat fraction map rather than a single whole-liver value. We anticipate that our deep learning framework can offer potential advantages for future assessment of heterogeneous disease development in liver for more complex, progres-sive liver diseases such as steatohepatitis.

papers.title: When Are Nearby Experts Composable? Cross-Task Model Merging in Neural Thickets
papers.abstract: Random perturbations around a shared checkpoint can produce experts for distinct tasks, but shared origin does not ensure that their gains survive composition. We formulate expert-pair selection for joint base-relative retention, measured by strict joint success and worst-task gain with unconditional abstention accounting. An exact finite-difference decomposition and an arbitrarily small orthogonal counterexample show why proximity and orthogonality alone are insufficient. We instantiate this formulation with quality-constrained spectral selection, a fixed-budget framework combining cross-task screening, layerwise pair geometry, separate validation, and Base fallback. Across six checkpoints, 21 task pairs, and five independent perturbation pools, the procedure improves strict joint success over Top-1 averaging throughout and leads the four-method model-scale comparison on four of six checkpoints. For the five models with at least 1.5B parameters, matched quality-only, global-cosine, and spectral ranking attain 49.1%, 50.5%, and 53.1% joint success. Under this matched protocol, the spectral selector also yields the highest worst-task gain and Weak Pareto rate and the lowest regression rate. Mean worst-task gain reaches +0.61 percentage points, while 17.1% regression and 13.0% abstention show that composability remains conditional. Project page: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Thickets-Merge/.

papers.title: A second-order estimate linear in the gradient for complex Hessian equations
papers.abstract: We use the maximum principle to prove a second-order estimate with linear dependence on the gradient for the nondegenerate complex Hessian equation on a compact K\"ahler manifold. The proof combines $C^0$ compactness and a refined concavity inequality with the use of nearby smooth admissible functions. A standard interpolation argument then yields the known uniform gradient and complex Hessian bounds.

papers.title: Quantum entanglement as a resource for self-organization and stabilization
papers.abstract: Can quantum entanglement generate macroscopic order that persists after the entanglement itself disappears? We establish such a mechanism in a driven-dissipative bosonic lattice, where local entanglement enables transport that amplifies spatial fluctuations into extended Turing patterns. For the full nonlinear dynamics with noise and disorder, we derive rigorous finite-time bounds on pattern intensity for all admissible separable evolutions, allowing arbitrary classical correlations. Quantum dynamics produces pattern intensities beyond these bounds during both formation and stabilization under noise. The excess intensity also provides a lower bound on the accumulated transport contribution beyond the separable limit. We further introduce an environment that responds to emerging order by suppressing local coherence and activating classical transport. The patterns then persist as local entanglement is lost, with both stages arising from a single time-independent Lindblad equation. These results show how transient quantum resources can establish persistent macroscopic order, opening new directions for harnessing self-organization in nonequilibrium systems.

papers.title: What Changed in Engineering Writing After Generative AI Chat Assistants: Evidence from 1.8 Million Articles
papers.abstract: This study asks what changed in engineering articles after conversational language models became publicly available on November 30, 2022, and develops methods for measuring such change in a field without a uniform abstract index. It assembled 1,839,962 articles published from 2015 to 2025 in 256 engineering journals, tracked twelve measures of wording, style, and article structure, and compared each with the projection of its own pre-2023 trend. Building the monthly series showed that records dated only by year fall on January 1 and create false January peaks unless removed. In abstracts, 31 words associated with language model output appeared 82% more often than projected (55.4 against 27.0 per 10,000 words in 2025), while four control words of the same formal register fell 16%. Words that soften a claim, such as may, fell 13%, words that strengthen one, such as clearly, rose 20%, and long words rose 11%. Author counts, reference lists, page counts, and publication volume stayed within 4% of trend. The change appears in all fourteen subject categories, and false release dates, dropping any one journal or word, and word lists chosen from the data support it. A random sample of 12,866 full texts from the same corpus, including subscription articles and weighted back to it, shows the same words rising 99% in article bodies. Statements disclosing AI writing assistance, measured apart from mentions of language models, went from none to 3.7% in 2025, four in five of them at one publisher. The design is descriptive, not causal.

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations with H\"older continuous right-hand sides
papers.abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation on bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains with $C^3$ boundary and $C^3$ boundary values. For every $n\ge2$ and $0<\alpha<1$, each continuous Bedford--Taylor solution with a strictly positive $C^\alpha$ right-hand side satisfies a global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate. There is a unique such solution, which is strictly plurisubharmonic up to the boundary. Combining new boundary estimates with weighted integral estimates for the trace of the complex Hessian along an auxiliary parabolic flow, we obtain global $C^{1,\beta}$ bounds for every fixed $0<\beta<1$ in every dimension. Green function estimates and comparison arguments near the boundary give the boundary Hessian bound. Solutions of auxiliary Dirichlet problems with locally constant right-hand sides have uniform $W^{2,2n^2}$ bounds. Rescaling and interpolation then reduce the global Hessian estimate to interior regularity.

papers.title: Do Benign-Trained Hidden-State Probes Detect Tool Errors Under Adversarial Conditions?
papers.abstract: Although hidden-state probes efficiently monitor model operation, it remains unclear whether probes trained on benign tool use remain useful for detecting incorrect actions under adversarial conditions. In this research, we assess this problem from the perspective of operational tool-action correct- ness. we use four AgentDojo suites, four conditions, and three models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, and GLM- 4.6V-Flash (9B). We perform a five-fold, task-grouped out-of-fold (OOF) evaluation for each model. We train step-specific logistic- regression probes only on benign and non-defended trajectories and evaluate them on held-out trajectories for benign, prompt- injection, system-override, and tool-poisoning conditions. We compare our hidden-state probe to mean tool-call-token entropy, negative mean tool-call-token log-probability, and self-consistency uncertainty. The paired tests highlight six significant differences after Holm correction. All of the tests involve Qwen2.5-14B- Instruct under the system-override condition, with all three scalar uncertainty metrics obtaining higher area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and average precision (AP) than the hidden-state probe. These results suggest that benign-trained hidden-state probes should not be assumed to reliably detect operational tool-action errors under adversarial conditions.

papers.title: Local study of generic dynamical systems on the b-symplectic plane
papers.abstract: Let $\Gb$ be the group of germs of planar diffeomorphisms, fixing the origin, which preserve the standard b-symplectic form. The group acts on itself, under the usual left-right action and we identify, in the generic case, a simple representative of each orbit, depending on a non-vanishing, univariate, function. We then study the action of $\Gb$ on b-symplectic vector fields. For those fields that do not vanish at the origin, we establish a flow-box type theorem, while, for those that do vanish there, we show that the study of their conjugacy classes reduces to a classification of functions. We present this classification, when the origin is a regular point for these functions, while if it is a critical point, we present the orbits of their 2-jets. Finally, we address the problem of whether an element of $\Gb$ can be realised as the time-1 map of a b-symplectic vector field.

papers.title: ClusLoad: Cluster-Guided Model Sharing for Scalable Distribution Transformer Load Forecasting
papers.abstract: Large-scale device-level load forecasting for distribution transformers is challenged by substantial cross-device heterogeneity and the deployment burden of maintaining device-specific forecasting models. Existing approaches typically rely either on device-specific models, which are difficult to scale to large transformer populations, or on global models, which reduce deployment complexity but may overlook heterogeneous load patterns across devices. To address this trade-off, this study develops a trend-clustered forecasting framework that enables model sharing among transformers with similar temporal behaviors. Representation Learning for Time Series using Time-Embeddings (T-Rep) is employed to learn compact temporal representations of transformer load series, which are subsequently grouped using a Gaussian mixture model (GMM). Representative transformers are sampled within each cluster to train cluster-specific Patch Time Series Transformer (PatchTST) models while retaining device-level predictions. The framework is evaluated using real-world 15-min operational data from nearly one thousand distribution transformers. The proposed framework reduces mean absolute error (MAE) by approximately 20% relative to the direct PatchTST baseline, achieves a high-load warning accuracy of 95.66%, while requiring only seven cluster-specific forecasting models. These results demonstrate that behavior-based device organization provides an effective balance between forecasting accuracy, deployment scalability, and risk-oriented operational support for distribution transformer management.

papers.title: Map2SLAM: From Streaming Map Prediction to Real-Time SLAM
papers.abstract: Streaming 3D foundation models (3DFMs) estimate camera poses and dense geometry online, but they fall short of SLAM: their predictions are fixed once emitted, so loop closures cannot correct accumulated drift. With such models already providing strong geometric capability, a central question for SLAM becomes how to schedule their inference and how to keep its results as revisable state. We present Map2SLAM, which keeps LingBot-Map frozen, trains only a lightweight retrieval head, and builds SLAM on the model's inference interface, turning its predictions into observations of an external persistent SLAM state. The front-end tracks every incoming frame with the model's causal streaming inference and decides which frames are written to the persistent state as keyframes. The back-end asynchronously decides when and which past frames to re-observe, re-running the model's joint inference over them with fresh context; verified loop observations correct the trajectory online, and segment observations refine dense geometry after the sequence. All invocations share a single frame encoder pass per image, whose cached features also drive loop retrieval, so frequent re-invocation incurs no additional encoding cost. Map2SLAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on KITTI, VBR, and Oxford Spires, reducing mean ATE by over 40% compared with the best uncalibrated baselines, while maintaining real-time tracking at over 28 FPS at a resolution of $518\times154$ on an NVIDIA RTX 5090D GPU. Please visit our project page at https://robbyant-research.github.io/Map2SLAM/.

papers.title: A unified approach to Manin triples of Lie algebras and the corresponding bialgebra structures
papers.abstract: We introduce self-module Lie bialgebras as a common framework for bialgebra structures associated with different types of Manin triples of Lie algebras. A self-module Lie algebra is a Lie algebra with a specified representation on its underlying vector space; equivalently, it is an NS-Lie algebra expressed in different notation. We define a generic Manin triple as a finite-dimensional Lie algebra equipped with a nondegenerate bilinear form and two complementary isotropic Lie subalgebras, and establish the equivalence among standard generic Manin triples, suitable matched pairs of Lie algebras, families of matched pairs of self-module Lie algebras and self-module Lie bialgebras. The framework recovers Lie, pre-Lie and anti-pre-Lie bialgebras as special cases and admits examples outside these three families. We also introduce the self-module Lie Yang-Baxter equation and show that its solutions yield self-module Lie bialgebras and admit the $\mathcal{O}$-operator characterization. Finally, we obtain solutions in semi-direct product self-module Lie algebras, including constructions arising from self-bimodule pre-Lie algebras.

papers.title: Numerical Stability Issues and a Mitigation Method in Switching Events Calculation Considering State Variable Discontinuities for EMT Simulation
papers.abstract: Some existing methods for switching events calculation considering state variable discontinuities for EMT simulation can encounter numerical stability issues, either over-stabilizing or destabilizing the studied power systems. This paper documents these issues in detail with a concrete example. The underlying mechanism of the issues are revealed via systematic analysis. A mitigation method for the issues is proposed. The convergence behavior of the method is analyzed. Numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the method. It is observed that the method also helps to improve the accuracy of the simulation results.

papers.title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight
papers.abstract: Dexterous manipulation requires rich spatial foresight over both the surrounding scene and the robot hand. Existing world-action models often acquire such predictive knowledge through explicit future prediction. We introduce DexForesight, a framework that learns spatial foresight implicitly by injecting dynamics-aware world representations into the latent space of a dexterous policy. During training, DexForesight learns an action-conditioned spatial world model from offline scene depth, kinematic hand geometry, and demonstration trajectories. The world model predicts 3D hand-point motion and visual feature changes, capturing both articulated hand dynamics and scene changes under demonstrated actions, including the motion of fingers occluded from the cameras. We then freeze the world model and align policy queries with its predictive world queries, transferring the learned spatial dynamics into policy latents and using them to condition action generation. At deployment, only the policy is retained, operating on RGB observations, language, and robot state without depth input or explicit future prediction. On 11 DexJoCo simulation tasks, DexForesight improves the overall success rate of the base policy from 49.4% to 60.5%. On three real-robot dexterous manipulation tasks, DexForesight achieves 58.3% success, compared with 50.0% for the strongest baseline.Project page https://dexforesight.github.io/

papers.title: The Race Is Decided Early! A Kernel Law Predicts Lock-In in Majority-Vote Test-Time RL
papers.abstract: Test-time reinforcement learning with majority-vote rewards trains a language model on unlabeled questions by rewarding the samples that agree with its most frequent answer. During training, each question locks into one answer, on hard questions often a wrong one, but which answer it locks into is known only after training. In this paper, we show that this outcome is decided early, in a short race driven by sampling noise between the answers that are close at the start, and we derive the probability of each outcome. With a separate logit for each answer, the runner-up wins with a normal tail probability of the initial gap, scaled by an explicit noise constant. In a network, however, the answer logits depend on shared parameters, and through the kernel of these parameters the updates of the trailing answers also change the gap of the two leaders. This spillover shifts the boundary between the starts won by each leader, and a closed form computes the shifted probability from a kernel probe and the start logits. In LoRA experiments with three models from two families, predictions made before training with the kernel frozen at its start value forecast which answer each question locks into better than a logistic model refitted on the outcomes, although they use no fitted constants. The closed form matches these predictions on the runs in which a check before training finds that the two leaders stay above the other answers, and it explains why a law that ignores the spillover needs a strongly inflated step.

papers.title: Tutorial: Vision-Based Formation Control with Differential-Drive Robots
papers.abstract: This tutorial presents a step-by-step introduction to multi-robot formation control using differential- drive robots, an overhead camera, and Python.
