We give complete differential and boomerang spectrum formulas and obtain closed-form evaluations for selected constructions based on Coulter--Matthews monomials and Dembowski--Ostrom polynomials. For $q>7$, comparison of differential spectra establishes CCZ-inequivalence to all APN monomial families listed in the paper and every APN binomial in the original Ness--Helleseth family or its extension by Zeng et al. We characterize CCZ-equivalence within our construction, showing that any two linearly inequivalent even PN functions over the same field yield CCZ-inequivalent APN functions. We obtain three pairwise CCZ-inequivalent APN functions with boomerang uniformity one over $\F_{p^{15\ell}}$ for every $\ell\ge1$, six over $\F_{p^{120r}}$ for every $r\ge1$, and unbounded numbers of such classes in characteristic three. We further prove that CCZ-equivalence and EA-equivalence coincide for functions at Hamming distance at most $m$ from a PN function, provided that $m(m+1)<q-q/p$. We also show that all our APN functions have the maximal possible algebraic degree $n(p-1)$. Finally, we exhibit both CCZ-equivalent and CCZ-inequivalent APN pairs with boomerang uniformity one at Hamming distance one.

papers.title: Cascading Circle Loss: Order-Preserving Contrastive Learning for Graded Legal Retrieval
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Cascading Circle Loss (CasCL), a contrastive learning framework for legal retrieval tasks with graded relevance. CasCL combines an InfoNCE objective for positive-negative separation with a cascade of ranking boundaries that model ordered relevance levels between queries and legal clauses. The framework also includes a negative-aware self-paced optimization mechanism and a relevance gain weighting strategy to improve ranking quality. Experiments on legal passage retrieval benchmarks show that CasCL consistently outperforms existing methods, including InfoNCE, Circle Loss, MNRL and Margin MSE, across both binary retrieval and graded ranking metrics.

papers.title: BAPLe++: Cross-Model Transferability and Prompt-Level Defense of Backdoors in Medical Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Medical foundation models (Med-FMs) are increasingly adapted to clinical tasks through prompt learning, which tunes a small set of prompt tokens while the backbone remains frozen. Recent work has shown that this efficiency introduces a vulnerability: jointly optimizing learnable prompts and an imperceptible noise trigger during few-shot adaptation implants a backdoor that leaves clean performance intact but steers triggered inputs to an attacker-chosen class. Since prompts are compact and readily shared, this raises two questions: whether a backdoored prompt remains effective on a different Med-FM, and whether it can be repaired without retraining the backbone. We address both in BAPLe++. First, we present the first study of cross-model transferability of prompt-based backdoors, quantified by two proposed metrics, Clean Accuracy Difference (CAD) and Backdoor Accuracy Difference (BAD). Second, we propose DePLe (Defense via Prompt Learning), which uses the infected prompt as a fixed anchor and learns a new prompt on a small clean set that preserves the clean task while diverging from the compromised embedding region. Experiments on four Med-FMs and six chest X-ray and histopathology datasets show that backdoors transfer across models, but asymmetrically and in a dataset-dependent manner. Compared with four training-free input transformations, DePLe reduces backdoor accuracy more consistently while preserving, and in several settings improving, clean accuracy. Our code can be accessed on https://github.com/Ufaqkhan/Baple-Plus-Plus

papers.title: Local turnpike property for a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model
papers.abstract: We study a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model. It couples Hamilton--Jacobi and Fokker--Planck equations for the harvesters with a reaction-diffusion equation for the resource. The coupling is nonlocal in space and time. For standard second-order mean field game systems, exponential turnpike estimates are known under assumptions such as monotonicity of the coupling. For the present system, Kobeissi, Mazari-Fouquer, and Ruiz-Balet proved algebraic convergence to a stationary solution in a space--time averaged sense, but no exponential turnpike estimate has been obtained. We prove such an estimate near a stationary solution with strictly positive density components. Inspired by the relative entropy method, we add the relative entropy of the resource density to the standard energy for local turnpike estimates. In the time derivative of this modified energy, the nonlocal coupling terms cancel. The two key assumptions are coercivity of a quadratic form determined by the stationary resource density and smallness of the relative density perturbations in $L^\infty$. Under these assumptions, we bound the absolute value of the modified energy by two terms that decay exponentially away from the initial and terminal times. We derive weighted $L^2$ exponential turnpike estimates for the harvester density, the resource density, and the gradient of the value function. We give sufficient conditions for coercivity. For each fixed $T>0$, classical solutions satisfying these assumptions exist for initial and terminal data sufficiently close to the stationary solution. We extend the modified energy estimate to a more general reaction term under the corresponding assumptions.

papers.title: Integral Compensation for Discrete-time Bearing-only Target Localization and Circumnavigation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the discrete-time control problem of driving an agent to localize and circumnavigate an unknown target at a prescribed radius using bearing measurements. Discretizing existing continuous-time circumnavigation controllers can introduce steady-state orbit bias, even at sampling rates that preserve stability. To eliminate the sampling-induced orbit bias, we propose an adaptive compensator for a circumnavigation controller formulated directly in discrete time. Driven by the estimated agent-to-target distance, the proposed compensator dynamically learns the geometric correction required to achieve the desired circumnavigation radius. Unlike existing static correction methods, neither the proposed controller nor the compensator update explicitly uses the sampling interval. Exponential convergence is rigorously established using Lyapunov-based analysis. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithms.

papers.title: Directional weak mixing and directional Kronecker for $\Z^2$-actions
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a measure preserving $\Z^2$-action on a Lebesgue probability space $(X,\mu)$ and let $L\subseteq\R^2$ be a $1$-dimensional subspace. For a rational subspace $L$, direction $L$ weak mixing corresponds to weak mixing for the measure preserving transformation $T^{\vv_0}$, where $\vv_0$ is a primitive vector in $\Z^2$ generating $L$. For an irrational direction $L$, we study two different definitions of direction $L$ weak mixing, and show that they are the same: ``Dynamical'' direction $L$ weak mixing is defined to be the absence of any direction $L$ Kronecker factors. These factors are defined in terms of almost periodicity along a finite width direction $L$ strip in $\Z^2$. ``Spectral'' direction $L$ weak mixing is defined as the absence of any direction $L^\perp$ line segments $I\subseteq\T^2$ with positive spectral measure. We also give a spectral characterization of the directional Kronecker property defined in \cite{liuxu}, and provide examples of $\Z^2$-actions $K$ that are direction $L$ Kronecker.

papers.title: ConwayNet: Interpretability, Activation Coherence, and Noise Resilience via a Game-of-Life-Inspired Lateral Inhibition in Artificial Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks achieve universal function approximation by stacking interconnected nonlinearities, but as a consequence they are sensitive to noise and resist mechanistic interpretation. In contrast, the local update rules of cellular automata, such as Conway's Game of Life, give rise to not merely interpretable but programmable dynamics. We explore a bridge between these worlds: a lateral inhibition in neural networks based on continuous Game-of-Life rules that derives inhibitory and excitatory responses from the layer input and blends them into the activation map in a state-conditioned way. The mechanism is differentiable and architecture-agnostic, and its regulation is imposed rather than learned: the rule's parameters are fixed and are not optimised, while the rule's values and derivatives shape training throughout the network. Wired into fully connected, convolutional, wide-residual and graph convolutional networks, it gives rise to several properties. Activation maps become coherent across space, depth and seeds, with coarse structure persisting through depth while fine detail is renewed at every layer. The co-activation graph of the hidden units departs from an Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph: it is laid out on the image and its giant component grows in steps, as in a spatial graph. Networks started from nearly identical initialisations, under label noise, disagree on thirty times fewer test images. Saliency maps rest on the object rather than the background, and resilience to pixel noise not seen in training is substantially improved.

papers.title: A Bayesian oriented exploration and reinforcement learning in continuous-time mean-variance portfolio optimization
papers.abstract: We propose a new reinforcement learning (RL) framework for the continuous-time mean-variance portfolio optimization with unknown market parameters. To better reflect the impact of improved information of the unknown drift on the degree of exploration, we consider a novel randomization based on continuous-time stochastic filtering. Specifically, we construct a continuous-time analog to Thompson Sampling by treating the unknown drift as a random draw from a generalized sampling distribution parameterized by the filter's posterior mean and variance. The new learning objective measures the tradeoff between the wealth performance and the weighted KL divergence between the policy and the true Bayesian posterior, which transforms the classical feedback control into an information guided stochastic policy. As a result, the degree of exploration endogenously depends on the Reward-Biased Maximum Likelihood Estimation that decays with the shrinking filter's variance. This allows us to devise an efficient model-based learning algorithm in the mean-variance portfolio optimization with theoretical guarantee and superior learning performance.

papers.title: Unified Framework with Convex-Concave Decomposition and Sparse Topological Learning for Skeleton-Based Clinical Assessment
papers.abstract: Skeleton-based rehabilitation assessment faces fundamental limitations of fixed topologies which cannot model compensatory patterns, uniform joint treatments overlook clinically important deviations, and lack of geometric understand- ing. We propose Concave-Convex Decomposition Sparse Topological Graph Convolutional Network (CC2-STG), a multi-stream model that combines geo- metric decomposition, sparse feature learning, and adaptive topology. Our framework decomposes joint relationships into complementary convex-concave distance functions to model both local and global movement characteristics, with sparse regularization with proximal optimization selecting clinically relevant geo- metric features, while multi-scale topological analysis captures non-anatomical joint dependencies in pathological movements. Experiments on the KiMoRe and UIPRMD datasets validate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance on clinical pathological movement assessment.

papers.title: Simultaneous 3D acoustic modulation and imaging of proton-induced nanodroplet vaporization for proton therapy monitoring
papers.abstract: Superheated nanodroplets exposed to ionizing radiation vaporize into echogenic microbubbles, enabling ultrasound-based radiation therapy monitoring and proton range verification. However, at body temperature, decafluorobutane nanodroplets are insensitive to primary protons, and vaporize only when traversed by rare heavy secondary particles, limiting the in vivo applicability of this concept. We previously demonstrated that acoustic modulation at pressures well below the Acoustic Droplet Vaporization threshold can transiently increase nanodroplet sensitivity to radiation, enabling vaporization by primary protons. However, as acoustic modulation was applied by a focused single-element transducer, sensitization was restricted to a small region of the irradiated volume, and monitoring required an additional imaging probe. Here, we introduce a compact implementation that combines wide-field acoustic modulation and volumetric imaging on the same large-element matrix array, enabling simultaneous nanodroplet sensitization to protons and vaporization monitoring across the entire irradiated volume. The resulting 3D vaporization maps were fitted to the proton stopping distribution to estimate beam position and width parameters. At body temperature and starting from acoustic pressures as low as 122 kPa, we observed a transition from a response dominated by secondary particles to a response dominated by primary protons. The resulting vaporization peak at the proton range enabled sub-millimeter range estimation and detection of a 1.05 mm range shift with both accuracy and precision below 0.2 mm. These results demonstrate proton range verification and 3D treatment monitoring with acoustically-modulated decafluorobutane nanodroplets and represent an important step towards the envisioned clinical application.

papers.title: Mirage: Provable Defense Against LLM KV Cache Timing Side Channels with Topology-Aware Isolation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as shared multi-tenant services, relying on advanced optimizations like KV cache and prefix sharing to improve throughput and reduce latency. However, these optimizations introduce a critical vulnerability: attackers can exploit time-to-first-token (TTFT) variations between KV cache hits and misses to infer sensitive prompt tokens via prefix-matching side-channel attacks. Existing defenses indiscriminately restrict cross-tenant cache sharing, which incurs prohibitive performance overhead and negates the fundamental efficiency benefits of the KV cache. We propose Mirage, a topology-aware emission obfuscation framework that provably bounds timing leakage without sacrificing the performance gains of cache sharing. Instead of stalling the GPU or forcing redundant recomputations, Mirage delays token emission at the gateway so the attacker observes a natural cache miss distribution, while the GPU seamlessly continues serving other requests at full speed. Mirage uses a Privacy Odometer that persistently tracks the topological novelty of prefix fan-out expansions to distinguish aggressive probing from benign traffic. Once a prefix exceeds a safety threshold, Mirage engages a two-phase policy that uses a dynamic estimator to pad the TTFT to a calibrated cache-miss baseline. On a 500-sample public corpus across three models, Mirage suppresses the timing side-channel to near the random-guessing floor, while maintaining a significantly lower TTFT than defense baselines. We further show that Mirage withstands a strong adaptive adversary and the same principle carries over to semantic caching layers.

papers.title: Embeddings for Orlicz potential spaces with applications to mixed local-nonlocal problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide further insight into potential spaces within the nonstandard framework of Orlicz functions. More precisely, we establish continuous and compact embeddings of potential spaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$ into both unweighted and weighted Orlicz spaces. Special attention is devoted to the radial setting, for which compactness results are obtained through Strauss- and Ni-type inequalities. As an application, we prove the existence of positive radial solutions to a class of Henon-type problems involving both local and nonlocal contributions in the Orlicz framework.

papers.title: 2D polaritons for Squeezing and Shrinking Light
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials have emerged as an extraordinary platform for polaritonics, given their remarkable ability to confine light to deep sub-wavelength scales. However, as material thicknesses reach the nanometer limit, macroscopic electrodynamic models become inadequate for the description of light-matter coupling in 2D materials, leaving a significant gap in our understanding of 2D polaritons. In this work, we develop a comprehensive quantum microscopic framework that describes 2D polaritons through a general, scale-less Hamiltonian. Starting from the quantum properties of a polarizable 2D surface, we derive collective excitations and we identify both transverse electric magnetic modes existing outside the light cone. Our results demonstrate that these 2D systems facilitate a powerful synergy between extreme wavelength shrinking and intrinsic quantum squeezing of electric field quadratures. By establishing this theoretical roadmap, our work provides the essential architecture for controlling non-classical states of light at the nanoscale, opening new avenues for high-precision quantum sensing and the development of next-generation optoelectronic devices

papers.title: Search sensitivity for type-III seesaw heavy leptons in simulated \texorpdfstring{$pp$}{pp} collisions at \texorpdfstring{$\sqrt{s}=13.6$}{sqrt(s)=13.6} TeV at the LHC
papers.abstract: A search for the pair production of TeV-scale heavy leptons as predicted by the type-III seesaw mechanism is presented. The analysis is based on a simulated signal and Standard Model background data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $500~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV. The ATLAS detector response is modeled with Delphes. Events are categorized based on the number of final state leptons and large-$R$ jets into nine mutually exclusive search channels. Multivariate analysis techniques are employed to separate the signal from the Standard Model backgrounds. Under the flavor-democratic mixing scenario ($\mathcal{B}_e=\mathcal{B}_\mu=\mathcal{B}_\tau=1/3$), the expected 95\% confidence level upper exclusion limit on the heavy lepton mass is approximately $1.6$ TeV.

papers.title: Effect of Turbulence and Inhomogeneities on the Propagation of Kinetic Scale Waves
papers.abstract: Context. Electromagnetic ion-scale waves are well known to occur in the solar wind. Eikonal (WKB) like effects may play an important role in the interplay between the propagation and local kinetic plasma dynamics of ion cyclotron waves. Aims. This Letter aims to explore the interplay of ICW propagation with turbulence and local kinetic plasmas using ray tracing equations for ICWs in a moving medium, in which turbulent gradients are present. Methods. Parker Solar Probe observations of ICWs in the solar wind are studied using ray equations in a moving medium. Gradients in the dispersion relation responsible for WKB evolution of ICW are constrained and compared with a Parker spiral model. Results. The empirical gradients, which contain turbulent motions, greatly enhance the efficiency of WKB effects. However, the typical refraction rates are significantly slower than expected quasilinear evolution of the observed wave populations, which suggests that local kinetic physics dominates over nonlinear expansion effects. Conclusions. Turbulence can effectively increase WKB effects due to gradients caused by nonlinear interactions. In the solar wind these gradients are not sufficient to substantially change an individual ion-scale ICW over its lifetime. Incorporating kinetic effects of expansion may help advance the understanding of generation and absorption of ICW and their role in heating in the solar wind.

papers.title: Constrained Look-ahead Guidance for Interference-Aware Flow Editing
papers.abstract: Diffusion and flow models enable powerful generative modeling, but controlled editing remains challenging due to the need to balance source fidelity and edit compliance along the generative trajectory. We propose a principled, inversion-free framework for flow-based image editing from a trajectory centric perspective. Rather than relying on inversion or heuristic guidance, we introduce a one-step look-ahead mechanism that evaluates the effect of candidate updates on both edit and fidelity rewards estimated via denoising, and adjusts the current update based on this evaluation. At each step, our method applies reward-driven corrections guided by the look-ahead evaluation under an explicit fidelity constraint, resulting in stable and coherent trajectory evolution. This look-ahead design mitigates gradient interference between edit and fidelity objectives by anticipating their interaction in future states, leading to improved trade-offs. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves stronger semantic edits while better preserving source content compared to existing strong baselines.

papers.title: AERO: Adaptive Ensemble-Disagreement Routing for Oracle Feedback in Sample-Efficient Online RLHF
papers.abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences via Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has driven substantial improvements across a wide range of tasks, but the cost of acquiring preference labels remains the dominant bottleneck in the alignment pipeline. While many recent alignment methods improve sample efficiency through active exploration over candidate responses, they typically query the oracle uniformly across contexts, even for contexts where the learned reward estimates are already reliable enough to provide synthetic labels. We propose Adaptive Ensemble-disagreement Routing for Oracle feedback (AERO), a fully online RLHF algorithm built on a Dyna-style model-based RL architecture, in which an ensemble-based Epistemic Reward Model (ERM) serves both as a reward posterior for exploration and as a learned preference-feedback model for synthetic labeling. AERO uses ensemble vote entropy, a Query-by-Committee disagreement measure, combined with an adaptive thresholding mechanism to decide which contexts require oracle feedback and which can instead receive ERM-based synthetic preference labels, concentrating expensive labels where they are most informative. Empirical results across different model families and scales show that AERO achieves highly competitive alignment performance while reducing the required oracle-query budget compared to online DPO and strong active-exploration baselines.

papers.title: Nonlinear stability and time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: We prove the global-in-time nonlinear stability and establish explicit algebraic time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system of an ideal polytropic gas in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Given a smooth initial rarefaction profile of small wave strength \(\delta>0\), we first construct the corresponding global one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier solution \(U_b(t,x_1)\) and show that it converges toward the self-similar Euler rarefaction fan in \(L^\infty(\mathbb{R})\) at rate \((1+t)^{-12/25}\). For the three-dimensional Cauchy problem under small weighted $H^3(\mathbb{R}^3)$ perturbations with zero integral of mass, momentum, and total energy, we prove that there exists a unique global strong solution $U(t,x)$ converging toward $U_b(t,x_1)$ in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$, with $\nabla(U-U_b)$ decaying in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$.

papers.title: REINS: A Self-Evolving Agent Harness for Real-Time Trajectory Planning
papers.abstract: Agent harnesses -- runtime scaffolds that wrap an LLM's reasoning loop with tool dispatch, verification, and persistent memory -- have become the standard substrate for deploying LLMs as autonomous agents, as demonstrated by Claude Code and Codex in software engineering. In trajectory planning, however, this paradigm has not taken hold: existing LLM-based trajectory planning methods either keep the LLM in the decision loop, exceeding the millisecond-level control budget, or offload it to offline rules or training-time supervision -- leaving the runtime planner non-evolving. Intermediate hybrids still lack the verification-and-consolidation loop that makes harnesses reliable. We ask: what runtime harness would let an LLM planner meet real-time constraints while self-evolving into a deployable one? We propose REINS, a harness built on three LLM-planner couplings: LLM outputs are (i) grounded to a learned variable-level dynamics model, (ii) verified via calibrated predicates and forward rollout, and (iii) consolidated into an indexed rule memory that serves future scenes in O(log n) without re-invoking the LLM. The harness closes a self-evolution loop: familiar scenes resolve by memory lookup; novel scenes invoke the LLM, whose verified outputs enrich the memory. Without modifying LLM weights, REINS attains 98%+ compliance, nearly 50% collision reduction, and 1.9-4.6 ms latency on simulated and real-world benchmarks at the tactical decision layer, with LLM invocation rate monotonically declining as memory matures. Code: https://github.com/ZhihongCui/REINS

papers.title: Rigid Lie Algebras from Semisimple Lie Algebras and Their Symplectic Modules
papers.abstract: We consider two extensions associated with a nonzero finite-dimensional symplectic module $V$ over a complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{s}$, and study their rigidity. The toral extension adjoins a derivation acting as the identity on $V$ and trivially on $\mathfrak{s}$; the Heisenberg extension uses the invariant symplectic form on $V$ to define a central bracket. For the toral extension, we compute the first and second adjoint cohomology groups in terms of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak{s}}(V)$, and obtain rigidity precisely when $V$ is irreducible. These results hold for arbitrary nonzero finite-dimensional modules. For the Heisenberg extension, we express the second adjoint cohomology as the kernel of a map combining the symplectic centralizer with an equivariant Jacobi map. A Killing-form argument shows that every multiplicity-free sum of irreducible symplectic modules gives an algebraically rigid Heisenberg extension. We also treat constructions with independent toral generators or Heisenberg centers. Repeated summands lead to explicit nonrigid examples, including a deformation to $\mathfrak{sl}_3$. The proofs use invariant cochains and recover several previously studied families.

papers.title: RoadState: A Domain-Prior-Enhanced Vision-Language System for Industrial-Grade Lane-Level Map Updating
papers.abstract: Lane-level map updating requires temporally consistent, physically valid, and auditable road-scene semantics despite occlusions, ambiguous lane markings, temporary obstacles, and viewpoint changes. We present RoadState, a production-deployed vision-language system that transforms sequential road-scene observations into structured lane-level semantics for Baidu Maps' map-updating pipeline. Its core model, RoadState-VLM, formulates road-scene understanding as autoregressive state estimation, predicting the current structured road state from the previous observation and symbolic state together with the current observation. We introduce Geometric Chain-of-Thought (Geo-CoT), which uses a directed acyclic graph of semantic dependencies as a domain prior to improve semantic consistency and reasoning fidelity across interdependent road-state dimensions. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset show that RoadState-VLM achieves 94.33% mean accuracy across six road-state dimensions, outperforming the strongest fine-tuned VLM baseline. Ablation studies further demonstrate the complementary effectiveness of Geo-CoT and temporal transition context. A cascaded routing pipeline directs routine cases to lightweight models while reserving complex cases for RoadState-VLM. Since its deployment in March 2025, RoadState has supported lane-level map updating across more than 360 cities and reduced overall production costs by 30%. Together with human-in-the-loop auditing, the system maintains robust performance under stress-test conditions. These results demonstrate how domain-prior-enhanced reasoning, structured state interfaces, selective routing, and human quality control can bridge the gap between VLM-based road-scene understanding and large-scale lane-level map updating.

papers.title: Stochastic Acceleration Downstream of Astrophysical Shocks
papers.abstract: Generation and evolution of turbulence at shock fronts are crucial aspects of the process of particle acceleration in different classes of sources. Here we aim at describing the fate of non-thermal particles and turbulence in the downstream region of an astrophysical shock, both in the case in which turbulence is solely produced upstream and advected through the shock and in the case in which additional turbulence is injected downstream. In particular we will provide an estimate of the effect of stochastic acceleration on particles accelerated at the shock and then advected behind it. The calculations will be specialized to supernova remnant shocks. The temporal evolution of the particle distribution function downstream of the shock and the power spectrum of the turbulent perturbations are both followed by solving numerically the transport equations for the two quantities, accounting for the damping of waves due to the particles that resonantly interact with them, which makes the problem non-linear. Our calculations show that, if waves are only self-generated upstream via Bell instability, they are not able to significantly modify the particle spectrum in the downstream region. Additionally, turbulent cascading in $k$-space quickly drains their energy, further limiting the stochastic acceleration of particles. If, on the other hand, there are additional sources of turbulence downstream, then these waves can contribute meaningfully to second order Fermi acceleration and alter the spectrum of particles. This may reflect in the spectrum of gamma radiation produced through $pp$ scattering downstream. Although second order Fermi acceleration is typically slower than diffusive shock acceleration, particles are expected to stay downstream of shocks for much longer times during which stochastic acceleration can modify their spectrum and affect the spectra of multi-messenger emissions.

papers.title: Writer-independent handedness identification from offline Bangla handwriting under controlled acquisition
papers.abstract: Handedness is a soft-biometric cue for forensic document examination and writer profiling, yet reported accuracies from offline handwriting rarely keep writers, texts and image acquisition apart, so models may recognise the writer or capture conditions rather than the writing hand. Such controlled evidence is missing for Bangla. Using our BanglaHand dataset of 42 writers (21 left- and 21 right-handed), who each wrote six shared prompts and two own texts under controlled collection and photography, we evaluate handedness identification with all images of each test writer held out, whole-writer permutation tests and photometric controls. An ink-gradient descriptor identified the handedness of unseen writers with 77.4% balanced accuracy (95% writer-bootstrap interval 67.7-86.5%; p=0.001) and frozen ImageNet embeddings with 69.5-72.0%. Part of this signal is stroke darkness: in a post hoc analysis, right-handed writers' strokes were darker at their centres for equal stroke width, consistent with higher pen pressure and not explained by lighting drift. With ink density and brightness regressed out, the descriptor still reached 64.5% (p=0.027), whereas writing-only shape features were weaker (60.8%; p=0.090). Handedness is thus identifiable from offline Bangla handwriting under controlled acquisition, and photometric controls are essential to interpret such cues.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels
papers.abstract: This paper studies multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) quantum communication systems employing polarization-encoded discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), based on entanglement swapping, with the goal of extending secure communications beyond the reach of a direct link. The FSO channels are subject to atmospheric absorption, diffraction, beam wander, pointing errors, and turbulence-induced fading, while background noise and detector imperfections degrade the performance. An eavesdropper controlling the channels and the relay is also considered. To analyze the performance of the considered system, both hops MIMO channels are decomposed into parallel spatial eigenchannels via singular value decomposition (SVD), photon loss is modeled using Kraus operators, and a threshold-detector model is developed for the relay. Based on these models, closed-form per-eigenchannel expressions for the relay gain are derived, which are then used to obtain expressions for the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secret key rate (SKR). Numerical results demonstrate that entanglement swapping maintains a low QBER over longer distances than direct transmission, extending the communication range beyond the noise-limited cutoff of the direct link, at the cost of a lower SKR at short distances. The crossover distance beyond which entanglement swapping prevails is determined mainly by the background noise and the detector technology, and it is demonstrated to increase with MIMO configurations. Moreover, the reach gain is shown to be maximized for a midpoint relay. Finally, since each swapping event requires a single-pair emission from both sources, a near-deterministic entangled-photon source is required, which spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources do not provide at practical key rates, whereas MIMO substantially relaxes this requirement.

papers.title: Solid factors associated to the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ on $\mathbb{Z}^n$
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq 2$ be an integer. Set $\Gamma_n=SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ (respectively $PSL_2(\mathbb{Z})$) for $n$ even (respectively for $n$ odd). Then $\Gamma_n$ acts on $\mathbb{Z}^n$ through the restriction of the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that that the von Neumann algebra $L(\mathbb{Z}^n\rtimes \Gamma_n)$ is a solid factor. This generalizes the case $n=2$ proved by N. Ozawa.

papers.title: Configurational Information and Hadron Spectroscopy in Holographic QCD
papers.abstract: Based on the concepts of entropy and complexity, Configurational Information Measures (CIMs) are tools capable of extracting information regarding physical systems from their spatially localized energy density, determining properties such as stability limits and phase transitions. In this thesis, CIMs are employed to investigate hadron spectroscopy. By utilizing phenomenological AdS/QCD models in conjunction with CIMs, cataloged meson and baryon resonances are interpolated into structures analogous to Regge trajectories, from which analytical expressions are derived to estimate the masses of higher-order excited states. These estimates are compared with experimental data to search for possible correspondences that may elucidate the properties of particles that have been experimentally detected but remain unidentified. Using this CIM-based AdS/QCD hybrid method, this work analyzes light mesons within a dynamical model, strange vector kaons in a framework that accounts for constituent quark masses, and light-flavor baryons at finite temperature.

papers.title: Evaluating Physically Grounded Procedural Reasoning in VLMs through Real-World Execution: Crochet as a Testbed
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can generate procedures that look convincing on paper, but do they work in practice? In this paper, we propose crochet as an ideal testbed for physically grounded procedural reasoning in VLMs. Crochet cannot be reliably simulated or automated: the only way to know what a pattern produces is to make it by hand, yet verification is tangible and cheap, requiring nothing but a hook and a ball of yarn. We introduce FoundationChain, a deceptively simple test of procedural reasoning: given an image of a basic crochet object, can VLMs infer how it was made and generate a pattern that produces the same result? We crochet 40 patterns generated by four VLMs by hand. Even at this scale, physical execution not only reveals failures that automated proxies cannot detect, but also enables a more precise diagnosis of their causes and consequences: while models write fluent, convincing patterns, only four are free of errors, and our analysis exposes deficiencies in visual, geometric and procedural reasoning.

papers.title: Pulse waveform morphology encodes haemodynamic signatures of impending stroke
papers.abstract: Stroke is a disorder of the circulation, yet the haemodynamic state that immediately precedes it has rarely been observed, because continuous physiological recordings before a stroke are seldom available. Photoplethysmography (PPG), recorded by every pulse oximeter and by hundreds of millions of wearable devices, captures the peripheral pulse beat by beat, but its morphology is largely discarded. Here we ask whether pulse waveform morphology encodes haemodynamic signatures of impending stroke. Using in-hospital stroke as a natural experiment that provides continuous PPG before physician-adjudicated stroke recognition, we studied intensive-care (MIMIC-III, $n=176$) and emergency-department (MC-MED, $n=154$) cohorts and described each beat with interpretable descriptors of pulse timing, amplitude, contour and variability. At a nominal 360-min horizon, morphology separated pre-recognition from stable windows with $F_1$ scores of 0.941 and 0.989 (sensitivity 0.998 and 0.980), with models transferred unchanged to the second cohort, and outperformed heart rate alone on identical windows. The signature was dominated by systolic crest time and its change from each patient's own baseline, feature attribution was concordant across cohorts (Spearman $\rho=0.865$), and morphology recorded in the first two hours of care stratified the subsequent clinical course ($F_1$ 0.714 and 0.691). In high-risk patients without stroke, 29% and 14% of windows were positive, but five-window persistence rules limited alerts to 17% and 2% of patients. The results demonstrate that the routinely recorded pulse thus carries haemodynamic imprint of the period preceding stroke, positioning pulse morphology as a candidate continuous cerebrovascular biomarker.

papers.title: Matchability-Aware Conformal Prediction for Open-Ended Language Model Generation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often do not produce calibrated uncertainty estimates for their answers. We propose CAELUM, a framework that builds semantic prediction sets while separating aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty. CAELUM samples answers using an ensemble of clarification prompts, clusters them by semantic equivalence, and estimates the aleatoric and epistemic components via kernel-based von Neumann entropy before calibrating nonconformity scores with split conformal prediction. We use a weight $w_\lambda(x)=1+U_{\mathrm{ale}}(x)+\lambda\,U_{\mathrm{epi}}(x)$ to control for the contribution of the epistemic uncertainty of each instance and fit a coefficient $\lambda^\star$ to minimize prediction set size. When the objective is nonflat and selection is stable across splits, $\lambda^\star$ could be a diagnostic, where large values may indicate epistemic dominance (retrieve, abstain) and $\lambda^\star\to 0$ aleatoric dominance (clarify). For individual queries, a log ratio $R(x)$ compares the weighted epistemic component with the aleatoric component. Theoretically, we demonstrate that the coverage is capped by matchability, the fraction of items whose reference answer appears in any sampled cluster. Empirically, this matchability can be predicted from the original question features using a lightweight classifier. We use those predictions to define a stratum and derive a conformal coverage bound within it. Across 30 LLM and dataset combinations (4-32B), mean coverage is 0.74 in the learned stratum versus 0.65 overall, averaged over the 78 evaluations using the learned classifier. Project page: https://unco3892.github.io/caelum/

papers.title: The Lagrangian Brain: A Constraint Mechanics of Mind and Machine
papers.abstract: A brain is in one state at a time, yet most of what decides its next state is absent from it: the patterns its world never produces, the statistics of a lifetime, a goal that lies ahead. In mechanics a wire acts on a bead only through a force that appears when the bead presses on it, and Lagrange computed such forces with one multiplier for each constraint. We propose that a brain follows the same mechanics. Everything a circuit knows, is told or wants is a constraint on its single state and acts through its own multiplier, which accumulates the violation and pushes the state back. Neurons and synapses carry the multipliers, each with its own time constant: inhibitory interneurons carry what never happens, adaptation the cost of staying in one state, synapses the statistics of experience, and feedback to apical dendrites the future. From this hypothesis follow Dale's law, the reciprocal wiring and balance of excitation and inhibition, the paradoxical responses of cortex and the frequencies of brain rhythms. Belief becomes the time one trajectory spends in each state, learning becomes sleep proposing laws and waking refuting the false ones, and planning becomes a wave from the goal meeting a wave from the present. Connectionism and symbolism are the limits of frozen and of instantaneous multipliers, and between them the time a circuit runs becomes the depth of its computation. A machine built on these principles, trained without gradients on 1000 solved puzzles, solves all 422,786 Sudoku-Extreme test puzzles with one trajectory each. It rediscovers the rules of Sudoku by sleeping and waking, plans shortest paths in mazes of 64 times the training area, and tracks permutations exactly on strings 25 times longer than in training, where Transformers fail. A mind, on this view, is life that learns its own constraints.

papers.title: Tunnels: Compressing the Solution Subgraph of Regular Path Queries
papers.abstract: Regular path queries (RPQs) are increasingly expected to return the paths that match them, not only their endpoints. Since the number of matching paths can be exponential or infinite, a standard way to deliver them (PMR) is the subgraph $\Hs$ of the product between the graph and the query automaton that contains exactly the nodes lying on some solution path. We show that $\Hs$ can be compressed much further when the graph is available to the decoder: most of $\Hs$ can be regenerated by re-running small parts of the traversal, and only the places where the traversal would waste significant effort on dead branches need to be stored. We formalize this as \emph{tunnels}: regions of $\Hs$ that are re-expanded from a stored entry point with a bounded amount of extra work, either an absolute budget or one proportional to the output produced. We handle the three classes of RPQs: constant-to-variable, constant-to-constant, and variable-to-variable. In the latter, we study the combination of tunnels with cutting the query at a selective articulation point of the automaton and encoding the answer as a union of Cartesian products of leftward and rightward traversals. Our experimental results show improvements of 2 to 3 orders of magnitude over the baseline space of PMR, for an acceptable increase in traversal time.

papers.title: A 43-vertex 4-chromatic unit-distance graph in the plane with girth 5
papers.abstract: We exhibit a set of 43 points in the Euclidean plane whose unit-distance graph has 83 edges, girth 5 and chromatic number 4. The smallest previously known 4-chromatic unit-distance graph of girth 5, due to Hochberg and O'Donnell (1996), has 45 vertices. The new graph is 4-critical, has trivial automorphism group, and has exactly 2n-3 edges; it is a Laman graph and its unit-distance realisation is infinitesimally rigid. The coordinates are algebraic numbers, specified as the unique real solution of an explicit system of 82 quadratic equations inside an explicit rational box. Every claim is certified by exact computation: existence and uniqueness of the realisation by a rational contraction-mapping certificate (independently re-checked with interval Krawczyk arithmetic), and non-3-colourability both by exhaustive search and by a DRAT proof verified with drat-trim.

papers.title: Tiny Evidence Region Localization with Selective Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models have made progress in general visual tasks. However, limitations remain in fine-grained visual tasks requiring evidence from minute image regions. Existing methods primarily train models using evidence-related regions while overlooking the influence of extensive background regions, resulting in a limited ability to resist interference from irrelevant regions. We propose selective positive-negative on-policy self-distillation (SPN-OPSD), which considers both evidence and background regions. Supervision from both views improves the model's ability to resist interference from irrelevant regions. Furthermore, selective token-level distillation provides more informative supervision, improving the model's ability to attend to evidence regions in Fine-Grained Visual Tasks. On Qwen3.5-2B, SPN-OPSD improves accuracy on V* Bench, ZoomBench, and MME-RealWorld-Lite from 76.44%, 45.92%, and 57.43% to 84.82%, 54.56%, and 59.56%, respectively. Similar gains are also observed on Qwen3.5-0.8B.

papers.title: Spectrogram-Based CNN Autoencoder for One-Class Anomaly Detection in Machining Vibration Signals
papers.abstract: This work presents a one-class anomaly detection framework for vibration-based condition monitoring in machining processes using a convolutional neural network autoencoder. Three-axis vibration signals acquired during industrial broaching are transformed into time--frequency spectrograms and combined into a compact three-channel representation, enabling convolutional feature learning on multivariate time-series data. The autoencoder is trained exclusively on normal process data and detects anomalous strokes based on reconstruction errors. Labeled validation data are used for threshold calibration and an independent test set is reserved for final performance evaluation. To improve sensitivity to short-lived process instabilities such as chatter, a localized residual-based metric termed Segmented Vertical Error (SVE) is introduced. Experimental results on approximately 10{,}000 broaching strokes show a clear separation between normal and anomalous process conditions under strong class imbalance. The processing pipeline is additionally evaluated on an external public turning dataset as a proof of concept, indicating preliminary applicability beyond the original broaching setup. The results suggest that spectrogram-based autoencoder models can provide a practical and scalable basis for one-class anomaly detection in industrial vibration monitoring.

papers.title: Improving the convergence of coupled quasinormal-mode theory for optical resonators
papers.abstract: Quasinormal modes (QNMs) provide a rigorous framework for describing resonances in open optical systems, including radiative and material losses. Recent coupled-QNM theories use the modes of individual resonators to predict the resonances and optical responses of coupled systems, without relying on phenomenological coupling parameters. However, their accuracy can deteriorate when the resonators confine light weakly and radiate strongly, often requiring many modes to obtain reliable predictions. Here, we introduce a reformulation of coupled-QNM theory that substantially improves its accuracy when only a small number of modes of the individual resonators are retained. The approach builds on the same underlying QNM framework but treats the fields mediating the interaction between resonators differently, leading to a new expression for the coupling coefficients. Numerical comparisons show that this extended-domain formulation is particularly advantageous for resonators with strong ra-diative losses, enabling more efficient modeling of a broader range of coupled photonic sys-tems.

papers.title: Have wind and solar energy increased electricity price volatility? And what is electricity price volatility, anyway?
papers.abstract: It is widely held that wind and solar power increase the volatility of electricity prices. This paper argues that the literature conflates two distinct types of price variation: across delivery time and across trading time. Determined simultaneously in the same day-ahead auction, prices for power to be delivered in distinct quarter-hours differ. This price dispersion, which I call "variability," is rooted in non-storability. After that auction, trading continues in intraday markets until imbalance settlement. The price for the same delivery period changes as new information arises, such as updated weather forecasts. This price "volatility" is ultimately caused by uncertainty. This paper develops a simple algebraic model of day-ahead and imbalance markets that provides a formal definition of variability and volatility, allows for their decomposition, and derives their fundamental drivers: uncertainty and non-storability. It then presents empirical data on price variability and volatility in Germany over the past 25 years, during which the share of wind and solar energy increased from zero to nearly 50% of generation. Variability followed a U-shaped trajectory, falling from the 2000s to the 2010s before increasing again. Volatility, in contrast, declined over time.

papers.title: Breaking Precision Walls in First-, Second-, and Zeroth-Order Optimizers: One Constant, Set in Advance
papers.abstract: Under power-law signal decay across directions, an optimizer can fit strong directions and miss weak ones while average loss hides it. A precision wall measures the steepest decay where the weakest direction recovers within 5% in a fixed budget. On low-rank matrix sensing and quadratics one constant sets the wall: once it dominates the denominator, Adam or grafted Shampoo is momentum descent at step $\eta/c$, setting the wall; in Shampoo, matching grafting's constant to damping restores the wall after three hypotheses failed. In zeroth-order Adam, $\varepsilon$ acts against $\varepsilon^\ast$ from a mean-square spectral model; below $\varepsilon^\ast$ error hits a noise floor. Set from true curvature or spectrum on new shapes, the rule raised the wall above the same-step default by a forecast amount: on two sensing shapes by $1.96, 1.15$ (Adam) and $1.59, 1.74$ (grafted Shampoo), and on two Hadamard-rotated quadratics by $1.12, 0.73$ (zeroth-order Adam, longer budget), rising on all seeds; fixed-step momentum at that step reaches those walls. A cosine-scheduled default (small constant giving weak modes large steps) is higher on one sensing shape, matched on new seeds of the other, and lower with the rule's constant. A default step retuned per budget catches up on rotated quadratics and population logistic regression, fails at 1 query/step on two diagonal quadratics (catching up at 16), and exceeds the rule on digits logistic regression (full-batch and minibatches, where gradient noise sets the $\eta = 0.01, 0.1$ default walls). On logistic regression the rule did not raise the first-order wall: same-step default Adam was higher (its wall on 4 new shapes at the forecast stability limit), while in zeroth order on the population loss setting $\varepsilon$ raised the wall by $0.98, 0.88$.

papers.title: LIFT: Local Metric Alignment and Foundation-guided Propagation for Few-shot Depth Completion
papers.abstract: Few-shot depth completion aims to recover dense metric depth from sparse measurements using only a small number of target-domain annotations, offering a favorable balance between annotation cost and model adaptation. We propose LIFT, a framework that harnesses both depth and feature priors from a frozen pretrained monocular depth estimation (MDE) foundation model for few-shot depth completion. Specifically, LIFT first estimates local scale and shift parameters on a coarse grid and interpolates them into smooth, dense parameter fields, providing a spatially adaptive metric depth initialization. It then progressively refines this initialization through multi-scale depth propagation guided by foundation features. Finally, a lightweight residual decoder combines multi-level foundation features with propagation correction to refine the metric depth. Extensive experiments on NYUv2 and KITTI-DC demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art few-shot performance. The source code will soon be released.

papers.title: 3D Segmentation in the Clinic: A Grand Challenge
papers.abstract: This paper describes the set-up of a segmentation competition for automatic and semi-automatic extraction of the liver from computed tomography scans and the caudate nucleus from brain MRI data. This competition was held in the form of a workshop at the 2007 Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention conference. The rationale for organizing the competition is discussed, the training and test data sets for both segmentation tasks are described and the scoring system used to evaluate the segmentation is presented.

papers.title: A Prey-Predator Framework for Tumor-Immune Dynamics: Circuit-Based Modeling with Hilfer-Katugampola Fractional Derivatives
papers.abstract: This study focuses on modeling tumor--immune interactions through a fractional-order prey--predator framework, where tumor cells act as prey and immune effector cells as predators. To capture the hereditary and memory effects inherent in biological systems, we employ the Hilfer--Katugampola fractional derivative, which flexibly interpolates between Riemann--Liouville and Caputo formulations. In addition, a circuit-based analogy is introduced to map tumor proliferation, immune regulation, and therapeutic interventions onto resistive, capacitive, and inductive elements, providing intuitive interpretation of the dynamics. Analytical investigations, including equilibrium analysis and stability criteria, are conducted across varying fractional orders. Numerical simulations reveal that lower fractional orders lead to delayed oscillations, prolonged tumor persistence, and increased sensitivity to treatment strategies compared with classical integer-order models. The integration of fractional calculus with circuit analogies offers novel insights into tumor--immune dynamics and supports the design of memory-aware therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: A quantitative two-interval criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: We aim to study whether the Weil form can detect a zero of the Riemann zeta function away from the critical line using two functions with increasingly narrow, widely separated supports. We prove that the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on every such pair at all sufficiently large separations, provided the component widths decrease subexponentially. A zero to the right of the critical line forces the normalized cross term to exceed an exponential at arbitrarily large separations, with any exponent smaller than the horizontal displacement of that zero. In particular, reciprocal-width intervals suffice. Our proof combines a short-support positivity estimate, a smooth partition of fixed test functions and a pole obstruction for a one-sided Laplace transform. We also express the cross term through prime powers in a moving multiplicative interval. The resulting criterion specifies a uniform arithmetic inequality whose proof would establish the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: Symmetry-Induced Conservation Laws, Three-Channel Attribution, and Solid-Phase Recycling in Prebiotic Enantiomeric Excess Amplification
papers.abstract: Enantiomeric excess ($\mathrm{ee}$) is the primary observable used to quantify chiral amplification across prebiotic chemistry, asymmetric autocatalysis, and multiphase crystallization. Because $\mathrm{ee} = \Delta / M$ is the ratio of net chiral excess $\Delta = L - D$ to total chiral mass $M = L + D$, identical increases in $\mathrm{ee}$ can arise either by generating net chiral excess through parity-breaking reactions or by depleting total chiral mass through symmetric phase or oligomer partitioning. Here we establish a pathwise conservation law and a model-free three-channel attribution identity for $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric reaction networks. In any closed network without autocatalytic feedback or epimerization, net chiral excess is conserved along every stochastic trajectory ($\Delta(t) = \Delta(0)$), locking liquid-phase amplification to cumulative mass loss ($\mathrm{ee}_f = \mathrm{ee}_0 M_0 / M_f$). Re-analyzing seven experimental systems shows that standalone phase removal (Channel R) loses $91.7\%$--$98.9\%$ of chiral solute into racemic sediment in closed batches and washes out under open racemic inflow. Coupling eutectic partitioning (Channel R) with solid/solution racemization recycling (Channel B) converts the precipitated solid into homochiral product ($96.5\%$ recoverable homochiral crystal mass at $96.5\%$ total and $100.0\%$ solid $\mathrm{ee}$), whereas coupling evaporative concentration with liquid-phase autocatalysis crosses the open-flow bifurcation threshold against continuous racemic dilution ($81.9\%$ homochiral yield at $92.9\%$ active chiral $\mathrm{ee}$). We further establish non-crossing parity invariants for dual-monomer networks, derive a closed-form wet--dry amplification law, and resolve a one-dimensional identifiability ridge in chiral mineral adsorption via antipodal crystal-pair protocols.

papers.title: Dispersion interaction between two bodies of arbitrary shape
papers.abstract: Based on the vacuum tensor Green's functions of electrodynamics, the Lippmann-Schwinger-type equations were derived for the correlations of electromagnetic fields. These correlations were applied within the Maxwell stress tensor and the Lorentz force formula to determine Casimir dispersion forces for two arbitrary bodies. The analysis is performed by the excitation of bodies by electric and magnetic dipoles.

papers.title: CyberBinGym: Can AI Agents Turn Binary Patches into Real Exploits?
papers.abstract: Security fixes usually reach users as compiled updates, but deployment delays leave unpatched systems exposed. During this window, comparing patched and unpatched binaries can reveal how to exploit a vulnerability, turning a defensive update into actionable information for attackers. Existing benchmarks do not measure this capability: they expose source code, rely on human-crafted challenges, or evaluate binary comprehension without requiring exploitation. We introduce CyberBinGym, a benchmark containing 100 tasks derived from real vulnerabilities in 53 widely used projects, spanning six vulnerability families and three levels of analysis complexity. Agents receive stripped vulnerable and patched binaries without source code or vulnerability information, and must combine static and dynamic analysis to recover and exploit the vulnerability. Evaluation separately measures vulnerability recovery through differential crash testing and end-to-end exploitation through flag retrieval, with trajectory audits to reject reward hacking. The strongest evaluated agent recovers the target vulnerability in 88% of tasks and exploits it in 20%. Providing the patched binary raises its exploit rate from 10% to 25% on a matched 20-task subset; with standard binary hardening enabled, it still exploits two of its 20 previously successful tasks. These results demonstrate that current agents can turn released binary patches into working exploits in a controlled setting, although exploitation remains unreliable. These capabilities lower the barriers to targeting unpatched software and compress defenders' effective response window, increasing the urgency of timely patch deployment.

papers.title: Bifurcation-based phononic frequency combs in a forced van der Pol-Duffing oscillator
papers.abstract: Here, we analyze the dynamics of a forced Van der Pol-Duffing oscillator in search of phononic frequency comb (PFC) generation. When the drive amplitude is small, quasi-periodic self-oscillations are dominant, and we obtain a PFC spectrum response of the oscillator. When the drive amplitude is sufficiently large, we obtain frequency locking. We observe that near the transition to frequency locking the PFC spectrum is strongest and has more peaks. With increasing drive amplitude, the peaks coalesce, and the PFC spectrum disappears at an infinite-period saddle-node or homoclinic bifurcation. We also study the stability of the frequency-locked responses and find that a PFC spectrum can also occur near a subcritical Hopf bifurcation. We find that the first-order averaged equations of our nonlinear dynamical system are identical to the equations of motion of the Stuart-Landau oscillator. We use averaging techniques up to second order to characterize the quasi-periodic solutions. Very good agreement with numerical integration results are obtained. We complement our analysis by proposing a phenomenological model of nonlinear dissipative coupling between two modes that accounts for the negative dissipation term in the van der Pol-Duffing equation of motion.

papers.title: Behavioral Evaluation of Large Language Models Under Cognitive Biases in HAZOP Studies
papers.abstract: Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) studies safeguard industrial processes against catastrophic accidents. Large language models (LLMs) increasingly assist HAZOP drafting, yet evaluations rely on lexical overlap. Because LLMs internalize human heuristics, prompts may trigger biased judgments. Whether frontier LLMs withstand cognitive perturbations in safety-critical workflows remains unknown. Here we show across 420 trials that three frontier LLMs resisted 96.8% of cognitive manipulations, rendering overall susceptibility statistically inconclusive. Contrary to assumed broad fragility, models rejected confirmation and availability cues. However, safety-critical risk downgrades emerged under low anchors and gain frames. Thus, automated hazard analysis requires disciplined human-in-the-loop validation.

papers.title: Locating and Repairing Domain Shift in VLM Trajectory Planning
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly adopted as end-to-end driving planners, yet they suffer from cross-city domain shift. Existing methods treat this shift as a single quantity addressed by uniform alignment or single-site editing. We challenge this view on two counts: (i) domain shift in VLM trajectory planners is inherently structured across modality and layer, and (ii) a locate-then-repair recipe matched to this structure outperforms every uniform-objective baseline. We analyse domain shift via activation patching and uncover two regularities. (F1) Modality axis. Image and text tokens exhibit distinct shift patterns in each VLM. (F2) Layer axis. The layer-wise shift partition is architecture-dependent and dataset-stable. These findings recast domain shift as a two-dimensional tensor indexed by modality (image vs. text tokens) and layer, motivating a simple principle: locate where shift occurs, and repair only there. We instantiate this principle in MoLaRx (Modality-Layer Repair), a locate-then-repair framework. The Causal Importance Score (CIS) estimates the domain shift as a modality-layer tensor and partitions the layers into functional zones. CIS-Guided Selective Repair (CISR) then applies a matched operator (Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) / low-rank adaptation (LoRA) / freezing) to repair each zone, with the composition adapting automatically to each architecture. We evaluate MoLaRx on three architecturally distinct VLMs (LFM2-VL-1.6B, Qwen2-VL-2B, and PaliGemma2-3B) across two cross-city benchmarks (nuScenes and Argoverse 2). MoLaRx attains the lowest cross-city trajectory-error gap among adaptation methods in all six main-table settings, while using 50-60% fewer trainable parameters and 8.4-10.9 ms lower inference latency. In contrast, uniform MMD-only adaptation collapses in all six settings, highlighting the importance of structure-guided repair.

papers.title: No Second Run: Does RSI Stop at Frontier Pre-training?
papers.abstract: Pre-training is where every foundation model begins; bringing recursive self-improvement (RSI) there would let AI improve the process that creates AI. Yet public RSI work has so far targeted only post-training, which starts from an existing base model, runs trials costing GPU-hours, and returns verifiable scores. Pre-training breaks all three conditions at orders-of-magnitude higher cost: a run consumes hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours over months and cannot be repeated; its objective, post-training headroom, cannot be read off any single score; and what must improve is not a model but the whole production system, from data pipelines and training infrastructure to the teams that run them. To our knowledge, we are the first to apply RSI to an entire frontier pre-training run from scratch and to report it in detail. RSI does not stop at frontier pre-training, but it changes form: since no end-to-end loop can close over a single unrepeatable run, we decompose it into smaller loops that can, each repairing a step the full run breaks. The result is 801-30B-A3B-Base, a 30B-A3B MoE trained from scratch on 11.8T tokens in three months by a newly formed team. We release it as a base model; the lightweight SFT reported here (6B tokens, no RL) only probes post-training headroom. As a base model, 801-30B-A3B outperforms Qwen3-30B-A3B and Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B, trailing only the larger Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, and keeps this position under identical SFT; with lightweight SFT alone, it achieves the highest average on four agentic benchmarks against fully post-trained models, including Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Since post-training RSI presupposes a strong base model, bringing RSI into pre-training acts on the foundation every later stage builds on. We open-source 801-30B-A3B-Base and the lightweight SFT data at https://github.com/GAIR-NLP/801-30B .

papers.title: FedSGN: Federated Sparse Grassmann Newton Learning for IoT Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection plays a critical role in securing the Internet of things (IoT). Although existing federated principal component analysis (PCA) methods can learn the subspace of normal samples without sharing raw data, they often suffer from feature redundancy that may degrade detection performance. To address this limitation, we propose a novel and effective federated sparse Grassmann Newton (FedSGN) learning method for IoT anomaly detection. Technically, our FedSGN leverages the $\ell_{2,0}$-norm constraint on the global projection matrix to eliminate redundancy and introduces an orthogonality penalty to preserve the intrinsic structure. Moreover, we develop an augmented Lagrangian solver integrated with a semismooth Newton scheme to enable parallel client updates and Grassmann projection for robustness. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves favorable overall detection performance while reducing communication overhead. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/xianchaoxiu/FedSGN

papers.title: Disentangled Stylized Image Generation via IP-Cross-Attention Rearrangement
papers.abstract: With a solid theoretical foundation and pretraining on large-scale datasets, diffusion-based methods have achieved controllable generation leveraging text and image conditions, and generating excellent stylized images is possible using diffusion models. However, previous methods face significant challenges. First, because diffusion generation is iterative, the common approach of learning implicit style representations via cycle-consistency strategies is too costly and not well-suited to diffusion, even for LoRA-based methods. Second, decoupling style is difficult in the latent space of diffusion models. Representations of attributes are coupled in the latent space of diffusion models; thus, extracting style attributes with diffusion models usually suffers from the issue of content leakage. Furthermore, because style is hard to represent in natural language, capturing style using text prompts or textual inversion is deficient. In this paper, we propose a method for achieving disentangled stylized image generation through IP-cross-attention rearrangement, based on our experimental observations. We also propose negative content guidance, inspired by classifier-free guidance, to reduce content leakage in stylized image generation.

papers.title: The $\nu$-core label order and noncrossing partitions
papers.abstract: We prove that the poset of $s$-noncrossing partitions is isomorphic to the core label order of the $\nu$-Tamari lattice introduced by Pr\'eville-Ratelle and Viennot.

papers.title: From User Behaviors to Satisfaction Judgments: Reasoning about User Satisfaction with AI Overviews
papers.abstract: The growing presence of AI overviews in everyday search makes their effective evaluation essential. Response quality has been the primary focus of existing evaluation research, with only a small number of studies examining the user perspective. These evaluations rely on queries and response content, leaving the information conveyed by user behavior insufficiently utilized. This work investigates satisfaction prediction for AI overviews from a user-centered perspective and incorporates behavioral signals into the prediction process. Applying existing behavior-based satisfaction prediction methods from traditional information retrieval to this setting, however, presents limitations. We address these limitations with STaRS, an LLM-based approach designed specifically for predicting satisfaction with AI overviews. At its core is a structured reasoning procedure: individual behavioral signals are interpreted first, and their implications then inform the prediction of user satisfaction. Reinforcement learning further optimizes this procedure, while a reward shaping mechanism alleviates reward sparsity during training. Evaluation on two real-world datasets demonstrates that STaRS outperforms the comparison methods in satisfaction prediction, providing search providers with a practical means of accurately estimating users' satisfaction with AI overviews.

papers.title: Permute-then-Adapt: Weak-to-Strong Contrastive Image-Text Adaptation
papers.abstract: Image-text alignment models such as CLIP are typically trained with contrastive learning, where unpaired examples are treated as strict negatives. While this assumption introduces noise by penalising semantically related pairs, existing solutions often rely on heuristic similarity thresholds that lack statistical grounding and sensitivity to dataset-specific noise distributions. In this paper, we propose Permute-then-Adapt (PTA), a framework that leverages efficient weak models to identify missed positives while controlling Type-I error relative to a conditional permutation reference, up to calibration approximation error. Unlike standard distillation or arbitrary thresholding, PTA estimates a random-pairing reference distribution from the weak teacher's similarity scores and uses its upper tail, determined by $\alpha$, to select auxiliary positives. The calibrated positive set is then trained against by a single multi-positive contrastive objective: each anchor maximises the total probability mass it assigns to its positive set. Offline calibration with the weak model adds negligible training overhead. Experiments show gains over heuristic soft-label approaches in object recognition, cross-modal retrieval, and data efficiency. Project repository: https://github.com/JinhaoLee/Permute-then-Adapt.

papers.title: Quadratic Bezier Splatting with Structural Initialization for Efficient Painting Rendering
papers.abstract: Stroke-based rendering is often optimized as a pixel-level reconstruction task. This over-reliance on global error reduction not only degrades strokes into fragmented curves due to a lack of structured planning, but also allows locally defective primitives to be concealed by overlapping layers. To address these issues, we introduce a model-guided framework for stroke-audited rendering. Our framework uses Quadratic Bezier Splatting to analytically model continuous curved strokes with efficient differentiable alpha compositing. Built on this renderer, a feedforward multi-scale stroke decoder provides a structural initialization with learned stroke-scale allocation, while test-time stroke optimization supplies the reconstruction capacity needed for high-fidelity refinement. We further propose a single-stroke audit mechanism that explicitly evaluates local stroke quality, preventing defective primitives from surviving optimization through layer-wise compensation. Compared with existing methods, our approach achieves coherent layouts, improves PSNR by up to 5.46 dB, yields a 16% more compact representation, and accelerates combined renderer forward and backward computation by a factor of 220.3.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Massively Parallel Simulation for Low-Thrust Multi-Revolution Rendezvous
papers.abstract: The growing demand for on-orbit servicing and constellation management in low Earth orbit requires autonomous and reliable low-thrust rendezvous. Traditional numerical methods struggle with the long-horizon nature of multi-revolution maneuvers under perturbations, while standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods are limited by low simulation throughput and poor sample efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a massively parallel DRL guidance framework. A fully tensorized, GPU-resident orbital propagator is developed to integrate $J_2$-perturbed orbital dynamics and policy optimization within a zero-copy pipeline, achieving up to a 67-fold increase in simulation throughput over conventional CPU baselines. In addition, the rendezvous problem is formulated in modified equinoctial elements and trained with a progressive curriculum learning strategy to improve convergence and generalization across increasingly challenging rendezvous scenarios. Simulations show that the proposed framework can learn robust rendezvous trajectories for complex multi-revolution rendezvous over a broad range of orbital configurations. Additional evaluations under a high-fidelity model and eclipse-induced thrust interruptions further demonstrate the robustness of the learned policy under practical mission constraints. Moreover, the trajectories generated by the proposed framework can be used as effective initial guesses for optimization-based trajectory solvers, improving the convergence of high-precision trajectory optimization. The method offers a scalable approach for real-time low-thrust guidance and trajectory optimization.

papers.title: Applicative theories can count
papers.abstract: Applicative theories offer a proof-theoretic framework for studying complexity. In this paper, we introduce a family of applicative theories to characterize classes ranging from constant-depth circuits to polynomial space. Our approach relies on a simple axiom scheme, the small variations of which allows to capture various forms of counting and alternation. This leads to highly uniform results. When applied on notation, the scheme captures bit counting, yielding a characterization of the functions computable by constant-depth, polynomial-size threshold circuits ($\textbf{FTC}^0$); when applied lexicographically, it allows for the counting of accepting computations, yielding a characterization of the functions in the counting hierarchy ($\textbf{FCH}$). Increasing the logical complexity of the induction formulas allowed in the scheme, we obtain characterizations of the functions computable by bounded Boolean circuits of logarithmic-depth and polynomial-size ($\textbf{FNC}^1$) and of the functions computable in polynomial space ($\textbf{FPSPACE}$). The latter characterization solves an open problem in the field. Finally, we investigate separation results. While it is unknown whether $\textbf{FNC}^1$ and $\textbf{FCH}$ are different, there is an oracle relative to which (relativized) $\textbf{FNC}^1$ is strictly contained in (relativized) $\textbf{FCH}$. We use this fact to separate the theories characterizing them, by exploring their ability to represent higher-order functionals.

papers.title: Optimal orders for Hilbert-valued Littlewood--Paley functions of symmetric semigroups
papers.abstract: We study the Littlewood--Paley $g$-functions associated with symmetric submarkovian semigroups and Hilbert-valued functions. For every $1 0}$, and the Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$. Compactly supported radial functions show that, for each fixed $q>2$, the large-$p$ order cannot be replaced by $p^{1/q}$ in a dimension-free heat estimate. In particular, for the case $q=2$, we answers affirmatively the question posed by Xu in his \emph{JFA} paper (2022) \cite[Problem~7]{XuJFA}. For every finite $q>2$, our lower bound gives a negative answer to the dimension-free question in Xu's \emph{JEMS} paper (2025) \cite[Problem~1.8(i)]{XuJEMS}, already for real scalar functions. Together, the upper and lower bounds establish the sharp dimension-free order $\max\{p',\sqrt p\}$ for Hilbert-valued functions.

papers.title: Nonlocal bilinear differential operators induced by a third order hypermetric in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: The third order hypermetric $\rho(x,y,z)$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is given by the Euclidean distance of the point $(x,y,z)\in(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$ to the diagonal $\Delta^{(3)}=\{(x,x,x):x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}$ of $(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$. In this paper, we consider local and nonlocal fractional versions of bilinear differential operators generated by the geometry induced by $\rho(x,y,z)=\rho(0,x-y,x-z)$ instead of the usual $|(x-y,x-z)|$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. In doing so, we obtain a fractional nonlocal version $\mathbb{D}^s(f,g)$, $0<s<1$, of the Dirichlet bilinear operator $\nabla f(x)\cdot\nabla g(x)$ which converges to this classical form when the fractional parameter approaches its endpoint $s=1$. We consider both the kernel approach and the Fourier multiplier version.

papers.title: Distributed Intelligent Ad Hoc Routing Agents for Communication at Protests During Internet Shutdowns
papers.abstract: Governments around the world are increasingly using internet shutdowns to block digital communication.
