We prove that this holds for every simple matroid of rank at most three, thereby resolving Falk's conjecture.

papers.title: Ehrhart positivity for paving positroids
papers.abstract: A central conjecture of Ferroni, Jochemko, and Schr\"{o}ter posits that every positroid is Ehrhart positive. While Ehrhart positivity has recently been verified for notable classes such as lattice path matroids and series-parallel matroids, the general conjecture remains open. In this paper, we prove that the base polytope of any paving positroid has positive Ehrhart coefficients. This establishes a new class of Ehrhart positive positroids and provides substantial evidence supporting this conjecture.

papers.title: On the dimension conjecture for global Galois deformation rings in characteristic two
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $K$ containing all primes above $2$ and all archimedean primes. Let $G_{K,S}$ be the Galois group of the maximal algebraic extension of $K$ unramified outside $S$. We prove two refined lower bounds for the Krull dimension of unrestricted global Galois deformation rings of continuous absolutely irreducible representations of $G_{K,S}$ over finite fields of characteristic $2$. As applications, we construct the first counterexamples to the dimension conjecture in every dimension $n\geq 2$ over every number field with a real prime. Over every totally real number field, these constructions also yield the first examples of such universal deformation rings that fail to be complete intersections. Furthermore, we propose a modified dimension conjecture over arbitrary number fields and in every dimension.

papers.title: Complete gradient Yamabe solitons
papers.abstract: In this paper, all complete gradient Yamabe solitons of dimension at least three are classified. More precisely, we show that complete steady gradient Yamabe solitons are either rotationally symmetric manifolds or scalar-flat manifolds. We also classify nontrivial complete shrinking and expanding gradient Yamabe solitons.

papers.title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
papers.abstract: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.

papers.title: Square-difference factorization: ring structure, torsion splitting, and ideal classes
papers.abstract: We introduce and study commutative rings whose regular ideals, or all ideals, factor into square-difference factor absorbing ideals. We establish permanence under finite products, suitable localizations and quotients, and coefficient descent for monoid algebras. For an SP-domain, the regular factorization property is equivalent to the localization obtained by inverting $2$ being zero or Dedekind; equivalently, the maximal ideals avoiding $2$ are invertible and form a discrete subspace in the inverse topology. Over an arbitrary domain, we characterize unique functorial splitting of localization on all torsion modules by a condition excluding nonzero prime chains across the vanishing set of the localized element. Complementary localizations of one-dimensional Pr\"ufer domains give a decomposition of invertible ideal groups and an exact Picard-group sequence. For an SP-domain whose Picard group has finite exponent $m$, every irreducible element has local valuation at most $m$. We also give regular-ideal criteria for arbitrary idealizations and a complete strong-factorization criterion over von Neumann regular bases. The zero ideal is treated separately throughout, and explicit examples show why unrestricted quotient and localization assertions fail.

papers.title: All Order Gravitational Wave Tails from Classical Soft Theorem for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
papers.abstract: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arXiv:2610.07134.

papers.title: pcNN-SN: a physics-enhanced predictor-corrector neural network algorithm coupled with the discrete ordinates method for neutron transport equations
papers.abstract: Super-resolution machine learning methods hold promise for addressing the high computational costs associated with high-dimensional features in traditional transport simulations. This paper proposes a physics-enhanced neural network coupling algorithm for discrete ordinates (SN) transport calculations. Based on high- and low-accuracy data, we develop a predictor-corrector neural network (pcNN) to predict correction factors for coarse-grid solutions. Based on transport equations, local physical features containing subgrid-scale information are selected as network inputs. Dimensionless transformation of physical quantities reduces the input space dimensionality and narrows the range of parameter distributions, thereby facilitating network training. Physical constraints are incorporated into the network model, and the corrected solution retains its original conservation properties. pcNN and SN transport sweeps are internally coupled, and numerical solutions are corrected online. Numerical results demonstrate that this algorithm can effectively improve coarse-grid solutions to achieve a level of accuracy comparable to that of fine-grid results. The physics-based network design enables the model to demonstrate a certain degree of reusability under different computational conditions. Compared to mesh refinement, the pcNN-SN algorithm reduces the computation time for the three-dimensional test problems by more than 60%.

papers.title: Post-Newtonian theory in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes
papers.abstract: We develop the post-Newtonian framework for the near-zone dynamics of a binary in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetime. We consider a binary interacting via a free scalar field in a fixed (A)dS background in $D+1$ spacetime dimensions, with $D\ge3$ and odd. Using a novel multipole re-summation technique, we solve for the field degrees of freedom to obtain an effective particle description in the form of a Fokker action. We derive the equations of motion for the binary up to second post-Newtonian (2PN) order, and obtain the corresponding 2PN Hamiltonian and conserved charges in phase space. We show that the conformal algebra, corresponding to the isometry algebra of the (A)dS background, is realised in phase space as a curvature-dependent deformation of the Poincare algebra at each PN order. This serves as a non-trivial check on our results. Our results provide a systematic extension of post-Newtonian effective dynamics to finite-curvature backgrounds. This could serve as a useful framework for studying bound-state dynamics in (A)dS as well as in the corresponding holographic CFT.

papers.title: Smoothness criterion for Fano orbifolds and bases of Lagrangian fibrations
papers.abstract: We establish a smoothness criterion for Fano varieties with quotient singularities. As an application, we show that if $X\to B$ is a Lagrangian fibration from a compact hyper-K\"ahler manifold and $B$ has quotient singularities, then $B$ is a projective space.

papers.title: Rapid Graviton Thermalization through a Scalar--Gauss--Bonnet Coupling
papers.abstract: We show that gravitons can thermalize much faster than the universe expands in an effective scalar-mediated model. A thermal fermion bath maintains a massive scalar close to equilibrium, while scalar decay and inverse decay, $\phi\rightleftarrows g+g$, drive the graviton distribution toward a Bose--Einstein distribution with zero chemical potential. We establish this equilibrium state and calculate how it is reached from an initially empty graviton sector. For a scalar mass of $1\,{\rm TeV}$, an interaction scale $\Lambda_{\rm int}=m_\phi/0.03$, and a Yukawa coupling $y=0.03$, the graviton occupations approach their equilibrium values to within $0.1\%$ over $0.1\leq p/T\leq5$ after approximately $0.024$ initial Hubble times, including cosmic expansion and energy transfer from the bath. This interval contains the thermal energy-spectrum peak. The scalar remains close to equilibrium, its vacuum decay widths are narrow, and the graviton interaction is perturbative over the reaction domain. Assuming the effective theory applies on this domain, our results demonstrate that gravitons can reach near-thermal equilibrium under these conditions. We also derive the present-day thermal spectrum for a specified decoupling and entropy history.

papers.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
papers.abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.

papers.title: Universal Scaling and Geometric Correction of High-Frequency Mass Transfer in Porous Electrodes
papers.abstract: Classical film theory predicts a finite diffusion-limited current at porous electrodes. Transient operation can nevertheless produce peak interfacial fluxes above this steady limit, although the time-averaged flux remains bounded. Here, we use a frequency-domain volume-averaging framework to study this transient response in porous media. In the perfectly reactive limit, the spectral Sherwood number approaches $\Shnd\sim\sqrt{\iu\wstar}$ at high frequency, with magnitude proportional to $\omega^{1/2}$, phase $\pi/4$, and a universal leading prefactor. A boundary-layer analysis shows that this response follows from local transient diffusion and is independent of the global pore geometry. Numerical results for parallel plates, circular tubes, and twelve porous microstructures confirm the scaling across variations in particle shape, symmetry, porosity, array arrangement, flow orientation, and flow strength. We also derive the first geometry-dependent correction, which depends on interfacial area, surface curvature, and sharp edges, and verify it without fitted parameters. Comparisons with published impedance measurements for a carbon-felt fiber and a vanadium flow-battery electrode are consistent with the predicted transport response. Finally, we derive bounds on pulse duration and identify operating windows for representative redox couples. These results establish a temporal route to enhanced peak transport in porous electrodes without requiring surface charge, confinement, or electrokinetic instability.

papers.title: Elliptic theory and dimension drop for operators with divergence-free form-bounded drifts in one-sided chord-arc domains
papers.abstract:
We develop a boundary value and potential theory for elliptic operators \[ L=-\Div(A
abla)+\B\cdot
abla \] with form-bounded drift in one-sided chord-arc domains. Assuming that the positive part of $\Div\B$ has sufficiently small form bound, we establish local regularity estimates and solvability of the Dirichlet problem, and construct the associated harmonic measure. Under the additional assumption $\Div\B\le0$, we construct a Green's function and prove pointwise and gradient estimates. For the characteristic distributional identity with a Dirac mass at the pole to hold, we will additionally assume either $\Div\B=0$ or $\B\in L^{n,1}_{	extup{loc}}(\Omega)$. Moreover, in the divergence-free case, we obtain a local lower bound for the Green's function, CFMS estimates, doubling of harmonic measure, a comparison principle for nonnegative solutions with zero trace, and a change of pole formula. Finally, we construct, in the upper half-space, an operator of the form $-\Delta+\B\cdot
abla$ with $\B$ form-bounded and divergence-free, whose harmonic measure exhibits dimension drop.

papers.title: A Non-Dichotomy for CSPs of Stable $\omega$-Categorical Structures
papers.abstract: We construct countable, stable, $\omega$-categorical structures with at most two binary relations whose CSPs exhibit three complexity regimes: NP-complete, decidable but not in NP, and undecidable. The templates arise from a controlled Hrushovski construction of stable $\omega$-categorical graphs $M_\alpha$ for suitable irrational parameters $\alpha>1$. Some of these graphs have NP-complete CSPs. Expanding the graphs $M_\alpha$ by the non-edge relation turns age membership into a restriction of the CSP. For every time-constructible bound $t$, there is such an expansion whose CSP is decidable but not in DTIME$(t)$. For an explicit parameter $\alpha$, the restriction to complete instances belongs to $\mathrm{coNP}$ and the full CSP belongs to $\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}$. Separating the ages of the $M_\alpha$ using graphs with large girth and prescribed density yields $2^{\aleph_0}$ distinct CSPs of these expansions, all but countably many of which are undecidable.

papers.title: Optimal Design of Shaped Pupil Lyot Coronagraph for China's Large Segmented Telescope
papers.abstract: China's next-generation large telescopes, such as the Expandable Aperture Segmented Telescope (EAST) and the Large Optical/Infrared Telescope (LOT), are being planned as flagship facilities for high-angular-resolution astronomy, including the direct imaging and characterization of exoplanetary systems (e.g., exoplanets, circumstellar disks). However, their segmented, centrally obscured apertures present significant challenges for coronagraph design: diffraction from segmented gaps and spiders severely limit contrast, particularly at small inner working angles (IWAs). To address this, we investigate an optimal Shaped Pupil Lyot Coronagraph (SPLC) architecture tailored for these telescopes, which combines a binary shaped pupil apodizer, a focal-plane occulting mask, and a Lyot stop to suppress stellar glare and enhance contrast. We further augment the coronagraph design with a two-deformable-mirror (2-DM) adaptive optics (AO) system to correct atmospheric turbulence and residual aberrations. End-to-end simulations based on site parameters for Lenghu in Qinghai Province and assuming idealized extreme AO (ExAO) correction demonstrate that the optimized 2DM-SPLC designs can achieve raw contrasts of order 10^-6-10^-7 in the V, H, and K bands, providing an upper-bound estimate of the system performance. The simulated performance highlights the advantages of the SPLC in mitigating diffraction from segmented and centrally obscured pupils while maintaining a small IWA and practical throughput, indicating that the 2DM-SPLC is a promising coronagraphic architecture for high-contrast exoplanet imaging on China's future large segmented telescopes.

papers.title: Positivity and negativity for $h$-bases for $n$
papers.abstract: A set $A$ of integers is an $h$-basis for $n$ if every integer in $[0,n] = \{0,1,2,\ldots,n\}$ belongs to the sumset $hA$, that is, can be represented as the sum of exactly $h$ not necessarily distinct elements of $A$. The classical postage stamp problem asks for the largest integer $n_h(k)$ such that $[0,n_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of nonnegative integers of size $k+1$. We consider the effect of allowing negative elements. Let $n^{\flat}_h(k)$ be the largest integer such that $[0,n^{\flat}_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of integers of size $k+1$ containing at least one negative integer. For $k=2$, we have $n^{\flat}_h(2) < n_h(2)$ if $h$ is odd or $h=4$ and $n^{\flat}_h(2) = n_h(2)$ if $h$ is even and $h \neq 4$. Proofs of these comparison results were autonomously discovered and formally verified in Lean by https://aristotle.harmonic.fun/}{Aristotle}, a formal reasoning agent developed by https://www.harmonic.fun/}{Harmonic}. In this paper we give new proofs of these results.

papers.title: PMO-Dock: Benchmarking Docking, Specificity, and Generalization in Molecular Optimization
papers.abstract: The Practical Molecular Optimization (PMO) benchmark standardized evaluation in molecular optimization, but it is built on simple property-based oracles that do not capture structure-based drug design. As the field has moved to docking-based objectives, evaluation practice has become unstandardized, and different methods report results on different docking tasks, often without a shared protocol for fair comparison or sample-efficiency constraints. To address this, we introduce Practical Molecular Optimization for Docking (PMO-Dock), a benchmark and protocol for docking-based optimization consisting of 25 tasks covering hit generation, lead optimization, and a new specificity task requiring strong on-target binding while penalizing off-target interactions. The protocol separates model development from final evaluation: validation tasks are used for hyperparameter tuning, and test tasks are held out for final evaluation and are not used during development. Evaluation on the test tasks is done under a strict oracle budget to reflect realistic drug-discovery settings. We benchmark four diverse high-performing methods spanning different optimization paradigms, Saturn (reinforcement learning), GenMol (discrete diffusion), Genetic-guided GFlowNet, and ChemLlama (LLM-based evolutionary search). Our results show no universally best method across tasks, additional analyses of hyperparameter transfer (cross-task and cross-category) and sensitivity show that transfer is often limited and varies by method, motivating method-dependent selection strategies. This benchmark provides a concrete standard for evaluating generalization to unseen tasks and sample efficiency under a limited test-time oracle budget.

papers.title: A sharp pinching theorem for closed minimal Legendrian submanifolds in the unit sphere
papers.abstract: Let $F:M^n\to\Sph^{2n+1}$ be a minimal Legendrian immersion of a connected closed manifold, where $n\ge3$, and let $B$ be its second fundamental form. We prove that if $|B|^2\le(n-1)(n+2)/n$, then, up to a unitary transformation, $F$ parametrizes a totally geodesic sphere or is a finite covering of the image of the minimal Calabi product of a point and a totally geodesic Legendrian sphere. This proves Conjecture 1 of Luo and Sun [Ann. Inst. H. Poincar\'e C Anal. Non Lin\'eaire 40 (2023), p. 548].

papers.title: Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Reinforcement Learning for Derivative-Free Model-Based Control
papers.abstract: Optimal control problems become computationally challenging when the system dynamics are nonsmooth, learned from data, or available only through a simulator. In such settings, derivatives may be difficult to obtain, and evaluating different control actions through repeated trajectory simulations can be expensive. We propose Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Optimization (HPDPO), a method that uses numerical costates to guide the search for improved controls. The costates are estimated using finite differences of the numerical model and are used to rank candidate actions. Rather than performing a full remaining-horizon simulation for every candidate, HPDPO evaluates a small set of promising alternatives and accepts a control update only when it decreases the discrete objective. We derive a first-order costate-based approximation for ranking candidate actions and establish descent of the discretized objective under rollout-verified updates. We test the method on scalar and multidimensional control problems, including examples with nonsmooth and learned dynamics. The results show good agreement with analytical or published reference solutions and lower simulation costs than the direct-rollout methods considered. HPDPO requires only forward model evaluations, without analytical or automatically differentiated derivatives of the dynamics or a learned value function.

papers.title: IC 1297: The Most Distant Known X-ray Planetary Nebula and One of the Most Luminous
papers.abstract: We present the first targeted Einstein Probe (EP) X-ray observations of any planetary nebula (PN). Using the onboard Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT), we detect X-ray emission within the central region of IC 1297. The spectral analysis yields a plasma temperature of $kT = 0.086^{+0.054}_{-0.058}$ keV ($T\sim1.0 \times 10^{6}$ K), characteristic of shocked wind bubbles in PNe, whereas there is no evidence that its Wolf-Rayet central star emits X-rays. The absorption-corrected X-ray luminosity in the 0.3--2.0 keV energy band is $L_{\mathrm{X}} = 2.8 \times 10^{32}$ erg s$^{-1}$, also consistent with a hot bubble. At an adopted distance of $\sim3.8$ kpc, IC 1297 is the most distant X-ray emitting PN found to date, opening up a new observational window on hot-bubble formation and evolution. It is also among the most luminous known X-ray-emitting PNe. Our results demonstrate the capability of the EP FXT for detecting and characterizing faint, extended X-ray sources in the soft X-ray band for distant PNe, extending the known spectral properties of detectable X-ray emitting PNe. We also compiled the X-ray properties of all 41 known Galactic XPNe, finding a clear correlation between distance and X-ray luminosity that reflects an observational bias toward detecting the brightest sources at large distances. The compilation also shows a separation in X-ray luminosity between hot bubbles powered by H-rich and [WR]-type central stars, with the latter reaching luminosities up to an order of magnitude higher. The ten most luminous XPNe all host [WR]/PG 1159 central stars.

papers.title: A recurrence in logarithmic M\"obius sums with coprimality conditions via Euler-Maclaurin
papers.abstract: We derive a recurrence for logarithmically weighted M\"obius sums by combining M\"obius inversion with the Euler-Maclaurin summation formula. Consequently, starting from estimates of orders zero, one and two, we obtain polynomial approximations for these sums for every nonnegative integer exponent of $\log$. We then extend these estimates to sums with coprimality conditions via a convolution identity and to sums weighted by the reciprocal of the sum-of-divisors function. We also study the nonnegativity of the latter sums for every positive integer logarithmic order, establishing that they never change sign.

papers.title: Imaging the topological sign of a Dirac mass with spin-polarized tunneling
papers.abstract: A Dirac mass is characterized not only by its magnitude but also by its sign, which influences the Berry curvature, Hall response, and the propagation direction of chiral boundary modes. However, local spectroscopy of magnetic topological surfaces has so far accessed only the gap magnitude $|M|$. Here we show how the topological sign of $M$ can be determined locally. We first establish the sign information that spin-resolved tunneling can access and the reference required to obtain an absolute Hall sign. Although spin--orbital entanglement generally obscures the relation between measured spin and Dirac pseudospin, crystalline rotation symmetry alleviates this ambiguity at the band edge. On a $C_3$ axis, an axial tip couples to a fully spin-polarized state whose tunneling asymmetry directly reveals the sign of the occupied-band Berry curvature, independent of orbital composition. We further show that the zeroth Landau level provides an independent mass-sign measurement with an unpolarized tip, while opposite domains and their chiral domain-wall modes provide self-consistency checks. These results pave the way for imaging the locations where the topological character changes within a material, rather than merely identifying where a spectral gap appears.

papers.title: Reduced Embry characterizations of quasinormal operators
papers.abstract: We prove that, for any two integers $2\le m<n$, a bounded operator $A$ on a complex Hilbert space satisfying \[ A^{*k}A^k=(A^*A)^k, \qquad k\in\{m,n\}, \] is quasinormal. More generally, we show that the inequalities \[ A^{*m}A^m\ge(A^*A)^m \quad \text{and} \quad A^{*n}A^n\le(A^*A)^n \] already imply quasinormality. Together with the known single-exponent counterexamples, this completely resolves the reduced Embry problem for bounded operators: the identities $A^{*k}A^k=(A^*A)^k$, $k\in S\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots\}$, characterize quasinormality if and only if $S$ contains at least two distinct integers greater than one. We also resolve the flatness problem for operators of class $\mathcal A$: equality between two consecutive normalized moments $(A^{*n}A^n)^{1/n}$ and $(A^{*(n+1)}A^{n+1})^{1/(n+1)}$, with $n\ge2$, implies quasinormality. Both results rely on an interpolation estimate obtained either from Hansen's inequality or from the transformer inequality for weighted operator geometric means. The solution to the reduced Embry problem additionally uses an extremal argument for optimal power bounds.

papers.title: Holographic Pseudo Entropy from the Rindler Method in AdS and Flat Space
papers.abstract: Via the Rindler method, we study holographic timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) for a general timelike interval in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ and flat$_3$/CCFT$_2$. The TEE is the pseudo entropy of a timelike interval. In the bulk, the imaginary part of the TEE comes from a timelike geodesic. After a Rindler transformation to a rotating BTZ black hole, the two spacelike extremal curves lie on the inner and outer horizons, and exchanging $l_u\leftrightarrow \ell l_\phi$ takes one to the other. We clarify the geometric role of the timelike extremal curve in the Rindler frame. We show that it is the line $\tilde U=\tilde V=0$ stretched between the two horizons, starting on the inner horizon, touching the outer horizon at its midpoint, and returning to the inner one. No such curve exists outside the region between the horizons. Its length, $i\pi\ell$, is independent of the interval, and it alone produces the imaginary part $i\pi c/6$. We follow the same procedure in flat space holography, where the spacelike curve sits on the cosmological horizon and the timelike curve lies between the cosmological horizon and timelike infinity. Evaluating the holographic TEE for a timelike interval in CCFT$_2$ on the plane, we find that, in contrast with the cylinder, the real and imaginary parts are equal.

papers.title: Modular Flow and Holographic Timelike Entanglement Entropy in AdS and Flat Holography
papers.abstract: Timelike entanglement entropy provides a useful probe of holographic theories, yet an explicit bulk realization of the modular flow underlying its timelike extremal curve construction has so far been lacking. We construct modular flows associated with spacelike and timelike intervals in AdS$_{3}$/CFT$_{2}$ and extend this framework to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$. Beginning with the boundary symmetry generators, we explicitly derive the boundary modular flows and extend them into the bulk, providing a systematic procedure that relates bulk modular flows to the extremal curves and holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. For spacelike intervals, the resulting bulk modular flows determine the extremal curves, whose integrated line elements reproduce the standard holographic entanglement entropy. We then generalize this approach to timelike intervals, explicitly constructing the modular flows whose fixed points reproduce the extremal spacelike and timelike curves, which give the holographic timelike entanglement entropy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first explicit construction of the modular flow associated with a timelike extremal curve for a timelike interval. The same procedure is then carried over to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$, which gives rise to the holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. Finally, we show that the flat space results obtained in this work can be recovered from their AdS$_3$ counterparts in the flat space limit.

papers.title: Block Sensitivity and Certificate Complexity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions
papers.abstract: We investigate block sensitivity and certificate complexity of monomial rotation-symmetric Boolean functions, obtaining exact formulas and structural classifications for several families. For odd-degree monomial rotation-symmetric functions, the equality $s(f)=n$ established in our earlier work yields $bs(f)=C(f)=n$. For quadratic monomial rotation-symmetric functions, we determine both measures completely and prove that block sensitivity equals certificate complexity. For consecutive quartic monomials, we determine sensitivity, block sensitivity, and certificate complexity in every residue class of the number of variables. Our principal result is an exact global block-sensitivity formula for consecutive monomials of every even degree $d\ge4$. Writing $n=q(d+2)+\rho$, where $0\le\rho<d+2$ and $q\ge\max\{2,d/2-1\}$, we prove \[ bs(F_{d,n})=n-\min\left\{\left\lceil\frac{\rho}{2}\right\rceil,d+2-\rho\right\}. \] We also establish the corresponding sensitivity formula by a self-contained argument, yielding arbitrarily large gaps between sensitivity and block sensitivity as the degree varies. For certificate complexity, we obtain exact pointwise formulas for structured run-and-gap configurations and establish additional global equalities, including $C(F_{6,8q+5})=bs(F_{6,8q+5})=8q+2$ for $q\ge2$. Our methods combine cyclic run decomposition, parity arguments, explicit sensitive-block constructions, and constant-subcube certificates. The exact global certificate complexity for arbitrary even degrees remains open.

papers.title: Sensitivity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions via Binary Necklaces
papers.abstract: Rotation symmetric Boolean functions are important structured families in the theory of Boolean functions, where cyclic invariance permits compact algebraic descriptions while retaining nontrivial local behavior. We investigate their sensitivity through binary necklaces and monomial orbit sums. In the necklace quotient of the Boolean cube, ordinary adjacency does not record the number of coordinate flips: we give a directed flip-multiplicity formula involving stabilizers and distance-two near-periods, and derive exact local sensitivity formulas when the number of variables is an odd prime. For monomial rotation symmetric functions we determine sensitivity for all odd degrees and for quadratic orbit sums. For the consecutive-monomial family of every even degree $d\ge4$, we prove a run-cluster inequality and obtain the eventual exact formula $s(F_{d,n})=n-\min\{r,d+2-r\}$, where $n\equiv r\pmod{d+2}$, under the stated length hypothesis. The consecutive quartic case follows explicitly. We also evaluate sensitivity for cyclic run-threshold functions. Our results provide exact combinatorial and complexity-theoretic information about cyclic Boolean functions and clarify how cyclic symmetry governs local sensitivity.

papers.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
papers.abstract: We establish a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) that integrates three components: (i) a comprehensive, self-contained treatment of its particle-physics foundations and a broad range of model classes; (ii) a systematic, quantitative mapping from microscopic dark-sector physics to structure-formation simulation inputs through explicit expressions and numerical prescriptions; and (iii) the development, implementation, and validation of a broad suite of SIDM algorithms and a dedicated DM decay module in the moving-mesh code AREPO-2. Under (i), we detail the particle content, symmetries, interactions, production mechanisms, and constraints of a broad landscape of elementary and composite SIDM models, and present representative viable benchmark models. Under (ii), the mapping specifies cosmological initial conditions, internal-state masses and populations, reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, dissipative energy loss, and decay rates and recoil kinematics. We then apply this mapping to a broad range of SIDM model classes. Under (iii), we implement and validate SIDM algorithms with constant and velocity-dependent cross sections, covering isotropic and anisotropic scattering, multi-state elastic and inelastic reactions, and dissipative processes, alongside a dedicated DM decay module in AREPO-2. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection, thermalization and decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. The results recover analytical predictions and published benchmarks and demonstrate agreement across numerical schemes. Our theory-to-simulation framework serves as a cross-disciplinary reference and a practical bridge between SIDM particle physics and simulations of nonlinear structure formation.

papers.title: On the Stability of the Independence Number of the Distance Graph G(n,r,<s) for Growing r and s
papers.abstract: We consider a random subgraph G_p(n,r,<s) of the complete distance graph G(n,r,<s) whose vertices are the r-element subsets of the set {1,...,n} and whose edges join pairs of subsets that intersect in fewer than s elements; each edge survives independently of the others with probability p. The stability of the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem is the event that the independence number of the random subgraph equals that of the original graph, N = C_{n-s}^{r-s}. For fixed r and s, two-sided bounds for the critical probability, whose ratio depends on r and s, were obtained by P. A. Ogarok and A. M. Raigorodskii. In this paper we establish the order of the critical probability for growing r=r(n) and s=s(n): if min{C_r^s r^2, s r^3} = o(n), then the upper and lower bounds differ only by an absolute constant factor. The proof is elementary; only one of the two branches of the growth condition uses the complete nontrivial-intersection theorem of Ahlswede-Khachatrian.

papers.title: An Integrated Framework for Rule-Based Data Editing
papers.abstract: Statistical data editing in official statistics must restore consistency while limiting changes to observed data. Exact minimum-change correction can be computationally demanding. This paper develops a general framework for structured data whose dependencies admit a normalized acyclic routing representation. It connects routing metadata and explicitly specified semantic edits to logical admissibility, violation diagnosis, and correction. Under stated record semantics, the generated Horn theory characterizes admissibility without materializing its deductive closure. Canonical indices preserve the origin of each requirement and identify the variables that can affect a violation. With complete diagnostics and strictly positive weights, a nonnegative violation Hamiltonian vanishes exactly on admissible records within the specified domain. This characterization is independent of the correction procedure and provides both an objective for correction and a certificate: a verified zero-energy output is admissible and globally minimizes violation energy within its permitted candidate domain. Minimum modification cost is formulated separately, with sufficient conditions for an equivalent penalized objective and optimality certificates based on attained lower bounds. A household survey application illustrates the construction, the verification of admissible corrections, and minimum-cost certification for a subset of outputs. The framework supports traceable validation and correction in official statistics, while statistical accuracy of replacement values requires separate assessment.

papers.title: Well-posedness for the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation posed on a classical kinetic phase space. The nonlinear factor $f(1-f)$ appears both in the transport term and in the collision part of the Fokker-Planck operator, accounting for the exclusion principle of fermions. We prove the existence and uniqueness of global solutions without any smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. To construct solutions, we use a vanishing viscosity approximation by adding a Laplacian in the spatial variable. We derive uniform estimates for the regularized problem and obtain compactness in the space of functions of bounded variation $(BV),$ allowing us to pass to the limit as the spatial viscosity vanishes. Since the limiting equation is degenerate with a nonlinear transport, we formulate an appropriate notion of entropy solutions incorporating the kinetic structure of the equation. We prove uniqueness within this class and show that every vanishing-viscosity limit satisfies the entropy formulation. Our result provides a global well-posedness theory beyond the perturbative regime.

papers.title: Bogoliubov excitations of a Bose-Einstein condensate in the presence of the non-Hermitian skin effect
papers.abstract: The non-Hermitian skin effect is one of the most remarkable topological features of non-conservative physics. It causes a macroscopic accumulation of states at the boundaries of a confined system, opening new ways for controlling and directing waves in non-Hermitian settings. The non-Hermitian skin effect has recently been observed in experiments with Bose-Einstein condensates of exciton polaritons and ultracold bosonic quantum gases. Here, we develop a non-Hermitian extension of the Bogoliubov-de-Gennes theory for the collective excitations of the condensate, both in the semiclassical (mean-field) and second-quantised framework. By considering a trapped condensate under the action of an imaginary gauge field, we find that while the repulsive interactions oppose the localisation of the condensate, its excitations continue to display a strong skin effect. As a consequence, in the presence of harmonic confinement, we predict a strong shift in the dipole oscillation frequency, in contrast to Hermitian systems, where this frequency is fixed by the trap dimensions. Furthermore, we find that a second-quantised treatment removes the shift of the dipole oscillation frequency entirely. The two approaches describe different physical regimes, and identifying which one a given platform realises requires a microscopic open-system description. We suggest that this discrepancy between the two theoretical approaches can be resolved in experiments.

papers.title: Equilibria and Consensus in Mixed Weighted-Average and Weighted-Median Opinion Dynamics: The Consensus-Promoting Role of Weighted-Average Individuals
papers.abstract: How individuals respond to their neighbors' opinions shapes whether a networked group reaches consensus. This paper analyzes synchronous discrete-time opinion dynamics on a fixed influence network, where individuals use either weighted-average (WA) or weighted-median (WM) opinion-aggregation mechanisms with individual-specific inertia coefficients. We characterize equilibria through graph-theoretic conditions on opinion level sets and WA balance equations, proving that every solution converges to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium. We define type-dependent cohesive sets, whose WA members assign all their influence weight to the set and WM members assign at least half. The absence of two disjoint such sets gives a necessary and sufficient graph-theoretic criterion for consensus from any initial condition. Otherwise, an open set of initial conditions leads to persistent dissensus. Converting WM individuals to WA cannot create type-dependent cohesive sets and preserves existing guarantees of consensus from any initial condition. If the conversion eliminates every disjoint pair of these sets, the converted system also guarantees consensus from any initial condition. Four numerical studies examine the locations and proportion of weighted-average individuals, as well as the influence weights, while comparing the consensus criterion with finite-horizon simulation outcomes. In the four network ensembles with 100 individuals, the observed frequency of reaching a prescribed consensus tolerance is nondecreasing with WA proportion at each tested simulation horizon. This trend supports the consensus-promoting role of WA individuals, although individual realizations need not follow it.

papers.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
papers.abstract: We prove cone restriction estimates under half-scale dimensional conditions. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we incorporate the broad restriction estimate of Ou--Wang and a localized multilinear estimate obtained through cyclic bilinear pairing and multilinear Kakeya bounds for local packet energies. For certain ambient and weight dimensions, our estimates are sharp in suitable ranges of $p$, up to an $R^\varepsilon$ loss.

papers.title: Perfect discrimination of an orthogonal $2\otimes2$ basis may require collective separable measurements on two copies
papers.abstract: We consider an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2$ with three entangled states and one product state. This basis is not perfectly distinguishable by LOCC or even by separable measurements when a single copy of the unknown state is available. We show that with two copies no adaptive separable protocol, which measures the copies one at a time, distinguishes the basis perfectly. We then show that a collective separable measurement on the two copies does. Whether two copies suffice for LOCC remains open.

papers.title: Double circulant LCD codes over $\mathbb{F}_2+u\mathbb{F}_2$ and their related binary LCD codes
papers.abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ which attains the asymptotic Gilbert--Varshamov bound, i.e., whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/2)$ from below. More importantly from the constructive viewpoint, by combining Gray images with a known extension construction, we obtain a binary LCD code with previously unknown parameters $[29,15,7]$ and construct two explicit permutation-inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters $[45,23,9]$ and nine binary LCD codes with the best known parameters.

papers.title: Low Lying Zeros of Dedekind Zeta Functions
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n_K$, and let $h(K)$ denote the smallest absolute value of the imaginary part of a non-trivial zero of its Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K$. In 1979, Hoffstein proved the unconditional bound $h(K)\leq 0.87+o(1)$ as $n_K\to\infty$. In a 1990 survey, Odlyzko announced the stronger bound $h(K)\leq 0.54+o(1)$ without proof. No improvement on Hoffstein's bound has since appeared with a published proof. We construct a comparison kernel from a linear combination of three identities and show that Hoffstein's original parameters give $h(K) 0$ and $n_K$ large enough.

papers.title: Finite Root Sums in Symmetrizable Kac-Moody Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra with root system $\Phi$. A subset $S\subseteq\Phi$ is closed if $\alpha,\beta\in S$ and $\alpha+\beta\in\Phi$ imply $\alpha+\beta\in S$. For finite and affine Kac-Moody algebras, this closure property is known to extend from pairs to arbitrary finite sums that are roots. We prove that every closed subset of the root system of any symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra is closed under arbitrary finite sums that are roots. The proof uses real-root strings, a simultaneous separation lemma for positive imaginary roots, and a lemma on when the sum of two positive imaginary roots is again a root. As an application, we extend a necessary condition for wideness of regular subalgebras from finite and affine types to all symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebras: the symmetric closure of the roots associated to a wide regular subalgebra is the entire root system.

papers.title: Resource Allocation with Midterm Review
papers.abstract: A principal funds an agent's project over two periods, with a midterm review providing a public signal about project quality. The agent privately knows the project's quality and always prefers more funding, while the principal wants to match funding to quality. We show that the optimal mechanism frontloads the review's information value: the principal's expected payoff is strictly higher in the first period than in the second, even though she is better informed after the review. In the optimal mechanism, higher-quality projects receive more funding initially but face larger cuts after a bad review, leaving them with less funding than lower-quality projects. A good review increases funding, but the resulting allocation does not preserve the initial ranking of projects and, under a mild condition, declines with quality near the top.

papers.title: Discontinuous actions of rational special linear groups on manifolds
papers.abstract: For every $n\geq 1$, we construct continuum-many pairwise non-conjugate actions of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{Q})$ by homeomorphisms on the $n$-sphere. None of these actions extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{R})$. Our construction refines a blow-up procedure of Bowden and Mann, allowing the stabiliser action inside each blown-up disc to be prescribed. We motivate studying these actions and record some related observations.

papers.title: A Multi-View Low-Latency Direction-Sensing for Low-Altitude Network via a Multi-Armed Array
papers.abstract: Due to the directional antenna pattern, the received signal power decreases when the target deviates from the array boresight, degrading direction-sensing accuracy. Although rotatable arrays can alleviate this problem, repeated array rotations will induce an incremental long sensing latency. To break the dilemma of harvesting the directive gain from element and making a low-latency sensing, a multi-armed array comprising multiple subarrays with different orientations is proposed to provide wide spatial coverage encompassing low-altitude and terrestrial regions while enabling multi-view direction sensing. However, the different views lead to different direction-sensing accuracies. To fully exploit the complementary information from multiple views, two fusion methods, called SNR-weighted fusion and logistic-weighted fusion, are developed. The former directly assigns fusion weights according to the estimated received SNRs, whereas the latter employs an exponential SNR mapping to further emphasize high-SNR subarrays. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is derived to provide a theoretical benchmark for the proposed multi-view direction-sensing system. Simulation results show that logistic-weighted fusion achieves better accuracy in the very low-SNR regime, while both proposed methods approach the CRLB at medium and high SNRs and maintain stable sensing performance.

papers.title: Selection of Marginally Stable Patterns by Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: We study the effect of boundary conditions on the selection of wavenumbers in pattern-forming systems. Prior work established that, for a large class of boundary conditions, equilibria only within a narrow band of wavenumbers are compatible with the boundary. We demonstrate here that for a large class of initial conditions, solutions evolve towards an extremal member of this narrow band of equilibria. In fact, this extremal member is linearly stable, nonlinearly unstable, and the convergence is realized through a series of snapping events at the boundary. We observe this behavior in simulations of the Swift-Hohenberg equation when the pattern forming region is confined to a large spatial interval through a parameter quench. We prove the convergence in a phase-diffusion approximation using comparison principles and astutely chosen subsolutions that mimic the snapping behavior.

papers.title: On Waring-Goldbach problem for two squares and higher powers
papers.abstract:
Let $
u_1(n)$ and $
u_2(n)$, respectively, denote the number of representations of the natural number $n$ as the following form  egin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^4+p_4^4+p_5^4+p_6^5+p_7^8, \end{equation*} and  egin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^3+p_4^4+p_5^5+p_6^6+p_7^8, \end{equation*} where $p_1,\dots,p_7$ are primes in both above cases. In this paper, it is proved that $
u_1(n)\gg n^{43/40}(\log n)^{-7}$ holds for every sufficiently large integer $n$ subject to $n\equiv1\pmod2$ and $n\equiv\pm1\pmod3$. Moreover, we also establish that $
u_2(n)\gg n^{43/40}(\log n)^{-7}$ holds for every sufficiently large integer $n$ subject to $n\equiv1\pmod2$. These results improve and enhance the earlier work of Andrade [1] and Wang-Tian [17], respectively.

papers.title: Comparing randomized trials: a formal approach
papers.abstract: Disagreements between randomized trials that address the same causal question pose challenges for the interpretation and synthesis of evidence. We sketch a causal framework for comparing the results of randomized trials that explicitly accommodates the possibility of trial engagement effects. Using counterfactual outcomes defined under joint interventions on treatment assignment and trial-related actions, we compare trial-native treatment effects with the effects transported from one trial to the population of another in a common target population. We show that standard conditions for transporting treatment effects across trial populations are not sufficient to guarantee agreement between transported and trial-native effects. Agreement additionally requires conditions governing how trial-related actions affect outcome across studies - for example, absence of trial engagement effects, equivalence of such effects across trials, or lack of interaction between trial engagement and treatment assignment. Our framework clarifies potential sources of disagreement across trials and extends existing approaches to study comparison to settings in which trial engagement effects may be present.

papers.title: Oscillatory Integral Operators Along the Paraboloid and Applications
papers.abstract: We prove decay estimates for oscillatory integral operators along $(y_1, y_2, y_1^2+y_2^2)$ in the finite field and the continuous settings. In the continuous setting, our result allows a bi-parameter maximal modulation, which extends the one-parameter version previously established by Pierce and Yung. Our approach is different from theirs. Then we discuss three applications of our estimates: a power saving bound for certain pattern finding problem in finite fields, a short approach to $L^p$ boundedness of an one-parameter Pierce--Yung operator, and $L^p$ boundedness of a bi-parameter Pierce--Yung operator.

papers.title: The price of a weak shadow variable: inference under nonignorable missingness as relevance vanishes
papers.abstract: When an outcome is missing not at random, identification is commonly restored by a shadow variable: a covariate that predicts the outcome but is excluded from the response mechanism. The literature treats the first requirement, relevance, as a yes-or-no condition. We make it continuous, parametrizing it by a scalar that scales the shadow variable's entire contribution to the moment conditions, and ask what inference costs as that scalar vanishes. One functional of the inverse weight governs the answer. We characterize it exactly, show that it fixes the effective sample size, and use it to sharpen the rates of the estimator that avoids the weight. The characterization is concrete. Whether the functional saturates or diverges turns not on boundedness of the outcome but on whether the tilting variable has an atom at its essential supremum: a binary outcome saturates, a uniform one does not. It also bounds how far a scanned set reaches, and that reach grows only as the square root of the logarithm of the sample size, so a thousandfold increase buys one unit of tilt while the set to be scanned widens. A reanalyzed credit-scoring study shows the cost: a characteristic an optimizing selector uses cannot satisfy exclusion.

papers.title: Post-Newtonian Secular Dynamics of Hierarchical Triple Systems: A Consistent Canonical Treatment of Cross Terms
papers.abstract: We derive the secular Hamiltonian for hierarchical triple systems from the Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) three-body Hamiltonian through first post-Newtonian (1PN) order, using Lie--Hori--Deprit canonical perturbation theory and time averaging over the inner and outer orbits. The canonical framework systematically incorporates higher-order cross terms through scalar generating functions and Poisson brackets while preserving the Hamiltonian structure. We recover the electric and magnetic 1PN--quadrupole terms of Kuntz, Serra, and Trincherini (KST), rather than those reported by Lim and Rodriguez (LR). We further derive the next-to-leading-order 1PN--quadrupole term, the Newtonian quadrupole-squared Hamiltonian, and a third-order coupling between inner 1PN precession and the squared quadrupole. The outer-pericenter dependence of the quadrupole-squared Hamiltonian is removable by a canonical redefinition of the mean elements. Direct integrations of the Einstein--Infeld--Hoffmann (EIH) equations confirm the de Sitter term, the direct electric term, and the binding-energy renormalization of the inner-binary mass. For the systems considered by LR, the canonical terms do not reproduce the extreme merger acceleration they reported. Instead, the relativistic modulation of the eccentricity cycles is driven primarily by the outer-pericenter-dependent part of the next-to-leading-order 1PN--quadrupole term.

papers.title: Compact Quasi-Metric Spaces Are Expand-Contract Plastic
papers.abstract: On a totally bounded metric space, every non-contractive self-map is an isometry. For quasi-metric spaces this fails. Here quasi-metrics are $T_1$: $d(x,y)=0$ implies $x=y$. Zavarzina gave a hereditarily precompact counterexample and asked whether rigidity holds at least for bijections. The author's toll spiral (arXiv:2610.13973) shows that it does not. We prove that compactness restores it: every compact quasi-metric space is expand-contract plastic, that is, each of its bijective non-contractive self-maps is an isometry. Countable compactness suffices, as does compactness of the conjugate topology. Bijectivity is needed, even on a compact, hereditarily precompact space. For arbitrary non-contractive self-maps, we prove rigidity when the space is hereditarily precompact and its conjugate topology is sequentially compact, in particular when it is also Yoneda complete; neither hypothesis can be dropped. Such maps are then surjective. In both theorems the $T_1$ axiom can be weakened to $R_0$, $d(x,y)=0$ implies $d(y,x)=0$, if hereditary precompactness is taken to mean that every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence; surjectivity then holds up to points at distance 0 both ways. The weaker $T_0$ axiom is not enough: there is a $T_0$ space, compact in both topologies and satisfying all the other hypotheses of both theorems, with a bijective non-contractive non-isometry. Finally, for an asymmetric norm in finite dimension, the classical theorem makes the symmetric unit ball and sphere rigid for all non-contractive self-maps, and the forward ones if the norm is $T_1$. In infinite dimension, the symmetric ball and sphere need not be plastic, and for the forward ones we pose the quasi-metric form of the unit-ball question of Cascales, Kadets, Orihuela and Wingler. The two theorems and the counterexamples of Section 6 are machine-checked in Lean, except the steps listed at the end.

papers.title: Symmetric, rational and infinitely many $(23_4)$ configurations, and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
papers.abstract: A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Gr\"unbaum in 2000, and successive work of Bokowski, Gr\"unbaum, Schewe, Pilaud and Cuntz settled every case but $n=23$. We settle this last case by bounding the symmetry of such configurations and classifying the most symmetric ones exactly. We prove that for every prime $n\equiv3\pmod4$ the group of projective symmetries of a geometric $(n_4)$ configuration has order at most four, explaining why symmetric constructions failed at $n=23$, and the same argument bounds the symmetry of $(n_5)$ configurations for primes $n\not\equiv1\pmod5$. Reducing the Klein four-group case to 4021 bilinear polynomial systems and solving all of them exactly with Gr\"obner bases, we show that exactly two $(23_4)$ configurations reach this bound up to projective equivalence and that there are no others even over $\mathbb{C}$. Both are self-polar; the first has integer coordinates and the second is defined over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{17})$ but not over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consequently geometric $(n_4)$ configurations exist if and only if $n\ge18$ and $n\ne19$. The same classification recovers Cuntz's $(22_4)$ and $(26_4)$ configurations and finds three new combinatorial types at $n=22$ and $94$ at $n=26$. Among self-polar $(23_4)$ configurations with a single involution we find $50$ more, defined over number fields of degree at most $7$. Four of them deform in one-parameter families, and computing three of these exactly, one birational to the modular curve $X_1(11)$, we prove that there are infinitely many geometric $(23_4)$ configurations, among them infinitely many with rational coordinates that are self-polar and have no projective symmetry.

papers.title: Bijective Non-Contractive Maps of Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Spaces Need Not Be Isometries
papers.abstract: Zavarzina asked whether every bijective non-contractive self-map of a precompact quasi-metric space is an isometry. We show that it need not be, even when the space is hereditarily precompact. On the integers, take the distance of an irrational rotation and add a fixed toll $c>0$ to every step from a nonnegative integer down to a smaller one. The resulting space, the toll spiral, is a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, and the shift $n\mapsto n+1$ is a bijective non-contractive map that is not an isometry. The construction works over any metric space $Y$: for every bijective isometry $\sigma$ of $Y$ and every point whose $\sigma$-orbit is aperiodic and totally bounded, adding the same toll along the orbit gives such a counterexample, for instance over the $p$-adic odometer. The conjugate of the toll spiral is not even precompact, so the hypothesis on the conjugate in Zavarzina's positive result cannot be dropped, even for bijections. The toll spiral is also not expand-contract plastic, since the inverse shift is a non-expansive bijection that is not an isometry. For an arbitrary bijective non-contractive map $F$, the distance from $F^kx$ to $F^ky$ has a limit as $k\to-\infty$; $F$ is an isometry for this limit, and the excess $D_0$ of the distance over it is the defect. On a hereditarily precompact space, we prove a monochromy theorem: if a pair $(a,b)$ has positive defect $\eta$, then there are natural numbers $t_1 \eta/4$ for every difference $\Delta=t_j-t_i$ with $i \eta/4$ for every such $\Delta$. Three boundary results delimit the remaining question; the open case, that of separated spaces compact in one of their topologies, has since been settled by the author (arXiv:2610.14301). The construction, in general and for the circle, is machine-checked in Lean 4 using Mathlib, with no unproved steps.

papers.title: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes from the spectral edge of DSSYK and supersymmetric extensions
papers.abstract: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same $q$-deformed volumes can also be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call ``irrelevant'' contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how $q$-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.

papers.title: Scattering for the KP-II equation
papers.abstract: We prove scattering in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ for real-valued solutions of the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation with localized initial data. The localization is measured in scale-invariant Lorentz or mixed Lebesgue spaces. The admissible data include all real-valued Schwartz functions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing scattering for the KP-II equation for every real-valued Schwartz initial datum, without any smallness assumption and without the zero mean condition. We also show that some localization is necessary: there are smooth real-valued initial data of arbitrarily small $L^2$ norm, with a logarithmic moment, for which the solution does not scatter in $L^2$.

papers.title: A strategy for astrometric quasar selection with Gaia DR3 and its application to discover new luminous $z>2$ quasars
papers.abstract: We aim to provide a cookbook for purely astrometric selection of quasars with Gaia DR3 and to provide an example of its use for the identification of very luminous $z>2$ quasars. We analyse the Gaia DR3 astrometry of confirmed quasars and stationary sources. We show that the proper motion signal to noise $\mu/\sigma_{\mu}$ follows a Rayleigh-like distribution. We also show the importance of properly taking into account the correlation between proper motions in right ascension and declination, as well as the non-linear error propagation. We adopt the Mahalanobis distance to the null proper-motion hypothesis. A scaled $\chi^2$ distribution with $k=2$ and scale $s=1.1485$ is fitted to Gaia-CRF3; the corresponding $\pm2\sigma$ Gaussian-equivalent threshold is $D^2_{M(\mu)} 2$ quasars without redshifts in the literature. Our proposed astrometric selection strategy recovers 95\% of known quasars. Its potential use for new discoveries is demonstrated by the identification of 24 very luminous $z>2$ quasars. Ten of these are new discoveries and for an additional seven we correct the redshifts determined by other methods.

papers.title: MLP-Initialized Reinforcement Learning for Exit Timing in SPX Short-Straddle Portfolios
papers.abstract: This paper studies exit timing for SPX short-straddle portfolios using a two-stage supervised and reinforcement-learning framework. Historical episodes first generate ex-post optimal hold/exit labels for training a multilayer perceptron (MLP) using only contemporaneously available state variables at deployment. The trained MLP then initializes reinforcement-learning actors that are fine-tuned with a risk-aware trading reward. Out-of-sample evaluation over 2024-2026 shows that the supervised MLP substantially outperforms passive holding and representative fixed-time and profit-and-loss-based exit rules. Across seven independent seeds, MLP-initialized Actor-Critic averages 37.54% cumulative return and a Sharpe ratio of 1.705, compared with 35.01% and 1.651 for the supervised MLP. Actor-Critic trained from scratch averages only 0.18% return. These findings show that oracle-guided supervised learning provides a stable foundation for reward-based policy fine-tuning in a sparse and path-dependent option-exit problem.

papers.title: Maximal Linear Arrangement is NP complete on Bipartite Graphs
papers.abstract: The linear arrangement of a simple graph $G = (V,E)$ is a bijective labeling $\pi$ of the vertices of $G$ to the set $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. The maximum linear arrangement ($\texttt{maxLA}$) problem is to determine whether $G$ has a labeling such that the sum of labels across $G$'s edges, $\sum_{uv \in E} |\pi(u) - \pi(v)|$, is at least a given value $k$. Minimum linear arrangement ($\texttt{minLA}$) is defined analogously. Both $\texttt{maxLA}$ and $\texttt{minLA}$ are known to be NP complete for general graphs. $\texttt{minLA}$ has shown to be NP complete for bipartite graphs by Evans and Shiloah in 1975. It has been an open problem whether the same holds for $\texttt{maxLA}$. In this paper we prove that $\texttt{maxLA}$ is NP complete for bipartite graphs.

papers.title: Properness of the Cuspidal Hilbert Eigenvariety
papers.abstract: We prove that for any prime $p$ and tame level $N\geq4$, the weight map from the cuspidal Hilbert eigenvariety constructed by Andreatta--Iovita--Pilloni for a totally real field $F$ to the weight space is proper in the sense of Buzzard--Calegari, under a non-vanishing hypothesis on certain Sen polynomials of Galois representations at the primes above $p$. In particular, this yields the properness of the eigenvariety away from non-positive integral Sen weights. Our approach extends the $p$-adic Hodge-theoretic argument of Diao--Liu. When $p$ has a unique prime of $F$ above it, we remove this hypothesis and obtain unconditional properness, by establishing base-change compatibility for spaces of overconvergent Hilbert modular forms and analyzing the associated spectral variety over certain closed subspaces of the weight space.

papers.title: Cosmic topology. Part IId. Eigenmodes and correlation matrices of lens spaces
papers.abstract: The global topology of the Universe is a longstanding open question. In this work, we examine the statistical signatures of a positively curved universe with a Friedmann--Lemaitre--Robertson--Walker metric and the topology of a lens space $L(p,q)$. Since these manifolds are generally statistically anisotropic and inhomogeneous, their cosmic microwave background (CMB) covariance matrices contain non-zero off-diagonal entries that depend on observer location. We compute these full harmonic-space covariance matrices for scalar perturbations for arbitrary lens spaces and observer position. Using the Kullback--Leibler divergence, we assess the distinguishability of these spaces from a simply connected three-sphere with the same curvature. The results show that topological signatures can still be significant in a cosmic-variance-limited regime even when the length, $d_{\rm NC}$, of the shortest loop around the Universe through the observer exceeds the diameter, $d_{\rm LSS}$, of the last-scattering surface by up to $10\%$. This distinguishability depends on the curvature, the lens space and the observer position mainly through the ratio $d_{\rm NC}/d_{\rm LSS}$, which is set not only by the curvature radius but also by $p$, $q$ and the observer location. Therefore, for any value of the spatial curvature, however small, there are lens spaces and observer positions for which $0.985\,d_{\rm LSS}<d_{\rm NC}<1.1\,d_{\rm LSS}$. Such observers would find no matched circles in the CMB large enough to have been detected to date, yet the topology would remain potentially discoverable through its statistical signatures.

papers.title: Information Divergence and Endogenous Evolution of Asymmetric Information
papers.abstract: Standard theories trace information asymmetry to privately held information, heterogeneous signals, or costly information acquisition. We identify a distinct mechanism: otherwise identical rational agents observing a common Markov state at asynchronous times can hold different predictive distributions because their information differs in age. When the transition kernel separates information ages, independent Bernoulli observation arrivals make such divergence recur infinitely often almost surely, even with identical arrival probabilities. When agents instead choose costly updating intensities, independent update realizations can regenerate heterogeneous information ages among ex ante identical agents. In a stationary Gaussian AR(1) environment, the consequences depend on common staleness as well as the age gap: holding the gap fixed, older information raises individual uncertainty while reducing expected squared forecast disagreement and the value of certifying relative freshness. This generates stale consensus: low disagreement despite high uncertainty. With multiple ordered ages, costly certification supports partial-unraveling equilibria in which fresher types certify and sufficiently stale types pool. Under geometric information ages, more frequent updating weakly lowers the smallest and largest equilibrium disclosure cutoffs wherever positive-certification equilibria exist. The framework has implications for credit, insurance, financial markets, and multi-agent AI.
authors: Ratna K. Shrestha (University of British Columbia)

papers.title: BayesJudge: Uncertainty-Aware Bayesian Meta-Evaluation of Human and LLM Judgments
papers.abstract: AI evaluation pipelines often produce conflicting judgments rather than clean labels. Yet existing methods largely collapse disagreement into a single hard label. As a result, item ambiguity, rater biases, and the position preferences of LLM judges are erased together: evaluation outcomes appear deterministic while concealing the underlying uncertainty, and may even systematically favor one response. This conflict is especially acute in pairwise LLM evaluation. We propose \textbf{BayesJudge}, an online Bayesian meta-evaluation layer for conflicting human-LLM judgment streams. BayesJudge treats the latent preference of each item as a latent variable and jointly models two sources of evaluator bias: rater-specific confusion matrices for human annotation bias, and an explicit order parameter for the position preference of LLM judges, thereby separating response quality from evaluator bias. We derive an exact online posterior recursion and adopt a scalable Rao-Blackwellized assumed-density sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) approximation for streaming inference. Consequently, each comparison yields not a single hard label but a posterior distribution over each response winning (as well as a tie or ambiguity state), together with posterior estimates of the bias parameters, making evaluation uncertainty explicit and quantifiable. On synthetic data, BayesJudge accurately recovers human annotation biases and LLM position biases online, and strictly outperforms variants that freeze either bias channel in held-out predictive log-likelihood. On the real-world SummEval dataset, BayesJudge detects systematic order effects in LLM judgments, distinguishes the behavioral signatures of experts and crowdworkers without rater metadata, and yields posterior uncertainty that reflects genuine human disagreement. Our code is available at https://github.com/Killerofthecard/BayesJudge.git

papers.title: $L_p$-spaces, $1\leq p\ne 2<\infty$, associated with type III and semifinite von Neumann algebras are not isomorphic
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a type III von Neumann algebra, and let $N$ be a semifinite von Neumann algebra. We prove that the Banach space $M_*$ does not embed isomorphically into the Banach space $N_*$. More generally, we prove that $L_p(M)$ is not isomorphic to a subspace of $L_p(N)$ for $1\le p<2$. In particular, the Banach isomorphism class of $L_p(M)$ distinguishes type III algebras from semifinite algebras for $1\le p<\infty$, $p\ne2$. This answers several long-standing open questions in the literature.

papers.title: Inter-Categorical Subobject Analysis
papers.abstract: We introduce a systematic way to use the subobject functor on any category to set up a framework for generalized topological and measure-theoretic notions and inferences. Concretely, we develop two connected calculi: 1. a fourfold calculus derived from notions of smallness and density that generalizes, among other things, topological density and measure-theoretic negligibility, 2. a twofold calculus that generalizes topological and measure-theoretic inference procedures. The resulting theory is distinguished in that it is inter-categorical in character: its definitions can be applied not just to describe smallness and density of subobjects in any category and classify morphisms by how they handle them, but also functors and natural transformations by how they transform them, somewhat like the theory of limits but with a simple and intuitive conceptual meaning that applies to each incarnation. We provide examples of these notions from many areas of mathematics and outline their unfolding throughout category theory as we add assumptions that bring them closer to classical settings, which we complete by generalizing the topological duality of open and closed subsets and outlining a possible framework for a categorical measure theory. Central to this interaction is the subobject 2-functor and the 2-category of upward-bounded preorders, so in the last part of the text we provide a study of their function. Concretely we derive representation theorems for this 2-functor and 2-category and a conjecture about how to generalize these theorems to n-categories.

papers.title: The optimal information complexity of VC learning
papers.abstract: Steinke and Zakynthinou(2020) introduces the Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) framework of analyzing the information complexity of learning algorithms based on algorithm-dependent information-theoretic quantities. We study one of these quantities, the evaluated Conditional Mutual Information (eCMI). It has been an interesting question whether the optimal PAC guarantee for VC classes can be recovered from the algorithm-dependent analyses via CMI. And we show that it is possible to recover this guarantee by constructing a learning algorithm whose eCMI is of order O(d) in the realizable case, where d is the VC-dimension of the concept class. Specially, our algorithm is a randomized Majority-of-5 base learners with optimal in-expectation generalization guarantee.

papers.title: Taxonomic Classification with Tag Arrays
papers.abstract: We present a tool, KATKA, for taxonomic classification with tag arrays. Compared to Ahmed et al.'s state-of-the-art tool Cliffy ({\it Genome Research}, 2025) on the SILVA dataset from their paper and a readset similar to one of theirs, KATKA is faster, more accurate, much smaller and drastically easier to build.

papers.title: Nonlinear lower-tail large deviations at criticality
papers.abstract: We introduce general methods to derive lower tail large deviation principles, for a variety of nonlinear problems of combinatorial interest. These methods are especially effective in "critical" regimes, where the nonlinearities are not sparse enough for Poissonian lower tails (e.g., Janson's inequality does not provide a sharp tail bound), but the situation is not so dense that combinatorial effects dominate (e.g., we cannot directly apply the theory of hypergraph containers or the relative entropy framework of Kozma-Samotij). In particular, these are regimes where one expects interesting phase transitions to occur. Our results have a number of consequences related to subgraphs in random graphs, answering various questions of Warnke and Jenssen-Perkins-Potukuchi-Simkin. For example, consider a random graph $G\sim \mathbb G(n,p)$, and let $L_\triangle(n,p)=\log\Pr[G\text{ is triangle-free}]$. The first-order asymptotics of $L_\triangle(n,p)$ have long been known in all parameter ranges except the critical regime where $p$ has order of magnitude $1/\sqrt n$. We are able to fill this gap: for any fixed $c>0$, we show that $n^{-3/2}L_\triangle(n,c/\sqrt n)$ converges to a limit expressed in terms of a two-parameter variational problem, which has a single phase transition at $c\approx 4.341$. In contrast, we show that there is no such phase transition for the probability that $G$ is $C_{2\ell}$-free, for any fixed even cycle $C_{2\ell}$. We also obtain some applications in combinatorial design theory.
