Addressing conjectures of Glock-K\"uhn-Lo-Osthus, Kelly, and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney-Simkin, we obtain new estimates on the number of order-$n$ Steiner triple systems with no Pasch configuration and the number of order-$n$ Latin squares with no $2\times 2$ Latin subsquare (both tight up to a factor of $\exp(o(n^2))$).

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of the 2D Boussinesq equations around Couette flow in infinite channel
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the stability threshold of the two-dimensional Boussinesq system around the Couette flow in an infinite channel $\mathbb{R}\times[-1,1]$ under Navier-slip boundary condition. To address nonlinear echo chains induced by temperature-vorticity coupling, we construct a two-level frequency-dependent temporal decomposition, with the two levels matched to the infinite and finite superposition principles for the equation, respectively. By fully exploiting the enhanced dissipation effect at each decomposition level, we prove that if the initial perturbation $(\omega^{in}, \theta^{in})$ around the Couette flow satisfies $\|\omega^{in}\|_{H^4_{x,y}\cap L^1_xH^4_y}\leq c\nu^{\frac{1}{3}}$, and $\|\theta^{in}\|_{H^5_{x,y}\cap L^1_xH^5_y}\leq c\nu^{\frac{2}{3}+}$, the Boussinesq system admits a globally asymptotically stable solution. It should be emphasized that the method in this paper provides an effective approach for the hydrodynamic equations with coupling effects.

papers.title: Singlet sector of the vector model with angular potential
papers.abstract: We study the singlet sector of large-$N$, $O(N)$ vector model on $S^1_\beta\times S^2_r$ in presence of an angular potential $\Omega$. We compute the free energy of the model both at the free fixed point as well as the non-trivial fixed point. The model undergoes a phase transition when the temperature $T$ and angular potential attain the relation $T^2r^2\sim N (1-\omega^2)$, where $\omega=r\Omega$ and $r$ is the radius of $S^2$, with $Tr\gg1$, at both the fixed points, with different numerical coefficients. The transition was studied earlier at zero angular potential at $Tr\sim \sqrt{N}$. The holonomy eigenvalue distribution, having support on the full circle below the transition, develops a gap above it, called the Gross-Witten-Wadia transition. The angular potential introduces an additional parameter to such a transition, tuning it, the transition can occur even at a fixed temperature. We show that for the free model transition can occur as $1-\omega^2\sim 1/N$ while $Tr\sim O(1)$. For the interacting model the computation is performed at a limit $Tr\gg1$, thus we show the same at a large but fixed temperature which does not scale as $\sqrt{N}$. In the ungapped phase, the free energy exhibits a double pole near $\omega^2=1$ for both the fixed points. This is possibly due to the fact that the theory projected onto the singlets is non-local and therefore need not obey the leading simple pole scaling of a local thermal effective action.

papers.title: The consistency strength of the failure of amenable C-sequences
papers.abstract: We determine the consistency strength of the existence of a regular uncountable cardinal carrying no amenable $C$-sequence. It is equiconsistent with the existence of an inaccessible cardinal $\kappa$ which is $\Pi^1_\xi$-indescribable for every $\xi<\kappa^+$ in the transfinite second-order hierarchy of indescribability. For the lower bound, we prove that the failure of amenability at $\kappa$ implies that $L$ contains such a cardinal at or below $\kappa$, using constructible guessing sequences, correct constructible levels, and a transfinite induction. For the upper bound, we prepare the cardinal so that every proper initial segment of a full Hechler iteration of length $\kappa^+$ preserves weak compactness. Each final $C$-sequence appears at a bounded stage and is captured at the next stage on a stationary set; the remaining closed iteration preserves that capture.

papers.title: Relative isoperimetry in the three-dimensional cube: classification and quantitative stability
papers.abstract: We compute the relative isoperimetric profile of the three-dimensional unit cube. Up to cube isometries and complementation, its minimizers are corner eighth-balls, edge quarter-cylinders and coordinate slabs, with both adjacent families minimizing at $4\pi/81$ and $1/\pi$. At each fixed volume the perimeter deficit bounds the squared $L^1$ distance to the minimizing family, with optimal exponent two. Near each transition the deficit controls the minimum, over the two adjacent families, of squared distance plus excess perimeter. The best constant for distance to the minimizing family decays linearly as the volume approaches a transition. We also obtain the conjectured profile for $(0,\beta)\times(0,1)^2$, $0<\beta\le1$, and resolve the three-dimensional case of Brezis's Open Problem~10.1.

papers.title: Organizational Lifespan as Commitment: The Case of Foundations
papers.abstract: An organization's lifespan may commit future decision makers to continue, terminate, or retain discretion. We identify when each rule has value for philanthropic foundations. If the same aligned actor chooses investment and subsequent survival, discretion weakly dominates fixed rules; a commonly used investment comparison fails because it omits the option to invest enough to make continuation desirable in adverse states. With noncontractible organizational investment delegated to an earlier actor, however, perpetuity may improve incentives despite inefficient continuation in some states. The result survives an observable-investment extension. A finite terminal date is valuable under governance-induced overcontinuation, and its optimum reflects both direct operating benefits and investment incentives. We establish nonempty environments favoring each regime and distinguish institutional lifespan from payout policy, requirements to preserve the foundation's endowment capital, and the duration of grant commitments.

papers.title: GPU-accelerated Regularized Vector Multiplicative Error Models for Positive-valued Financial Time Series
papers.abstract: The logarithmic vector multiplicative error model (log-vMEM) provides a methodology for modeling and forecasting multivariate positive-valued time series. However, the number of autoregressive parameters increases rapidly with the system dimension and lag order, posing challenges for estimation and model selection. This paper develops a regularized estimation framework for the log-vMEM with multivariate Gamma errors by incorporating hierarchical lag structures to induce sparsity and accommodate heterogeneous lag dynamics. We consider three hierarchical lag structures: componentwise, own-other, and elementwise, in combination with group lasso, adaptive group lasso, group MCP, and group SCAD penalties. Parameter estimation is carried out through an alternating block-coordinate optimization algorithm with sequential Gauss-Seidel updates, while GPU-accelerated numerical quadrature is employed to address the computational burden of evaluating the multivariate Gamma likelihood. Simulation experiments investigate parameter recovery and lag selection under different sparsity structures. The real data analysis is carried out on the realized volatility measures for Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) which allows a comparison of the competing regularization approaches in an empirical financial setting. Together, these developments provide a computational framework for sparse multivariate volatility modeling with flexible lag structures and dependent Gamma errors.

papers.title: Pauli Decomposition by Character Theory: A Memory-Bounded Algorithm for Qubits and Qudits
papers.abstract: Pauli decomposition of an $n$-qubit operator is expensive if each of the $4^n$ Pauli strings is treated as an unstructured object. Labeling those strings by the configuration space $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ makes them displacement operators $X^{\otimes x}Z^{\otimes z}$ on the computational space: shifts by~$x$ and multiplications by characters $Z^{\otimes z}$ in the computational basis. That labeling organizes the operator into $2^n$ fibers of length $2^n$, one per shift~$x$, each collecting the computational-basis amplitudes that hop by~$x$. Expanding each fiber function in the character basis of $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ --- a length-$2^n$ Walsh--Hadamard transform --- recovers the Pauli coefficients at total cost $O(n\cdot4^n)$. The same fiber / shift--character picture extends to $(\mathbb{Z}_p)^n$ (Heisenberg--Weyl qudits). \texttt{paulikit} is a memory-bounded realization for qubits: for matrix-sparse inputs, peak memory need not densify to a full $2^n\times2^n$ operator. Performance is checked on a stated low-end GNU/Linux platform for a coupled-oscillator sweep beyond a billion Pauli terms.

papers.title: Strong Uniqueness for Instantaneously Complete Chern-Ricci Flow
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study strong uniqueness for smooth instantaneously complete Chern-Ricci flows on noncompact complex manifolds. Under suitable reference metric and positivity assumptions, we establish strong uniqueness for initial Hermitian metrics which are K\"ahler outside a compact set. The initial metric may be incomplete, and no curvature bounds or metric equivalence assumptions are imposed on the evolving solutions. In particular, we obtain strong uniqueness from complete initial metrics in this class with bounded Chern-Ricci curvature. We also prove stationarity of flows from the Euclidean metric on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and uniqueness of the instantaneously complete flow from the Euclidean metric on the complex unit ball for all positive time. Finally, on complex surfaces, we show that a Ricci flow remaining Hermitian for a fixed complex structure is K\"ahler at all times if it is K\"ahler at one time, and derive a corresponding strong uniqueness result for Ricci flows in this class.

papers.title: A method of moving planes for a mixed local-nonlocal parabolic equation with quenching
papers.abstract: In this paper we develop a parabolic version of the method of moving planes on systems with a mixed local and nonlocal diffusion operator, that being $\mathcal{L} = -(-\Delta)^s + \Delta$, where $(-\Delta)^s$ is the integral fractional laplacian. We then use this result to study the quenching phenomena occurring in said systems with a singular absorption term of the type $(1-u)^{-p}$. We prove that there exists a range of multiplicative parameters for which every solution presents quenching, and that for any initial datum $u_0$, there exists a small enough multiplicative parameter such as the solution is globally defined. We also prove that the quenching phenomena cannot happen arbitrarily close to the boundary, but they are contained in a compact subset of the domain.

papers.title: A Dimension-Free Bound on the Poincar\'e Constant of Isotropic Log-Concave Measures
papers.abstract: The Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits (KLS) conjecture asserts that isotropic log-concave probability measures have Poincar\'e constants bounded by a universal constant, independently of dimension. In this work, we provide a deterministic variational proof that the Poincar\'e constant $C_P(\mu)\le25$, where $\mu$ is any isotropic log-concave probability measure. The proof centers on mean-zero integration of compatible symmetric tensor fields. Starting from constant tensors, we obtain factorially normalized Appell polynomials by iterating this procedure. Using moment estimates and a quadratic variance inequality, we establish geometric bounds on these iterated primitives through a \emph{joint} variational argument over the measure and test function. At a maximizing pair, stationarity in the test function controls the weighted sum of the two highest-order cumulant terms arising from the measure variation. To extend these bounds to arbitrary compatible fields, we use a weighted Helmholtz--Hodge decomposition of weighted divergence, the formal adjoint of differentiation. Controlling the curl in the decomposition yields a curvature comparison for the integration operators, uniformly in tensor order. Combining this comparison with the Appell bounds gives a bound on the full integration operator and hence the stated Poincar\'e inequality. The estimate is independent of the auxiliary positive curvature, allowing approximation to general isotropic log-concave measures.

papers.title: Bayesian Optimization on Function Spaces via Sparse RKHS Manifolds
papers.abstract: Bayesian Optimization (BO) has become an established methodology for minimizing black-box functions of a vector input. Often, however, this parameter vector arises from the discretization of an inherently functional relationship. Several recent articles have considered the Functional Bayesian Optimization (FBO) setting, in which the variable to be optimized is not a member of a finite dimensional vector space, but rather an infinite dimensional function space. In this work, we propose $L^0$ Manifold Optimization (L0MO), a simple approach to FBO which searches the subset of a Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS) consisting of functions with a sparse representation in the kernel functions, optimizing both the kernel locations and their coefficients. We discuss in detail the relationship between our method and existing ones, providing a unifying lens through which to view prior works. To assess our method against the state of the art, we conduct an extensive computational study, and along the way develop a novel set of benchmark test functions which port standard finite-dimensional ones to the infinite dimensional domain. Our experiments demonstrate that, on balance, the proposed method achieves superior performance across a wide range of test benchmarks.

papers.title: Testing bosonic and fermionic Gaussian states with a constant number of copies
papers.abstract: Bosonic and fermionic Gaussian quantum states play a central role in quantum physics and quantum information processing. We study the problem of testing whether a given pure state is Gaussian or is bounded away from the set of pure Gaussian states. Earlier work left open whether a fixed number of copies could suffice even as the number of modes (system size) grows. We show that it does: the number of copies needed depends only on the desired accuracy and confidence. Our tests exploit the symmetries of identical copies of Gaussian states; their analysis combines a gradient flow argument with a spectral gap studied previously for the Kac random walk on the sphere.

papers.title: Staircase phase transitions for the extreme eigenvalues of heavy-tailed sample correlation matrices
papers.abstract: We establish phase transitions in the first-order asymptotics of the largest and smallest nonzero eigenvalues of high-dimensional sample correlation matrices formed from data with i.i.d. centered real entries of finite variance, allowing an infinite fourth moment. Because of self-normalization, spectral outliers are driven by collisions of large entries in distinct rows of a common column rather than by individual large entries. The resulting phase transitions depend jointly on the aspect ratio and the entry tail, producing staircase boundaries in the phase diagram. We prove convergence to the corresponding Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur edges in subcritical regimes and to deterministic outlier levels in supercritical regimes. In critical regimes, Poisson limits for the point processes of spectral outliers and nondegenerate limiting laws for the extreme eigenvalues are established.

papers.title: First-order plants are globally asymptotically stable under antithetic feedback
papers.abstract: We show that first-order linear plants are globally asymptotically stable under antithetic feedback. This is shown by constructing an explicit smooth, convex Lyapunov function and by appealing to a Krasovskii-LaSalle invariance principle.

papers.title: Irreducibility of Verma modules for symmetrizable Kac-Moody superalgebras
papers.abstract: We establish a criterion for the irreducibility of Verma modules over symmetrizable Kac--Moody superalgebras. Our main tool is the Weyl-Kac denominator identity.

papers.title: Price-Optimized EV and Heat-Pump Scheduling Can Exceed Uncoordinated Feeder Peaks
papers.abstract: Electric vehicles and heat pumps add large, time-flexible loads to low-voltage feeders. When each household independently minimizes its own charging cost against the same electricity price, this flexible demand piles into the cheapest hours, and the resulting synchronization can stress the feeder more than uncoordinated operation does. This work quantifies that effect on a rural low-voltage feeder with photovoltaics (97 buses, 250 kVA transformer) in 913 simulation runs that compare seven strategies across four seasons, device penetrations of up to 90 %, 208 price weeks from 2022-2025, and heterogeneous heat pumps. At 30 % penetration of each device, this decentralized cost minimization drives the transformer to 253 % of rated capacity, more than three times the peak of non-optimized Fixed-random charging with the same mobility and charged energy, and 478 % with electric vehicles alone at 90 % penetration, with undervoltage at the far end of the longest feeder arm. It exceeds Fixed-random and Fixed-times charging in every winter, spring, and autumn price week, and each 30 pp of heat-pump penetration raises its peak by about 110 pp, twelve times as much as without optimization. Centralized peak minimization removes all demand-driven violations. In the heat-pump-free summer case at 60 % photovoltaics, midday reverse power flow sets a transformer floor of 128.9 % that no strategy undercuts, since no commuting electric vehicle is at home at the export peak. With a time-variable grid fee added to the spot price, the weekly peak of decentralized cost minimization falls into the reduced-fee window in 99 of the 104 fee-active price weeks, compared with 53 without the fee, while keeping at least 89.8 % of its height, so the fee relocates rather than removes the synchronization. The simulation and optimization code is available at https://github.com/lukas-wagner/SynchronizationEffectsAnalysis.

papers.title: Sub-Voxel Displacement and Ipsilateral Territory Decoupling for 3D Bilateral Coronary Artery Tree Reconstruction in Cardiac CT Angiography
papers.abstract: Reconstructing topologically complete, sub-voxel-accurate 3D bilateral coronary artery trees from cardiac CT angiography (CCTA) requires simultaneously recovering continuous centerline trajectories and separating dense left/right coronary territories without cross-ostial collisions. We present a five-stage tubular drift and ipsilateral territory decoupling framework (M1-M5). Stage M1 pairs a 398,843-parameter multi-scale 3D pyramid encoder with a four-head tubular field network predicting vesselness probability, signed tubular boundary distance, unit tangent vectors, and continuous 3D centripetal displacement vectors. Stage M2 introduces recall-preserving multi-task optimization with 7-group AdamW parameter decoupling, L2-SP backbone regularization, and per-step anchor shrinkage. Stage M3 calibrates cylindrical Valsalva-sinotubular-junction wall coordinates and native-resolution orifice contact expectations for robust left and right ostial rooting. Stage M4 constructs a scalar-potential-weighted minimum-cost arborescence followed by normal-plane cross-sectional pullback and centripetal trajectory pruning. Stage M5 enforces coverage-guarded ipsilateral-field-coupled bilateral collision reduction and subtree handover. Across a 14-case held-out development cohort (Dev-14, 17-arm forward incremental build and 9-arm leave-one-out ablation) and an independent 50-case out-of-sample evaluation cohort (OOS-50) benchmarked against seven external architectures (nnU-Net, 3D UX-Net, Swin-UNETR, MedNeXt, CS2-Net, clDice-UNet, and Point-UNet), M1-M5 reduces bilateral chamfer distance on Dev-14 from 3.4381 mm to 2.2759 mm and achieves 2.7671 mm on OOS-50 with 7.11% bilateral collision rate and 79.7% distal branch completeness.

papers.title: Path-Space Optimal Transport with Interactions: Kinetic Equations and Eikonal Structure
papers.abstract: We study a dynamical optimal transport problem on path-space with kinetic cost and nonlocal interaction. For a Gaussian interaction kernel, cyclical monotonicity and the regularity of the effective endpoint cost yield a conservative vector field associated with the initial momentum of the optimal trajectories. Separately, the Gaussian interaction potential $W_{\pi_0}$ satisfies a uniform gradient estimate and, under a quantitative condition on the interaction strength, is a classical and hence viscosity subsolution of an eikonal equation. We also derive the Euler--Lagrange dynamics directly from path-space optimality by means of endpoint-preserving perturbations of the optimal path measure. The associated phase-space marginals satisfy a measure-valued Liouville-type, or nonlocal kinetic, equation driven by the smooth Gaussian self-consistent force. Conversely, a superposition principle lifts suitable measure-valued solutions of the phase-space continuity equation to measures on phase-space trajectories. Thus path-space optimal transport provides a variational connection between endpoint geometry, eikonal behavior of the Gaussian interaction potential, and kinetic mean-field dynamics.

papers.title: Distributed Learning of $\alpha$-Potential Functions in Strategic Multi-agent Systems
papers.abstract: We study the problem of computing the tightest \(\alpha\)-potential approximation of a general-sum game over continuous action spaces, within a prescribed class of potential functions and when each player has access only to its own utility function. The difficulty is twofold: the approximation error involves a worst-case search over an infinite set of unilateral deviations, and the required utility information is distributed across players. For a linear-in-parameters potential class, we use an exact finite-tuple reformulation that separates the problem into a global outer search over deviation tuples and distributed convex inner problems. We develop a primal--dual inner oracle tailored to this structure and establish a uniform one-sided accuracy guarantee. This oracle can be combined with global outer search to obtain an end-to-end guarantee on the outer optimization error. We also develop a projected zeroth-order outer method as a computationally lighter alternative for higher-dimensional problems. Numerical experiments illustrate the accuracy--computation tradeoff between the two outer-search methods and show that the proposed optimization framework can improve upon analytical \(\alpha\)-potential constructions.

papers.title: The decay $\eta_c\to p\bar p\eta$ with meson--baryon final-state interactions
papers.abstract: We study the decay \(\eta_c\to p\bar{p}\eta\) by combining the SU(3) flavor structure of the primary production with final-state interactions in the \(p\eta\) and \(\bar{p}\eta\) subsystems, using the chiral unitary approach. The low-energy \(S_{11}\) dynamics, including the dynamically generated \(N^*(1535)\), is incorporated into the complete coupled-channel amplitude, and a phenomenological \(N^*(1895)\) contribution is included coherently. The \(p\eta\) and \(\bar{p}\eta\) invariant-mass distributions are well described, and the \(p\bar{p}\) distribution is predicted as a kinematic reflection of the \(\eta N\) dynamics. The results support the dynamical interpretation of the \(N^*(1535)\) and suggest possible additional \(S_{11}\) strength near \(1.9\)~GeV.

papers.title: Diffuse Galactic Backgrounds with SPHEREx: A Pilot Study of Background Modeling and Its Impact on Extinction
papers.abstract: We present a spectral analysis of diffuse Galactic background emission using SPHEREx data in a pilot Galactic-plane field, where uncertainty in the estimation of the diffuse infrared background is a major source of systematic uncertainty in extinction studies at near- and mid-infrared wavelengths. We construct channel-resolved background maps across the 0.75--5~$\mu$m range using a Large Median Filter approach and then carry the extinction analysis forward only for the cleaner long-wavelength subset at $\lambda \geq 3~\mu$m. In the present field, comparison against an earlier masked-median background model gives a median channel-by-channel background difference of about 6\% and a maximum change of $|\Delta\tau_{\rm norm}|\simeq 7.4$ near 3.205~$\mu$m, underscoring the importance of wavelength-dependent background modeling. These results demonstrate that spectral mapping with SPHEREx provides a practical framework for controlling diffuse background systematics and enables improved constraints on dust opacity and extinction in the Galactic plane.

papers.title: On pointwise convergence of singular integrals of Christ-Journ\'e type
papers.abstract: The primary objective of this paper is to establish the pointwise almost everywhere convergence of the singular integrals of Christ-Journ\'e type. To this end, we prove the weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for the corresponding maximal operator defined as \[ T^*[a] f(x):= \sup_{r>0}\left|\int_{|x-y| > r} K(x-y) \int_0^1 a(tx + (1-t)y)\, dt f(y)\, dy\right|, \] where $K$ is a Calder\'on--Zygmund kernel and $a\in L^\infty$. This result resolves a problem posed by Seeger (Rev. Mat. Iberoam., 2014).

papers.title: The Right Wing of the SABR Smile with an Absorbing Boundary: Resolution of Conjectures of Henry-Labord\`ere
papers.abstract:
We determine the fixed-maturity right tail of the SABR model with $ eta\in(0,1)$ absorbed at zero, for every correlation $ho$: the probability $P(k)$ that the forward ends above $f_0e^k$ satisfies $-k^{-2}\ln P(k)	o(1- eta)^2/(2
u^2T(1-(ho\wedge0)^2))$. The implied volatility therefore tends to $
u\sqrt{1-(ho\wedge0)^2}/(1- eta)$. Henry-Labord\`ere's conjectured limit $
u/(1- eta)$, which Hagan's leading-order formula also gives, holds for $ho\ge0$ and fails for $ho<0$, where survival keeps the noise orthogonal to volatility above a moving square-root barrier. The Gaussian estimate behind his second conjecture does not hold for $ho<0$; the rate is instead given by the intrinsic distance within the survival domain.

papers.title: Poincar\'e duality and module topological complexity
papers.abstract: For every simply connected space $X$ of finite rational type with Poincar\'e duality cohomology, we prove $MTC(X)=TC_0(X)=TC_0^M(X)$: module, rational and monoidal rational topological complexity coincide. Neither formality nor finiteness of the total rational homotopy is required. For every rationally retractive map $f$ between simply connected spaces of finite rational type, we prove $relcat(f_Q)\le msecat(f_Q)+1$. This bound is sharp for rationally retractive maps. Both proofs reduce to the same question: can a module nullhomotopy taking values in a split Sullivan model be chosen with values in its kernel ideal? Comparing resolutions of consecutive ideal powers achieves this after increasing the exponent by one; for diagonals, Poincar\'e duality preserves the exponent. An ideal-preserving form of Hess's construction then converts the module nullhomotopy into a compatible algebra retraction.

papers.title: No Einstein Relation, No Problem: How Relativistic Weakly Coupled Heavy Quarks Equilibrate Beyond Leading Logarithm Anyway
papers.abstract: Relativistic heavy quarks equilibrate even when their microscopic drag and momentum diffusion violate the Einstein relation. We investigate how equilibration proceeds as a function of the coupling and compared to simplified Fokker-Planck models. To do this, we present a detailed calculation of the momentum-transfer kernel in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas through strict $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$, and study the resulting dynamics at leading order in the inverse heavy-quark mass. Beyond leading logarithm, its non-Gaussian structure plays a crucial role in equilibration. We examine closely the analytic structure of the evolution kernel, determine the large-order asymptotics of the momentum-transfer cumulants, and show how the kernel's bounded analytic domain fixes asymmetric exponential tails at the level of the momentum transfer probability. Strongly coupled $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM also features an approximately Gaussian core and exponential tails, but differs in the nature of the kernel's singularities and the velocity dependence of the transport coefficients and tail exponents. These differences have distinct dynamical consequences: for the parameters studied, the persistence of the relativistic population in steeply falling spectra is largely explained by drag alone at very weak coupling, whereas fluctuation-induced survivor bias produces a large relative enhancement at strong coupling. Nevertheless, the shared qualitative structure between weak and strong coupling points the way towards a practical phenomenological description of heavy quarks anchored in first-principles field theory.

papers.title: Strict non-tightness of the level-3 quantum bootstrap for a coupled three-dimensional double well, at an excited eigenstate
papers.abstract: For the coupled three-dimensional double well $H=\tfrac12|p|^2+2\sum_i(q_i^2-1)^2-\sum_{i<j}q_i^2q_j^2$ we exhibit, at the first excited energy level (and also at the ground state), a linear functional on polynomials of degree $\le 6$ that satisfies every constraint of the standard level-3 eigenstate bootstrap, has a strictly positive definite moment matrix, and nevertheless assigns a negative value to a nonnegative polynomial. It is therefore an interior point of the level-3 relaxation that is realized by no quantum state. The construction reflects a fact that holds at every level: the eigenstate rows never reach the top-degree momentum moments. At level 3, where strictly feasible points exist, this means that the corresponding block of the moment matrix carries no information about which energies admit one. Every algebraic ingredient is an exact rational certificate, and the only numerical ingredients (spectral enclosures of an eigenfunction) are carried out in rigorous ball arithmetic.

papers.title: Normalized ground states as sharp dynamical thresholds for the inhomogeneous NLS with an inverse-square potential
papers.abstract: We study the focusing inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with an inverse-square potential, in the mass-supercritical and energy-subcritical regime and in every dimension $N\ge3$. Two lines of research on this model have so far developed separately, namely the scattering theory below the ground state and the variational theory of solutions with prescribed mass. We connect them. We compute explicitly the minimax level $m_a(c)$ of the energy on the Pohozaev manifold of mass $c$, introduced by Hajaiej, Luo and Wang, in terms of the sharp constant of the associated Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality. We prove that the minimizers of $m_a(c)$ are exactly the optimizers of this inequality lying on the Pohozaev manifold, and that they are ground states of the stationary problem. This answers a question left open by these authors. We then show that $m_a(c)$ is a sharp dynamical threshold. Below it, the sign of the Pohozaev functional is preserved by the flow. If this sign is positive, the solution is global. If it is negative and the datum has finite variance, the solution blows up in finite time. For the three-dimensional cubic model, the global solutions also scatter, by the scattering criterion of Hajaiej, Luo and Wang read in its scale-invariant form. As consequences, we obtain the strong instability of all normalized ground states, with destabilizing data on the same mass sphere, the strict monotonicity of the threshold with respect to the coupling constant, and a positive lower bound for $m_a(c)$ which is uniform up to the critical Hardy coupling.

papers.title: On wall-crossing invariant combinations of Welschinger numbers for rational surfaces with a conic bundle
papers.abstract: We refine the real enumerative invariants insensitive to changes in the real structure introduced in our previous paper on del Pezzo surfaces, and extend these refined invariants to arbitrary rational surfaces. The construction involves a choice of an auxiliary conic bundle together with a Pin-structure. We prove that the resulting invariants are independent of these auxiliary choices and establish recursive relations for their computation.

papers.title: From Static Lindblad Stabilizability to Robust Physical Control Sequences
papers.abstract: We derive checkable convergence, error, and execution-cost bounds for repeating a supplied finite control sequence from a static Lindblad stabilization certificate and complete implementation data, including concurrent background dynamics. The static decay bound and error bounds from static to planned evolution and from the plan to execution together bound the actual cycle's contraction factor in one fixed Lyapunov metric. For target-preserving planned and actual paths and a controller returning to its initial state each cycle, a uniform contraction bound below one gives cycle-end convergence from every initial state under cycle-varying uncertainty. Uniformly bounded within-cycle amplification in that metric extends this convergence throughout physical time when cycle durations are bounded above and away from zero. With leakage, uniform error bounds relative to certified target-preserving paths give explicit long-time distance bounds. Cycle and within-cycle bounds also screen a specified finite hardware library for sequences certified to meet and maintain a prescribed tolerance. In a four-level cascade with finite pulses, calibration and timing errors, always-on dephasing, and bounded pumping, the selected sequence brings every initial state within trace distance $0.1$ of the target in one complete cycle of explicitly bounded duration and maintains that tolerance under repetition.

papers.title: Toward Controlling Biology with Language: Offline Learning of Prompt-Conditioned Interventions for Cells, Organoids, and Biobots
papers.abstract: Natural language has become an interface to code, images and molecules, but not to living matter: a stimulus applied to cells has no fixed linguistic meaning, and every paired example of an instruction and its outcome costs a wet-lab experiment. We ask how far an existing archive of experiments can take this interface, using xenobots, motile multicellular constructs made of frog cells, stimulated by a single electrical pulse of varying duration. We re-track 155 archived recordings with two independent methods, measure what the pulse does from each bot's own behaviour before and after it, and separate behaviours the pulse controls from behaviours it does not. Longer pulses stop bots and short pulses leave them moving, sometimes faster; turning direction and starting from rest do not depend on duration, and restarting at most weakly. We then replace hand-made behaviour labels with a blind language critic: fresh sessions of a multimodal language model read plots of each bot and score how well its behaviour matches each of 176 instructions. The critic agrees with the measured labels whenever its plots contain the information the labels are defined on, and dose curves learned from its scores match those learned from the measurements. A prompt-to-intervention model trained only on critic scores maps unseen instructions, including negations, to the right end of the dose range on unseen bots, as well as the same model trained on measured labels. The archive therefore supports a calibrated, refusing language interface for the three behaviours a pulse can set, and identifies, rather than hides, the behaviours it cannot.

papers.title: Arbitrary Stage Spectra for Raikov Remainders Along Quotient Towers
papers.abstract: Let $\theta$ be an ordinal and let $(N_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\theta}$ be a continuous increasing tower of closed normal subgroups of a Hausdorff topological group $G$, with $N_0=\{e\}$. Write $\rho G$ for the Raikov completion of $G$, and put $K_\alpha=\overline{N_\alpha}^{\rho G}$ and $H_\alpha=GK_\alpha$. The successive and limit differences of the groups $H_\alpha$ mark the first stages at which points of $\rho G$ become old quotient points. For every nonzero ordinal $\theta$ and every set $S\subseteq(0,\theta]$, there is a Hausdorff pseudocompact Boolean group with a continuous tower of closed normal subgroups such that every member of the tower is pseudocompact and the nonempty strata occur exactly at the stages in $S$. The terminal quotient can simultaneously be chosen isomorphic to $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, and for every $\delta<\theta$ the successive factor $N_{\delta+1}/N_\delta$ is compact exactly when $\delta+1\notin S$. Thus a tower may have a single nonempty stratum at a limit stage even when every successive factor is compact. For a closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$, let $\widehat q:\rho G\to\rho(G/N)$ extend the quotient homomorphism and put $K=\overline N^{\rho G}$. Over $gN\in G/N$, the fiber in $\rho G\setminus G$ is $g(K\setminus N)$, homeomorphic to $\rho N\setminus N$, while for $y\in\widehat q(\rho G)\setminus(G/N)$ the entire $\widehat q$-fiber lies in $\rho G\setminus G$ and is homeomorphic to $\rho N$. For precompact kernels this gives a canonical decomposition, and nested quotients give the two-stage identity underlying the transfinite filtration. Further results concern pseudocompact Raikov remainders and include countable Abelian examples.

papers.title: A No-Go Theorem for Order-Two Clifford Electric-Magnetic Duality
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic duality in the toric code has order two at the level of anyon types and acts as a Hadamard-type logical transformation on the encoded quantum information. Here, we ask whether it can likewise be realized microscopically as an order-two Clifford operation. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ toric code, we prove that any locality-preserving Clifford realization of electric-magnetic exchange cannot have order two. Our proof is fully general and requires neither translation symmetry with restricted families of system sizes nor a fixed pairing between vertex and plaquette stabilizers. Geometrically, the proof locally emulates the unavoidable crossing between electric and magnetic strings, similar to a cross-cap in a non-orientable manifold. Extending the problem to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ toric code, we find that an order-two Clifford realization exists for odd $N$, whereas it is impossible for even $N$. Our result shows that the order-two exchange of closed-string operators cannot be extended to an order-two exchange of open-string operators.

papers.title: Sequential Capacity of Quantum Processes with Finite Memory
papers.abstract: How complex can the responses of a quantum process become as it runs longer with fixed internal memory? We measure this complexity by sequential response capacity, the depth of an adaptive tree of experiments whose acceptance probabilities separate possible processes by a prescribed gap. Each experiment uses a fresh complete run, and one fixed process must realize every response along a path. For any fixed common visible dimension of at least two and internal memory cap, we prove that capacity has order $K\log((K+1)/\gamma)$ for $K$ transitions per run and probability gap $0<\gamma\leq1$. Time-dependent single-qubit phase channels without internal memory already attain the fixed-gap $K\log K$ growth, realizing each path with zero-or-one response probabilities. Under the same tester permissions, classical stochastic processes that measure in a fixed basis at every transition have only linear capacity at fixed dimensions and gap. For phase sequences selected by a classical address stored inside the process, we then quantify how known independent Pauli noise changes this logarithmic enhancement. With ideal tester controls and weak residual phase noise after correction, we prove matching capacity bounds at a fixed small gap. At fixed address size and fixed positive residual noise, the logarithmic enhancement saturates once the phase-sequence length exceeds the inverse noise scale, and capacity then grows linearly with sequence length.

papers.title: Trinity of Carrollian Gravity: Dynamically Equivalent Formulations of Magnetic Carrollian Gravity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend the paradigm of the Geometrical Trinity of Gravity to the Carrollian geometry to construct a comprehensive framework of dynamically equivalent theories for Magnetic Carrollian gravity. Utilizing the inherent ambiguities and freedoms of affine connections on degenerate metrics, we systematically relax the metric-compatibility and zero-torsion constraints of the rigid magnetic sector. By imposing global flatness on these modified connections, we prove that the curvature of a Magnetic Carrollian universe can be dynamically traded for isolated kinetic energy densities of torsion and non-metricity. Unlike the Lorentzian Trinity which maps gravity to alternative gravitational frameworks, the Carrollian equivalences can also map spacetime geometry to non-gravitational theories. Specifically, we demonstrate that intrinsic torsion recovers Electric Carrollian gravity as the Teleparallel equivalent of Magnetic Carroll gravity; purely spatial torsion reproduces kinetic terms stracturally similar to the magnetic Hamiltonian of scalar-charge Fracton gauge theory; and temporal torsion sectors map independently to $U(1)$ Maxwell electric fields and Carroll-Weyl conformal dilaton theories. Finally, by formulating a Symmetric Teleparallel Carroll connection with minimal non-metricity, we show that the Magnetic Carrollian Lagrangian is dynamically equivalent to an ultralocal, isotropic Electric Carrollian gravity upon exploiting the present freedoms in connection. These results establish a geometric dictionary translating Carrollian gravitational dynamics into the language of tensor gauge theories, electromagnetism, and dilaton theory.

papers.title: Detuning-Controlled Vibrational Autler--Townes Passage toward Single-Sublevel Orientation of Nonpolar Molecules
papers.abstract: Single-sublevel preparation would give collision and surface-scattering experiments access to oriented molecules, yet established orientation methods either require a permanent dipole moment or select only partially. We introduce all-optical Autler--Townes state-selective adiabatic passage (ASAP), in which a detuned infrared field dresses a rovibrational transition, and the selected dressed branch is mapped adiabatically onto one magnetic sublevel as the field vanishes. We resolve the magnetic-sublevel-selected rovibrational Autler--Townes doublet of the R(0) transition of $^{13}$CO$_2$ and show that the coupling strength and detuning set both its separation and the partition of the bare-state composition between its two components. The spectral selectivity of the target dressed branch reaches 97\% at a coupling detuning of $-1.2$~MHz. A density-matrix model calibrated against these spectra returns, for the dressed molecules, a target-sublevel population approaching 0.9 over a broad range of coupling powers and detunings.

papers.title: Second-order Wasserstein response for L\'evy laws
papers.abstract: Moving an atom and splitting it symmetrically can give the same weak change in a L\'evy characteristic, yet produce Wasserstein errors of different orders. We explain this through first- and second-order expansions of the distribution function for infinitely divisible laws with a Gaussian factor. The expansions are uniform over Lipschitz tests and include distributional directions from moving atoms. When the first response is nonzero, analyticity gives the signed second coefficient of the Wasserstein--1 distance. When it vanishes, a finite second displacement moment gives a quadratic response, with a positive coefficient whenever the dispersion is nonzero. For local balanced remeshing, we prove matching bounds in terms of grid-alignment variance and construct a linear program with a controlled optimization gap. We also determine the sharp transition as Gaussian smoothing vanishes. The appendices give proofs, metric speed and length, and multivariate and state-dependent extensions.

papers.title: Conditional Fluctuations of Mean-Field Systems with Stable Common Noise
papers.abstract: We study conditional fluctuations of smooth mean-field systems on a torus with symmetric stable common jumps of index $0 \tfrac{\alpha}{2}$. A second-order tail expansion identifies the response when this condition fails: it shifts the conditional Gaussian mean at criticality and, when nonzero, dominates sampling below criticality. We also identify the transition from a stable to a Brownian rank error. In a translation model, rank and clock couplings give the same microscopic laws but different path fluctuations. Rank coupling gives a functional Gaussian limit. Clock coupling admits no diverging additive path normalization at the limiting center.

papers.title: Homology and higher-order intermediate categories for proper abelian subcategories
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an extension-closed proper abelian subcategory of a triangulated category $\mathcal{C}$, and put $\mathcal{D}_\ell=\Sigma^\ell\mathcal{A}*\cdots*\mathcal{A}$ for $\ell\geq 1$. Assuming that $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(\Sigma^p\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})=0$ for $1\leq p\leq\ell+1$, we construct homology functors $H_i:\mathcal{D}_\ell\to\mathcal{A}$ for $0\leq i\leq\ell$ and prove that triangles in $\mathcal{D}_\ell$ induce natural long exact sequences in $\mathcal{A}$. If $\mathcal{C}$ is Krull--Schmidt, we introduce compatible sequences of subcategories of $\mathcal{A}$ and use them to classify the homology-determined subcategories $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathcal{D}_\ell$ that are closed under extensions and direct summands.

papers.title: Complete Factorial Asymptotics and Integrable Structure of Generalized Charlier Recurrence Coefficients
papers.abstract: We investigate the recurrence coefficients of monic generalized Charlier polynomials for the weight $\rho_\mu(k)=\mu^k/(k!)^2$, $\mu>0$. The coefficients satisfy a discrete Painlev\'e reduction, and their deviations from the limiting values $\beta_n\sim n$ and $\gamma_n\sim\mu$ occur on a factorial rather than algebraic scale. A comparison with the recessive solution $J_n(2\sqrt\mu)$ of the associated discrete Bessel equation, together with a Hankel-determinant sector decomposition, identifies the connection constant as one. For fixed $\mu>0$, this gives $\beta_n-n\sim\mu^{n+1}/[n!(n+1)!]$ and $\mu-\gamma_n\sim\mu^{n+1}/(n!)^2$. We further derive a uniform expansion for the normalized sector factor $\Phi_n(\mu)=e^{-\mu}\mathcal R_n(\mu)$, valid for $0<\mu\le cn$ with each fixed $c<1$: $\log\Phi_n(\mu)=\mu[(n/(n+1))^2-1] -\mu^2(2n-1)/[2(n+1)^4] +O_c(\mu(1+\mu)^{3/2}/n^4)$. The proof uses transition-content moments for Plancherel growth and weighted Poisson-tail estimates. It yields joint refinements of both recurrence coefficients in the subcritical linear regime. We distinguish these quantitative asymptotic results from the classical Painlev\'e, Toda, and Young-diagram identities on which the analysis rests.

papers.title: On the quadratic length of plane Cremona maps of degree 4
papers.abstract: Every non-linear plane Cremona map can be decomposed into quadratic maps, and the minimum number of quadratic maps required is called its quadratic length. It is known that plane Cremona maps of degree 3 have quadratic length either 2 or 3. In this paper, we study the quadratic length of plane Cremona maps $\varphi$ of degree 4. Recall that either $\varphi$ is de Jonqui\`eres, i.e. it has a base point of multiplicity 3, or it is not de Jonqui\`eres. In the latter case, $\varphi$ has quadratic length 2, whereas in the former case we prove that $\varphi$ has quadratic length 3, 4, or 5, and we classify those maps that reach the upper bound.

papers.title: Cohomological non-rigidity of toric manifolds
papers.abstract: For every integer $d\geq4$, we construct pairs of projective toric manifolds of complex dimension $d$ that are not homotopy equivalent but have isomorphic integral cohomology rings and homotopy equivalent 5-fold suspensions. We also construct pairs of quasitoric manifolds over the $d$-dimensional cube with these properties. Our construction starts with a closed, oriented smooth manifold $B$ of real dimension $6$ whose integral cohomology ring is generated by $H^2(B)$. For a class $u\in H^2(B)$, let $L_u$ denote the complex line bundle with first Chern class $u$, and set $P_u=\mathbb P_B(L_0\oplus L_u)$. We show that if $u,v\in H^2(B)$ satisfy $uv=0$, then, for every finite product $N$ of complex projective spaces, the manifolds $P_{u+v}\times N$ and $P_{u-v}\times N$ have isomorphic integral cohomology rings and homotopy equivalent 5-fold suspensions. To distinguish their homotopy types, we introduce the sets of strong zero-product pairs $\mathrm{SZ}^{n,m}(X)\subseteq H^n(X)\times H^m(X)$, which are preserved by homotopy equivalences. Using these sets, we give explicit conditions on $u$ and $v$ ensuring that these manifolds are not homotopy equivalent, and exhibit toric and quasitoric examples satisfying these conditions.

papers.title: Optimal Scaling of Unitary Design Formation in $U(1)$-Symmetric Random Circuits: A Bottleneck Slower than Charge Transport
papers.abstract: Understanding randomness formation under conservation laws is important both for characterizing chaotic phenomena in isolated quantum systems and for symmetry-constrained quantum information processing. $U(1)$-symmetric random circuits on an $N$-qubit system provide a minimal tractable setting for this problem, in which the formation rate of unitary designs was conjectured to be governed by charge transport in the underlying circuit geometry. However, whether charge transport indeed sets the slowest relaxation mode has remained an open problem, due to the difficulty in deriving a tight lower bound on the symmetric design formation rate. In this work, we resolve this problem by determining the optimal scaling of the unitary $k$-design formation rate for $k\leq O(\sqrt{\log N})$ across a wide range of circuit geometries, including lattices, expander graphs, and all-to-all interactions. In particular, for $k\geq 2$, we find that the formation rate is governed by a two-particle encounter rate---the rate at which two random walkers encounter each other in a given circuit geometry. This encounter rate is parametrically smaller than the single-particle transport rate in many geometries, thereby disproving the previous conjecture. We further establish that this encounter mechanism indeed sets the design formation rate by deriving its matching lower bound with a novel proof technique based on an auxiliary subgroup ensemble. Although this encounter mode imposes a robust bottleneck on design formation in $U(1)$-symmetric random circuits, we also show that this bottleneck can be circumvented by using symmetry-breaking local gates and provide an explicit protocol that achieves faster design formation. These results establish a new picture of randomness formation under conservation laws and provide guiding principles for characterizing and efficiently generating symmetry-constrained randomness.

papers.title: Adaptive Inference for Functionals of M-Estimands
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning and contextual bandit algorithms have become increasingly common in sequential decision-making applications. When these methods are deployed in high-stakes domains, there is growing interest not only in learning effective policies, but also in conducting statistical inference for quantities learned under adaptive data collection. However, classical procedures applied naively in these settings can fail: even when estimators are unbiased, their variance becomes path-dependent and as a result may not be asymptotically normal. A growing literature has emerged to ameliorate this problem, but solutions tend to be problem specific and often rely on correct specification of a working model. In this work, we develop a unified framework for constructing asymptotically valid confidence intervals to cover smooth functionals of nonparametric M-estimands under adaptive sampling. Under Neyman orthogonality, we provide two novel methods for performing inference: (1) a self-normalized statistic based on the realized quadratic variation of the influence function and (2) a statistic using a plug-in estimate of the conditional variance based on reweighted influence function increments. Our results allow for flexible nonparametric estimation of nuisance parameters and remain valid under model misspecification. Our theory is supported by a simulation study for a dynamic pricing application which demonstrates that this method can produce asymptotically valid confidence intervals where standard methods fail.

papers.title: Breaking the Bounded Entanglement Barrier for Quantum Position Verification
papers.abstract: Position verification, introduced by Chandran et al. (SIAM J. Computing 2014), allows verifiers to test a prover's claimed position by an interactive protocol. Classical position verification is impossible. Even for Quantum Position Verification (QPV), there always exists an LOCC (Local Operations and Classical Communication) attack if the adversary can hold an exponentially large amount of preshared entanglement. Somewhat surprisingly, we show that we can circumvent this barrier in the idealized continuous-time model, where time is represented by a real-valued parameter and challenge messages can be sent at a time sampled uniformly from a real interval. In this model, we give a BB84-based protocol that remains secure against any finite coalition of LOCC adversaries with arbitrary finite (possibly exponential) quantum storage and entanglement. Our construction can also be instantiated in the discrete-time model. Although prior impossibility results apply, our information-theoretic QPV protocol achieves any desired polynomial gap between the honest parties' total resources (communication and storage) and the adversarial resource bound. To our knowledge, all prior constructions that do not rely on idealized oracles required resources of the honest parties to be at least as large as the proven adversarial entanglement bound. Interestingly, the resource gap depends on the precision in measuring time. As clock precision improves, the adversarial resource bound increases while honest resources remain largely unchanged. We call this the "I sleep, you work" paradigm. Finally, we show that our techniques extend to an information-theoretic, position-based message authentication protocol, which in turn extends to an information-theoretic, position-based quantum key exchange protocol with the same guarantees as our position-verification protocol in the continuous-time and discrete-time models.

papers.title: Piecewise Parabolic Kinetic Energies and Classical Time Crystals
papers.abstract: We present explicit, exact analytic solutions for classical time crystals embedded in a parabolic potential for the position. While Lagrangians with a quartic kinetic energy yield complex trajectories governed by inscrutable elliptic integrals, we demonstrate that unconventional piecewise parabolic kinetic energies -minimized at nonzero values of the speed- admit simple, transparent periodic solutions. In these systems, the speed acquires definite periodic discontinuities but remains always nonzero. The requirement that the action be the smallest available determines the branch that the solution will follow, ensuring in addition that it is stable there and rendering the Hamiltonian single-valued as a function of momentum. Furthermore, we introduce a powerful piecewise parabolic emulation framework to approximate highly non-linear kinetic energies, demonstrating its utility on both quartic time crystals and the relativistic harmonic oscillator. We show that finding exact solutions to these emulated models provides accurate, physically transparent simulacra of complicated problems, offering a robust alternative to standard numerical approximations for non-quadratic kinetic energies.

papers.title: Relative entropy of entanglement and tripartite minimal surface
papers.abstract: We propose a holographic dual of the relative entropy of entanglement for a boundary tripartition $A:B:C$. Our proposal is that, at the leading order, \begin{align} E_R(\rho_{AB}) = \frac{1}{4G_N}\Big[\mathrm{Area}(\Gamma_{\min}) - \mathrm{Area}(\gamma_{AB})\Big] \notag \end{align} where $\Gamma_{\min}$ is the minimal bulk tripartition surface and $\gamma_{AB}$ is the minimal surface homologous to $AB$. For a general random tensor network, we prove the corresponding upper bound by constructing a separable state associated with $\Gamma_{\min}$ and evaluating its relative entropy. We also establish the matching lower bound rigorously for networks of one, two, and three Haar random tensors by bounding the maximal tripartite product-state overlap. In appropriate geometries, the minimal tripartition surface can form a nontrivial tri-junction resembling the Mercedes logo.

papers.title: Bianisotropic Space-Time Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: We experimentally demonstrate bianisotropic space-time metasurfaces based on varactor-loaded omega-shaped meta-atoms. Full-wave simulations reveal coexisting electric and ring-associated magnetic responses at the operating frequency, while a traveling-wave modulation drives reactive loads embedded in both responsive regions of the meta-atom. The resulting space-time modulation generates a reconfigurable polychromatic spectrum with directional sideband radiation governed by Floquet phase matching. Under free-space illumination, the same metasurface preferentially couples the received field toward one guided port, producing modulation-controlled directional routing. The measurements characterize the collective bianisotropic response rather than independently retrieving its electric, magnetic, and magnetoelectric susceptibility components. These results establish bianisotropic space-time metasurfaces as a platform for jointly controlling frequency generation, directional radiation, and wave routing within a single dynamically modulated aperture.

papers.title: Generative sequence modeling for infinite memory processes via predictive states
papers.abstract: We consider estimating the one-step-ahead conditional distribution of a multivariate stochastic process. Many existing approaches rely on assumptions such as finite-range memory, sparsity, or additivity, which can be poorly suited to processes with long-range nonlinear interactions. However, without such structural assumptions, nonparametric estimation is challenging due to the curse of dimensionality. To address this challenge, we introduce a new estimator based on learning representations of the \emph{predictive states} of a stochastic process. We show that the statistical complexity of the estimation problem is determined by the dimension of this predictive state representation. Furthermore, we show that a $p$-dimensional predictive state space can be represented in a $2p+1$-dimensional feature space. Our results imply that faster convergence rates are achievable when the predictive state space is lower-dimensional, i.e., when the past history can be compressed into a lower-dimensional statistic that is sufficient for predicting the future. We establish theoretical convergence rate guarantees for an instantiation of our method based on deep neural network estimators. We implement our method in PyTorch and evaluate its performance on processes with infinite-range memory.

papers.title: Exact Operator Complexity Measures from Random Matchgate Unitaries
papers.abstract: Matchgate circuits describe classically tractable dynamics in a physically relevant setting while nonetheless exhibiting features characteristic of complex quantum systems, such as high amounts of magic. This invites the broader question: to what extent are typical complexity measures saturated under trivial dynamics? Here, we address this by studying the behaviour of different Heisenberg-picture complexity measures in random matchgate ensembles. Our main technical contribution is a tractable and generalisible free-fermionic unitary Weingarten calculus formulated entirely in the Majorana basis. This method is tailored to computing moments of operators, and simplifies to a combinatorics problem which depends on the boundary conditions prescribed by a given operator functional. Using this framework, we derive closed-form expressions for the typical local-operator entanglement, operator stabiliser entropy, and higher-order out-of-time-ordered correlators. For extensive initial Majorana strings, both operator entanglement and stabiliser entropy obey volume laws, even though the underlying circuits remain classically simulable. Out-of-time-ordered correlators can likewise become exponentially small, showing that their late-time saturation value alone does not witness computational hardness and constituting a classically tractable example of emergent free independence. Finally, we relate these separations to operator resource theories, showing how operator entanglement beyond the Gaussian baseline lower-bounds the number of non-Gaussian gates in doped matchgate circuits. Our results present a practical toolbox for computing exact averages over random matchgates, while clarifying the distinction between quantum resources versus simulation complexity, and their dependence on the representation being exploited.

papers.title: LEMON-ZEST: Evolution-Informed Tokenization for Efficient Protein Language Modeling
papers.abstract: Protein Language Models (PLMs) have made remarkable progress following scaling laws established in natural language processing across sequence- and structure-based tasks, yet the potential of tokenization remains underexploited. Unlike human language, proteins preserve structure despite extensive sequence variation, a property standard tokenization strategies fundamentally fail to capture. We introduce ZEST (Zoned Encoding of Sequence Traits), an evolution-informed vocabulary derived from conserved regions of multiple sequence alignments. ZEST allows embedding domain-level biological priors directly at the tokenization stage rather than learning them implicitly through scale. ZEST natively compresses sequences to an average token length of 3.3 residues, enabling our model to process $\geq3380$ residues within a standard 1024-token context window. Building on this, we present LEMON (Layered Extraction of Molecular Ordering from Nature), a compact 200M-parameter sequence-based model for detection of remote homology between protein sequences trained on a single H100 GPU for one week. Despite its modest size, LEMON outperforms models of 600M to 3B parameters and is on-par with TM-Vec. Our results demonstrate that evolution-informed tokenization can substitute for massive parameter scaling, opening a new direction for efficient, biologically-grounded protein representation learning. All code and model weights are publicly available (at \href{https://github.com/LDWLab/ZEST}{github.com/LDWLab/ZEST}) under the MIT license.

papers.title: First Post-Newtonian Cross Terms in Hierarchical Triple Systems: Multiple-Scale Averaging and its Canonical Consistency
papers.abstract: We develop a two-stage multiple-scale method for hierarchical triple systems, using osculating orbital elements and time as the independent variable. We examine the disputed cross terms at orders $\delta\varepsilon^{3/2}$ and $\delta\varepsilon^{7/2}$, for which the multiple-scale results of Lim and Rodriguez (LR) disagree with the effective field theory results of Kuntz, Serra, and Trincherini (KST). Here, $\delta$ is the first post-Newtonian (1PN) parameter, and $\varepsilon=a_*/a_2$ ($a_*\simeq a_1$) measures the orbital hierarchy. These terms arise from couplings between relativistic interactions and the tidal field of the third body. Our results agree with KST: there is no secular term at order $\delta\varepsilon^{3/2}$, while the $\delta\varepsilon^{7/2}$ contribution consists of three parts: a direct term, a first-stage coupling between the inner binary's center-of-mass motion and the tidal field, and a second-stage coupling between the 1PN dipole and the quadrupole. Their sum reproduces the inner-orbit secular dynamics generated by KST's magnetic 1PN--quadrupole Hamiltonian, including its exact mass dependence, for nonsingular eccentricities and inclinations in the nonresonant, hierarchical weak-field regime. The analysis includes mean-anomaly perturbations and resubstitution of short-period corrections in both directions. We clarify how the choice of averaging variable affects the normalization of the mean elements and establish agreement with canonical perturbation theory. In particular, osculating and canonical mean elements give the same inner-orbit secular rates at this order.

papers.title: An information circuit driven by a skyrmion Maxwell's demon
papers.abstract: At the nanoscale, observation and feedback may transform thermal fluctuations into valuable resources. Nevertheless, a framework for experimentation with the resulting probability currents has yet to be firmly established. Here, we present an information heat engine incorporating two interacting magnetic skyrmions in adjacent potential wells. Feedback from a skyrmion in Brownian motion at room temperature to the other yields a Maxwell's demon and a circulating probability current in their joint state space. A linear relationship is confirmed between the probability current and the information affinity, the thermodynamic conjugate value, within certain response range and conditions. We identify the slope as the "information conductance" analogous to electrical conductance. The information conductance is modified by skyrmion interactions and scattering, while Kirchhoff's laws remain valid. These results establish a circuit representation of the state space of an information heat engine with potential applications to computing devices, biological systems and chemical reactions.

papers.title: An Algebraic Approach to Continuously Updating GMM: Estimation and Inference
papers.abstract: The continuously updating GMM estimator (CUE) minimizes a nonconvex objective. We give an algebraic solution in linear instrumental variables models with a fixed joint variance estimate that allows for heteroskedasticity, autocorrelation, or clustering. With one endogenous regressor and a positive definite variance estimate, the objective is a ratio of polynomials. Its global minimum is obtained by comparing the objective at no more than 4k-2 real stationary points and at infinity, with k instruments. The roots can be computed as eigenvalues of a companion matrix. We extend the results to singular variance estimates and characterize the multivariate minimum using finitely many stationary objective values. These results provide methods for computing CUE, overidentification statistics, and likelihood ratio-based tests. Simulations show that local optimization can lead to substantially different estimates and test decisions. The algebraic results are exact, although their numerical implementation requires care in computing polynomial coefficients and roots.

papers.title: Delegation without Priors
papers.abstract: A principal makes decisions relying on the private information held by a biased agent. Lacking a prior over the circumstances that may arise, she seeks a delegation rule that minimizes worst-case regret relative to the complete-information benchmark. The optimal delegation mechanism governs two distinct margins: whether to depart from a common default action, and how much discretion to grant conditional on departure. This rule pairs the default action with an action gap, followed by a discretionary interval with randomized boundaries designed to balance regret across states. This structure is globally optimal within the class of all stochastic, incentive-compatible mechanisms.

papers.title: Holography for integrable field theories
papers.abstract: We develop a holographic dual to the integrable field theories built from $4d$ Chern-Simons theory. The dual theory is a topological string on a generalized Calabi-Yau manifold, which is entirely encoded in a geometric object we call a planar spectral curve. We describe the RG flow for a planar integrable field theory as a geometric flow on the moduli of planar spectral curves. This description is valid at all orders in the 't Hooft coupling. We compute this flow explicitly up to two loops in many examples, and find an exact match with known field theory results. At one loop this includes a wide class of models. At two loops we reproduce the RG flow for the principal chiral model with WZ term, and for a class of integrable $\sigma$-models with target $U(N) \times U(N)$.

papers.title: No infinite spin in the $n$-body problem in all dimensions
papers.abstract: In the planar $n$-body problem, Moeckel and Montgomery \cite{MM25} showed that there is no infinite spin for total collision solutions, when the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Following their approach, generalizations have been obtained for partial collision solutions and parabolic solutions in the planar case, and for total collision solutions in the spatial cases by various authors, all under the same assumption that the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Here we prove there is no infinite spin for any collision or parabolic solution in all dimensions without such an assumption.

papers.title: Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer Actor--Critic: Diffusion Policy Improvement with Finite-Sample Analysis
papers.abstract: Diffusion policies represent multimodal action distributions, but a $Q$-weighted update does not specify how to sample from the resulting target distribution. We propose Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer Actor--Critic (SFAC), an offline-to-online reinforcement learning (RL) method for Kullback--Leibler (KL)-regularized policy improvement through conditional diffusion. A minimax Bellman critic estimates the action-value function, which defines an exponentially tilted target policy. A Doob $h$-transform expresses this update as a correction to the reference diffusion drift. The target drift is a weighted conditional mean of Brownian-bridge labels. We fit it by weighted regression using endpoints from the current policy and pointwise action-value evaluations. In the small-update regime, the KL-regularized update follows the natural policy-gradient direction, and the Doob correction represents the same local change in the space of diffusion drifts. Under suitable conditions, we derive finite-sample bounds that separate the errors from critic estimation, weighted neural drift regression, and diffusion discretization through a reverse-KL actor bound. The average-performance bound depends explicitly on the comparison coefficients over the policy iterations. Across six D4RL offline-to-online tasks, the final scores of the $Q$-guided bridge-regression implementation exceed its offline initialization on every task and Cal-QL on five tasks. We also compare with offline RL and online-only baselines.

papers.title: On the hit problem of rank five
papers.abstract: Let $P_q$ be the graded polynomial algebra $\mathbb F_2[x_1,x_2,\ldots ,x_q]$ over the prime field of two elements, $\mathbb F_2$, with the degree of each $x_i$ being 1. We study the {\it hit Peterson problem} of finding a minimal set of generators for $P_q$ as a module over the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra, $\mathcal{A}.$ In this note, we present the minimal sets of $\mathcal{A}$-generators for $P_5$ in the cases where the degree are sufficiently general.

papers.title: Profinite Non-Rigidity of Arithmetic Lattices and the K\"ahler Property
papers.abstract: We prove that the K\"ahlerness of a finitely presented, residually finite group is not determined by its profinite completion, which answers a question asked independently by Arapura and Libgober. In the proof, we give explicit constructions to characterize the absolute Dynkin types that admit non-isomorphic real forms of higher-rank Lie groups containing torsion-free arithmetic lattices with isomorphic profinite completions.

papers.title: Beyond Empirical Support: Structured Outlier Generation via Sinkhorn Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Outliers are essential for evaluating and improving the robustness of machine learning systems, especially when future distributions may differ significantly from historical training data. In high-stakes applications, robustness often depends on rare cases that finite datasets fail to capture, making simple resampling or perturbation insufficient for stress scenario generation. Existing outlier synthesis methods typically rely on sparse neighborhoods, low support latent regions, or classifier boundary crossings, which can be heuristic, unstable, and tied to specific modalities or architectures. We therefore propose Sinkhorn Boundary Outlier Generation (SBOG), a structured framework for latent-space outlier generation that couples Sinkhorn optimal transport geometry with distributionally robust boundary modeling. The resulting Sinkhorn-induced support cost guides the sampler toward weakly supported boundary regions, while semantic constraints prevent uncontrolled drift from the intended context, yielding controlled deviations from the in-distribution reference measure rather than arbitrary sparse-region samples. Experiments on time series anomaly generation and image outlier synthesis show that our framework produces informative, semantically controlled outliers and improves downstream robustness evaluation across modalities, providing a foundation for stress scenario generation beyond empirical support.

papers.title: Counterdiabatic quantum optimization for efficient state preparation in the Schwinger model
papers.abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), whose design is underpinned by the adiabatic theorem, is one of the leading variational quantum algorithms for preparing the ground states of gauge theories. A recently proposed variant, DC-QAOA, incorporates counterdiabatic driving to accelerate the adiabatic process, reducing both circuit depth and runtime. In this work, we present a systematic analysis, from both theoretical and computational perspectives, of DC-QAOA and related counterdiabatic variants for preparing the ground state of the Schwinger model, the paradigmatic (1+1)-dimensional lattice gauge theory. Benchmarking these methods against standard QAOA, we show that counterdiabatic driving improves ground-state preparation while lowering circuit depth requirements. Our results establish counterdiabatic protocols as a practical route towards efficient quantum simulation of gauge theories.

papers.title: Multiple change-point detection via bottom-up scanning
papers.abstract: We study nonparametric multiple change-point detection for high-dimensional sequences, aiming to identify time points at which the underlying distribution changes. While many existing methods perform well when change-points are well-separated, their performance can deteriorate when structural breaks are densely clustered. To address this challenge, we propose gBottomup, a graph-based bottom-up framework for multiple change-point detection in high-dimensional settings. gBottomup constructs a hierarchical segmentation by proposing merges of adjacent segments and verifying them through an unmerge rule that combines absolute significance with relative local heterogeneity, thereby adaptively refining partitions and estimating the number of change-points. Simulation results demonstrate that gBottomup performs reliably across a range of structural configurations and is particularly effective in frequent change-point settings, where existing top-down procedures may lose sensitivity. We illustrate the proposed method through an analysis of high-dimensional sensor data from an experimental hydraulic system.

papers.title: A Log-Star Comparison Between Expectation Threshold and Fractional Expectation Threshold
papers.abstract: We proved a log-star comparison between the expectation threshold $q(\mathcal F)$ and the fractional expectation threshold $q_f(\mathcal F)$ for any nontrivial increasing family $\mathcal F$ on a finite ground set $V$ of size $|V|=N$. Specifically, we show that $$q_f(\mathcal F)\le64\log_2^*(N+2)\,q(\mathcal F),$$ where $\log_2^* x$ is the iterated logarithm of base-2. Using similiar methods, one can extend this result to the following stronger form: there exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that \[ q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(l(\mathcal F)),\quad q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)), \] where $l(\mathcal F):=\max\{2,\max_{S\in\min\mathcal F}|S|\}$ and $\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)$ denotes the VC-dimension of $\min\mathcal F$. On October 7, 2026, OpenAI released a result proving the equivalence of fractional and integral thresholds, which supersedes the findings in this note. The authors are keeping this note for historical reference.

papers.title: Rational homotopy theory of flag manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $G/P$ be a flag manifold with $G$ simple. We determine the rational homotopy groups $\pi _{\ast }(G/P)\otimes \mathbb{Q}$ and describe the rational cohomology ring $H^{\ast }(G/P;\mathbb{Q})$ solely in terms of the rational homotopy types of $G$ and $P$, respectively. The proof is based on the restrictions of basic Weyl invariants of $G$ to suitable simple factors of $P$, which also address a key nonvanishing issue not settled by earlier approaches of Meier, Shiga-Tezuka, Kotschick, and Terzic.

papers.title: Skyrmion topology of scalar waves in real and momentum space
papers.abstract: Generalizations of magnetic skyrmions to the context of other areas of physics, such as plasmonics, optics (including microcavity polaritons) and even water waves have become an important research topic. However, the generalization of the skyrmion number in such systems is still the subject of active research. While magnetic skyrmions textures are inherently formed by vectors (magnetic spin vectors), recent developments in other areas of physics have generalized the concept of skyrmions and skyrmionic patterns to the case in which scalar fields are used to define 3-component pseudo-spin vectors. This gives rise to a wide variety of skyrmion-like textures, depending on the detailed functional forms of the scalar fields. For example, steady-state outgoing waves in driven-dissipative polariton systems fail to have a well-defined global skyrmion number in real (configuration) space but can have one in momentum space. We classify the skyrmion integral for various scalar fields with different asymptotic behaviors in real space as well as momentum space, and in both cases give conditions for the skyrmion number not to exist, or be integer, half-integer or non-integer. Examples of physical systems to which our analysis can be applied include polariton condensates, water waves and gain-guided lasers.

papers.title: Feedback Stabilization for Sampled Linear Systems with Control-linear Noise
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider linear stochastic systems with control-linear noise and periodically sampled measurements.
