To address these challenges, we propose a framework for solving the Continuous-Time Constrained Linear Quadratic Regulator (CT-CLQR) problem for switched linear systems. Our approach partitions the time horizon into a finite number of intervals, each associated with a specific system mode. The duration of these intervals is parameterized by the switching instants, enabling a reformulation of the problem. We indirectly optimize the switching sequence by fixing the switching sequence and optimizing the interval durations. We derive analytical expressions for the cost function and its gradient, which are critical for efficient optimization. Unlike state-of-the-art methods that impose equality constraints on state evolution, our approach inherently considers the state evolution in the cost function. This not only simplifies the problem formulation but also reduces computational overhead by precomputing shared terms offline, enhancing efficiency during online operations. The proposed method significantly advances existing techniques, offering improved computational efficiency and flexibility. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through comprehensive numerical examples, showcasing its potential for practical applications.

papers.title: Autonomous Precision Milling of Biological Structures via Generic Anatomical Priors and Active Boundary Perception
papers.abstract: Autonomous precision milling of biological structures is challenged by incomplete knowledge of target geometry, local material thickness, and critical internal boundaries. Subject-specific preoperative models can address geometric and thickness variations, but static models cannot determine boundary status encountered during execution, while repeated target-specific imaging limits scalability. This article presents a state-adaptive autonomous milling framework that assigns complementary roles to generic anatomical priors and active boundary perception. A generic anatomical prior provides conservative global guidance and is transformed through semantic-guided registration and hybrid vision-force calibration into robot-executable guidance for individual targets. As milling approaches uncertain boundaries, the robot actively probes the remaining structure and uses relative stiffness changes to estimate boundary status and structural detachability. A state-adaptive controller governs transitions between active perception and spatially selective incremental refinement, repeating this cycle until the termination criterion is satisfied. Hierarchical experiments on biological surrogates and in vivo mouse cranial window creation demonstrate accurate anatomical prior transfer, reliable boundary adaptation, and autonomous precision milling of biological structures.

papers.title: Parallel Circuit Execution for Scalable Quantum Computation
papers.abstract: Today's quantum processors have tens to hundreds of physical qubits, but reliable execution of arbitrary circuits remains limited to fewer than 30 entangled qubits across hardware modalities. Building upon prior work, we introduce an error- and topology-aware method for mapping multiple independent circuits onto disjoint regions of a single large-scale QPU for parallel circuit execution. For applications with many similarly sized circuits, such as observable estimation for Hamiltonian simulation, this approach can reduce billed QPU execution time, with ideal speedup proportional to the number of usable partitions. We demonstrate the approach on IBM's 156-qubit ibm_boston processor using standard QED-C benchmark and Hamiltonian-based observable-estimation workloads. Compared with standard sequential execution, parallel execution reduces billed execution time by 3.5-5.5x while retaining 83-92% of the sequential fidelity. We further evaluate the scaling of parallel circuit execution using GPU-accelerated classical simulation, distributing measurement circuits across GPUs via MPI. Using CUDA-Q on the NERSC Perlmutter system, we achieve up to 13.8x speedup on 16 GPUs (86% parallel efficiency) for an H2 electronic-structure simulation, with scaling evaluated across multiple Hamiltonians and circuit counts. These results provide an indication of the performance ceiling that parallel execution on future quantum hardware may eventually approach. Both execution modes are implemented as a runtime option within the QED-C Application-Oriented Benchmark suite. Together, the results show that circuit-level parallelism can reduce execution cost on current quantum hardware and simulation time on GPU clusters, with the potential for greater benefits as device quality and qubit counts increase.

papers.title: 3D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Novel View Synthesis
papers.abstract: Solving novel view synthesis (NVS) for millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar requires a renderer that is physically faithful, complex-valued, and multi-viewpoint-tractable. No prior method achieves these three properties simultaneously. Differentiable Monte Carlo (MC) ray tracers implement the radar forward model directly with explicit material modeling and complex outputs, but a joint fit across views takes over an hour per scene. Optical-NVS ports of NeRF, hash grids, and 3D Gaussians train fast but discard phase and replace explicit material modeling with opaque learned features, restricting them to power-only range-azimuth (RA) magnitudes. We propose 3D Point Splatting (3DPS), the first differentiable point splatting renderer for radar, derived directly from the standard solid-angle form of the radar equation. Each oriented 3D point carries a material model built on ITU-R P.2040 permittivity and slab reflection, evaluated in closed form, with the resulting complex phasor splatted into range bins through a precomputed point spread function (PSF). The complex-valued output makes the renderer product-agnostic. The same optimized scene yields analog-to-digital converter (ADC), complex range profile (CRP), and RA outputs through standard fast Fourier transform (FFT) pipelines without retraining for each format. On six outdoor ColoRadar scenes, 3DPS reaches 0.587 mean Pearson correlation on held-out RA images. This is between 1.7x and 5.2x the three optical-NVS baselines (RadarSplat, Radar Fields, DART) and 1.3x the mmIR ray tracer at 1/25 of its wall-clock time. Training takes approximately 3 minutes per scene on a single RTX 4090. Project page: https://3d-point-splatting.github.io/

papers.title: Universality transitions in the logarithmic law of random determinants beyond the fourth moment
papers.abstract: For real random matrices $A_n=(a_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le n}$ with independent centered entries of unit variance, \citet{BaoPanZhou2015} established the classical logarithmic law under a uniform fourth-moment condition: \[ \frac{\log|\det A_n|-\frac12\log(n-1)!} {\sqrt{\frac12\log n}} \Rightarrow \mathcal N(0,1). \] We find that this Gaussian universality can be extended beyond the fourth-moment condition, with two distinct transitions in the center and fluctuation scale as the moment condition gradually weaken. The first critical condition is the uniform integrability of the family $\{|a_{ij}|^4/\sqrt{\log(e+|a_{ij}|)}\}_{n,i,j}$. The classical law remains valid under this weaker condition, with no change in center or scale. As the moment condition is weakened further, the classical center can fail. Replacing the classical center $\frac12\log(n-1)!$ by the actual mean $\mathbb E\log|\det A_n|$ preserves the standard Gaussian limit at the original scale and allows the moment condition to be relaxed to a second critical condition: uniform integrability of $\{|a_{ij}|^4/\log(e+|a_{ij}|)\}_{n,i,j}$. Under still weaker moment conditions, the classical scale $\sqrt{\frac12\log n}$ can also fail. Replacing this scale in turn by the actual standard deviation $\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(\log|\det A_n|)}$ yields a standard Gaussian limit whenever the expectations of $|a_{ij}|^4/\{\log(e+|a_{ij}|)\}^{\alpha}$ are uniformly bounded over $n,i,j$, for any fixed $\alpha\ge0$. The results using the actual mean or standard deviation additionally assume uniformly bounded entry densities. We establish the sharpness of the first two critical conditions via counterexamples. We further obtain Berry--Esseen bounds for all three normalizations, with optimal rates under a uniform fourth-moment bound.

papers.title: Function spaces, web spaces, and Lawson-compactness in Domain Theory
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the structural properties of function spaces and their connections with Lawson-compactness and web spaces in domain theory. First, using finite-refinement and palette methods, we characterize the topological spaces $X$ for which the function space $[X\to L]$ is an RB-domain for every RB-domain $L$. In particular, we establish the equivalence between this preservation property and the condition that $X$ is compact, core compact, core coherent, and a web space. We further investigate its relationship with RW$^*$-spaces and obtain partial results concerning the Lawson-Mislove's problem. Second, we construct a countably based topological space $Z$ that is compact, core compact, core coherent, and a web space, but is neither a wide web space nor a C-space. More precisely, its lattice of open sets is a continuous frame satisfying $\kappa$-distributivity for every finite cardinal $\kappa\geq 2$, while failing to be $\omega$-distributive. This provides a negative answer to a question raised by Erne and demonstrates that finite distributivity, even at every finite level, does not imply countable distributivity. Finally, by introducing labelled posets and employing constructions based on presheaves over finite sets and their element posets, we prove that every Lawson-compact domain is a Scott-continuous retract of a Lawson-compact algebraic domain, thereby answering a problem proposed by Kou. As applications, we show that the function space from an RB-domain to a Lawson-compact domain is Lawson-compact. Moreover, for an FS-domain $X$, we establish that $X$ is an RB-domain if and only if $[X\to L]$ is Lawson-compact for every Lawson-compact domain $L$. This characterization also yields the existence of an FS-domain $X$ and a Lawson-compact algebraic domain $L$ for which $[X\to L]$ is not continuous. This gives a negative answer to the question raised by Shen et al.

papers.title: A Complex Structure on A Rational Homology Six-Sphere with Two-Torsion
papers.abstract: We construct a compact, smooth, simply connected complex threefold. Its second and third integral homology groups are cyclic of order two, and its remaining homology groups agree with those of the six-sphere.

papers.title: Minimax-Optimal Early Stopping for SGD via the Discrepancy Principle
papers.abstract: We study early stopping for stochastic gradient descent with a constant step size applied to noisy linear inverse problems with polynomially decaying spectrum. The iteration is stopped by the discrepancy principle, that is, as soon as its residual reaches the prescribed noise level. For H\"older source conditions below a saturation level determined by the polynomial decay, we prove that the mean-square reconstruction error at the stopping index is bounded by the classical rate, up to an explicit factor involving the step size and the incoherence of the design, and that the expected number of iterations is of the order of the oracle stopping index. The rate is minimax-optimal for deterministic noise whenever the spectrum contains an eigenvalue at the oracle scale and this factor stays bounded. The step size is restricted by a spectrum-weighted incoherence condition. The analysis allows rank-deficient designs and inconsistent observations.

papers.title: A Time-Frequency Framework for GKP Codes
papers.abstract: We develop a time--frequency framework for lattice GKP codes in which ideal codewords are realized in the modulation space $M^\infty$ and identified, through a vector-valued Zak transform, with a finite logical fibre over the continuous syndrome torus. Multi-window Gabor analysis then represents the logical vector by a finite block of adjoint-lattice coefficients. We prove that the normalized block map is an isometry, obtain an explicit recovering projection, and derive stable logical reconstruction. We further construct normalizable GKP approximants as lattice-envelope Gabor multipliers and establish weak-$*$ convergence and asymptotically isometric encoding. Finally, we recover displacement syndromes from phase relations between translated coefficient blocks and quantify their stability under additive perturbations.

papers.title: Metric Source Completions and Integrability in Celestial Gravity
papers.abstract: Opposite-helicity soft limits carry ordering information, whereas a metric generating functional has a symmetric mixed response. We compare these structures for Einstein tree amplitudes, retaining the full momentum-conservation distribution. Normalized transport of primary sources fixes the metric response, and a common Banerjee--Pasterski prescription fixes the two ordered scattering currents on compact regular hard packets. At the reference metric, both ordered scattering responses agree with the transport Hessian, so the two matching defects vanish separately. A four-hard-particle example displays the same nonzero recoil coefficient in both orders and in the transport Hessian; an overlapping-source packet resolves the lower-order spin-frame contact. Six-graviton factorization independently tests the recoil and undifferentiated coefficients of the ordering difference. At seven points, angular integration produces a nonzero relative current whose connector variation contains a conjugate bulk term. We derive this term and its cancellation under coherent transport; global cubic scattering matching still requires the physical Ward comparison on the remaining singular overlaps. Transporting the states, kernels and inverse chains together gives a finite Ward identity and coefficientwise reconstruction for that chosen family. Regular packets leave extensions supported solely on excluded hard--hard coincidences undetermined, and the vacuum functional, independent of the hard sources, remains free.

papers.title: Representation Varieties of Stacks and Trace Maps
papers.abstract: We define a derived stack $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ which generalizes the assignment $A\leadsto \operatorname{Rep}_n(A)$ to an algebra of its derived $GL_n$-representation variety of arXiv:1112.1449 from algebras $A$ to perfect stacks $X$ over characteristic 0 fields. In the case of a quasi-projective classical scheme $X$, we show that $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ admits a subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)\subset \mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$, which is in fact represented by a derived scheme almost of finite type. We further construct a Fourier-Mukai integral transform between the derived categories of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$ and $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ which induces a trace map at the level of Hochschild homology generalizing the trace morphism constructed in arXiv:1112.1449 (for finitely presented commutative algebras). We show that the subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ is a derived enhancement of the framed locus of the Quot scheme of points and that this derived scheme is a $GL_n$-torsor over the stack of coherent length $n$ torsion sheaves. Hence, this stack is an analog of the derived character stack for quasi-projective schemes, and we show that for smooth, Calabi-Yau $X$, it inherits a shifted symplectic structure in the sense of arXiv:1111.3209 from the one constructed in arXiv:1812.11913 on the moduli stack of perfect complexes with proper support. This structure is shown to give a generalization of the classical symplectic structure on character varieties of surfaces of genus 1 constructed by Goldman \cite{gold}.

papers.title: Cosmological Collider Signals From a Triangle Loop
papers.abstract: Triangular loop signals appear frequently in cosmological collider models but their analytical forms remain unknown due to multiple technical challenges. Here, we determine for the first time the leading analytical cosmological collider signals generated by a massive scalar triangle loop in inflationary bispectrum and trispectrum. Combining a directional cutting rule with partial Mellin-Barnes representations, we obtain both the local and nonlocal trispectrum signals in a soft limit and derive the leading signal in the squeezed bispectrum. Remarkably, all these signals are reproduced by the corresponding bubble diagram with a single effective pinched coupling. Signals beyond leading order and cases with arbitrary internal masses, spins, and interactions can be generated within the same framework. Our approach also provides a systematic route to extracting analytical loop signals from general cosmological correlators.

papers.title: Distributed Linear Programming on GPU Clusters at Extreme Scale
papers.abstract: Large linear programs can exceed the memory of a single compute node. Although first-order methods replace sparse factorizations with GPU-suited matrix-vector products, other solver phases can reintroduce a single-node memory limit. We present SHARDLP, a distributed GPU LP solver that keeps the matrix and primal-dual state partitioned from sharded input through solution output. On the Google PDLP benchmark, SHARDLP solves ten of eleven instances, compared with eight in the published CPU PDLP study. On the largest benchmark, eight H200 GPUs solve a 1.185-billion-variable, 6.338-billion-nonzero LP in 9.9 minutes; the published CPU experiment reports 21.06 hours on different hardware. Beyond this benchmark, separately checked multi-node solves reach up to 13.604 billion variables and 40.807 billion nonzeros, while validated executions span up to 76 GPUs across 29 compute nodes. For column-partitioned solves, support-aware communication skips GPUs that store no coefficients for a row; on an LP with 2.76 billion nonzeros, it cuts modelled communication by 92.97% and improves solver time by 1.27x-1.52x. The code for SHARDLP is available at https://github.com/ArnaudDeza/ShardLP.

papers.title: Equilibria for Time-inconsistent Regular-singular Control Problems with Non-exponential Discount
papers.abstract: This paper studies a time-inconsistent mixed regular-singular control problem in continuous time with non-exponential discount. We seek time-consistent equilibria in an intrapersonal game framework and propose two novel definitions of regular-singular equilibrium where both regular and singular controls are unified via control laws. The standard equilibrium definition allows simultaneous perturbations of both controls, while a mild definition restricts perturbations to one control at a time. Verification theorems providing sufficient conditions are established for both definitions. We illustrate the applicability of the theory through the effort and dividend problem. First, a mild equilibrium is constructed, yet not a standard equilibrium, highlighting the distinction between the two definitions. Moreover, we derive semi-explicit threshold-type equilibria under both a mixture of exponential discount functions and a pseudo-exponential discount function. In both cases, the convexity of the value function is rigorously established, the equilibrium conditions are verified, and the existence of the effort and dividend thresholds is proved. Numerical results reveal the impacts of exogenous parameters on the effort and dividend thresholds and the equilibrium value function, along with their economic implications.

papers.title: PAC-Bayesian Bounds for Learning Partially Observed Stochastic Linear Time-Invariant State-Space Systems with Inputs and Sub-Gaussian Noise
papers.abstract: In this paper we derive a Probably Approximately Correct (PAC)-Bayesian error bound for partially observed linear time-invariant (LTI) stochastic dynamical systems in state-space form with inputs and sub-Gaussian noise. Such bounds are widespread in machine learning, and they are useful for characterizing the predictive power of models learned from finitely many data points. The bound derived in this paper relates the expectation of prediction errors with the prediction error generated by the model on the data used for learning. In addition, we show that it can also be used to derive bounds for the parameter estimation error. In turn, this allows us to provide finite-sample error bounds for the prediction error and parameter estimation error for a wide class of system identification algorithms. Furthermore, as LTI systems are a sub-class of recurrent neural networks (RNNs), these error bounds could be a first step towards PAC-Bayesian bounds for RNNs.

papers.title: Time-Dependent Quantum Monte Carlo for fermions: from Bayesian conditioning to spinor dynamics
papers.abstract: The time-dependent quantum Monte Carlo (TDQMC) method represents a many-electron state by an ensemble of replicas. Each electron is represented by a cloud of walkers sampling its density in physical space, with one walker and one guide wave per replica. The method replaces the Hartree potential with a conditional interaction constructed from the walker positions. Here, we derive this conditional interaction. By treating a walker as a finite-resolution localization of its electron, we show that Bayes' theorem, together with a single empirical substitution, leads to the Nadaraya-Watson form previously introduced on heuristic grounds. This form is recovered as an approximate Bayesian inference and becomes exact in the limit of vanishing resolution length. Because conditioning removes the gauge freedom that eliminates the orthonormality multipliers in Hartree-Fock theory, we enforce orthonormality through a term derived directly from the constraint. We further generalize the formulation to spinors, in which Pauli suppression at coincidence is graded by the local spin alignment. The resulting equations recover the established two-particle spin equations in the mean-field limit. For two electrons in a double quantum dot subjected to an inhomogeneous magnetic field, comparison with the exact solution shows that the spinor equations reproduce the non-collinear spin geometry inaccessible to collinear calculations. At strong exchange, determinant replicas recover most of the one-body entanglement entropy missing from a single-determinant description, although their spin contribution remains deficient. This deficiency is remedied by replicas constructed as the spin-coupled pair of valence-bond theory, which also reproduce the exact spin angle and singlet probability throughout the crossover between the exchange- and Zeeman-dominated regimes.

papers.title: Adaptively Incorporating Directional Hints into Zeroth-Order Optimization
papers.abstract: We study zeroth-order optimization of nonconvex functions with the aid of directional hints, which are cheap but potentially inaccurate approximations of the true gradient direction, given by linear subspaces at each iteration. To leverage these hints adaptively while maintaining robustness to their quality, we introduce Control-Variate Zeroth-Order Descent (CV-ZOD), a new framework that refines the classical zeroth-order gradient estimator with a control variate that can be set based on the directional hints. We first show that the oracle algorithm that optimally sets the reference vector and step size at each iteration achieves a convergence rate that interpolates between the first-order $O(1/T)$ rate and the zeroth-order $O(d/T)$ rate, depending on the quality of the hints along the trajectory. We then develop a practical variant of CV-ZOD that achieves the same oracle guarantee up to logarithmic factors, without any prior knowledge of the hint quality. We validate the method empirically on simulation-based scientific optimization tasks, demonstrating sustained progress on nonconvex landscapes where zeroth-order descent is slower and existing guided methods stall as guidance deteriorates.

papers.title: SGD in Multiclass Logistic Regression: Sequential Learning and Scaling Laws
papers.abstract: We study the training dynamics of multiclass logistic regression on high-dimensional mixture models with a large number of classes and establish precise scaling laws governing the cross-entropy risk under gradient-based optimization. We show that learning proceeds sequentially across classes, from most to least frequent. When the class priors follow a power law distribution, the risk dynamics decompose into three phases: an initial plateau until the first class is learned, a power-law decay regime during which sequential learning occurs, and a final convergence regime. We then analyze how model capacity interacts with optimization under a fixed compute budget. When the effective dimension is restricted via projection onto leading principal components, the risk decomposes into a capacity term (a power law in the retained dimension) and an optimization term (a power law in training time). Optimizing this tradeoff yields a compute-optimal scaling law for logistic regression, with explicit prescriptions for model size and training time as functions of compute. These results extend theoretical scaling laws from linear regression to multiclass classification, while connecting to empirical scaling laws observed in large-scale neural networks.

papers.title: Topology Obstructs Pure Foundation Neural Quantum States
papers.abstract: Foundation models for ground states in spin-1/2 systems are a promising method for problems ranging from quantum chemistry to identifying new phase diagrams. Nearly all such models are currently pure-states that condition on the Hamiltonian's parameters, whose Monte Carlo samples give energy estimates according to the variational principle. In this contribution, we show that this representation is topologically obstructed. For any gapped Hamiltonian family whose ground-state bundle is non-trivial, every continuous normalized state-vector model has zero fidelity with the ground state at some parameter value in the Hamiltonian family. For that value, the energy is at least one spectral gap, $\Delta$, with an $O(\Delta)$ gap in an open-neighbourhood of that point. We show that this is a sufficient no-go also in the case of degenerate ground-state manifolds, time dynamics, and periodic systems with mixed space-time topology, demonstrating these obstructions on one- and two-qubit systems. We discuss how this causes a spike in the fidelity susceptibility, giving a numerical signature of a phase-transition where there is none. Finally, we show that operator-valued models canonically avoid these obstructions and preserve topological information, implying a structural necessity in representation for foundation neural quantum states.

papers.title: Broad-angle photon-pair generation from high-$Q$ flatband resonant 3R-MoS$_{2}$ metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) in ultrathin optical resonant metasurfaces offers a promising platform for integrated quantum light sources. However, conventional resonances suffer from steep momentum dispersion, limiting photon-pair generation to narrow excitation and emission angles. Here, we demonstrate a high-$Q$ flatband resonant 3R-MoS$_{2}$ metasurface for high-efficiency, broad-angle SPDC photon-pair generation. By combining Brillouin zone folding with in-plane symmetry breaking, we engineer a high-$Q$ flatband resonance in the near-infrared regime, maintaining a robust $Q$-factor across a wide range of incident angles. Exploiting the strong local electric field enhancement of resonance and the large second-order susceptibility of 3R-MoS$_{2}$, the metasurface boosts the degenerate SPDC pair-generation rate with orders of magnitude enhancement over an unpatterned film of identical thickness. Crucially, the near-zero band dispersion extends the effective emission angle to $\pm 5^{\circ}$ with negligible spectral drift $\sim 0.1$ nm and high directional tolerance. Under pulsed excitation with a finite spectral bandwidth, the metasurface maintains a substantial bandwidth-averaged photon-pair yield, while demonstrating strong spectral locking of the resonant emission channel against pump wavelength detuning despite the expected trade-off in generation efficiency. This work establishes a versatile strategy for momentum-independent quantum light sources, opening new avenues for scan-free quantum ghost imaging and quantum information processing.

papers.title: Choosing the Dictionary and Penalty for IV-LASSO
papers.abstract: Estimating an instrumental variables (IV) first stage with the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) requires choosing a dictionary and penalty. Existing rules target first-stage objectives rather than precision of the structural parameter estimate. We derive a feasible approximate mean squared error (AMSE) criterion for full-sample IV-LASSO with one endogenous regressor and homoskedastic Gaussian errors. For a prespecified list of dictionary-penalty pairs, the criterion trades off approximation of the optimal instrument against a complexity cost that depends on the first two moments of the LASSO effective dimension and on the degree of endogeneity. The selected pair attains the smallest candidate-specific AMSE component up to vanishing relative error. In simulations calibrated to Paravisini et al. (2015), the criterion improves substantially on plug-in rules at low endogeneity and on cross-validation at high endogeneity, with nearly identical results under non-Gaussian errors. A supplementary appendix formally extends analysis to a class of non-Gaussian errors.

papers.title: Inverse-seesaw and inflationary scale relations in a supersymmetric 331 model from an SU(6) GUT model
papers.abstract: We propose a $N=1$ supersymmetric $SU(6)$ theory with an intermediate $(SU(3)_C\times SU(3)_L\times U(1)_X)$ phase, in which common fields and operators relate the neutrinos, gauge mediation, unification, and symmetry-breaking sectors. The antisymmetric Dirac matrix of the inverse-seesaw sector has rank two, yielding one vanishing light-neutrino mass at leading order. A higher-dimensional symmetry-breaking correction lifts this zero mode through its projection onto the left and right null vectors of the Dirac matrix, leading to a quartic suppression in the ratio of the intermediate and ultraviolet scales. Complete unified messenger multiplets preserve the relative one-loop gauge coupling evolution while modifying the unified coupling. When the same supersymmetry-breaking spurion generates the singlet lepton-number-violating parameter, an analytical relation emerges between the messenger scale, the lepton-number mediator scale, and the unified coupling. The two-loop gauge evolution remains perturbative for the assumed heavy-threshold spectrum. In the inflationary sector, the scalar-amplitude normalization determines the coupling governing both the inflationary potential and the radial scalar mass in the broken vacuum. The physical scalar directions transverse to the inflaton are stable within the neutral supergravity subspace, while the combined inflationary and gauge-mediated conditions imply a significant sensitivity of the symmetry-breaking vacuum. An examination of the allowed operators shows that additional ultraviolet conditions are required to obtain the observed active-neutrino mixing, suppress competing lepton-number-violating terms, and complete the heavy-field spectrum. Our analysis establishes the analytical scale relations among the neutrino, messenger, unification, and inflationary sectors and identifies the conditions necessary for their simultaneous realization.

papers.title: Thermodynamic performance of a measurement-driven quantum engine with a two-parameter $(p,q)$-deformed harmonic oscillator
papers.abstract: We address a single-bath measurement-driven engine with a two-parameter $(p,q)$-deformed oscillator spectrum. A nonselective Gaussian quadrature measurement supplies energy between two population-preserving work strokes. We evaluate its finite-dimensional transition matrix without outcome quadrature and derive the leading weak-measurement heat. Uniform spectral scaling gives the Otto efficiency exactly; deformation changes the relative gaps and the conversion of measurement energy into work. The infinite quadrature is essentially self-adjoint for $\max(p,q)\le1$; above this range a self-adjoint extension must be specified. We instead choose an explicit $N=40$ effective matrix model. At $\beta\hbar\omega_i=1$, fixed physical resolution $\sigma=4$, and $\omega_f/\omega_i=2$, the largest reported efficiency in $0.7\le p_f,q_f\le1.2$ is approximately $0.782$, compared with the undeformed value $0.5$. Independent dimension checks reproduce these values but do not establish an infinite-dimensional limit in the enhanced regime. Comparisons at selected matched resources and at fixed mean deformation reveal dependence on spectral shape beyond first order. The working-medium efficiency excludes measurement-apparatus and control implementation costs.

papers.title: Schwartz-Class Gabor Windows and the Balian-Low Classification
papers.abstract: A lattice Gabor frame consists of a window function and its time-frequency shifts along a lattice. We classify the lattices that admit Schwartz-class and, equivalently, Feichtinger frame windows. Except for symplectically irrational lattices of critical covolume 1, we determine the lattice-dependent achievable window smoothness and decay using the scale of modulation spaces. For symplectically rational lattices, including the rational lattices typically used in digital applications, the classification is governed by an integer lattice parameter introduced herein, the symplectic index gap. Our results extend the classical and amalgam Balian-Low theorems. The companion paper "Tilings, Packings, and Smooth and Compactly Supported Gabor Windows" develops the associated tiling-packing theorem and compact-support constructions.

papers.title: Physical policy gradient theorem for in situ stochastic-adjoint training
papers.abstract: In situ adjoint training extracts parameter gradients directly from measurement, but has so far been limited to reciprocal or restricted systems. We introduce the physical counterpart of the policy gradient theorem: a stochastic-adjoint gradient estimator that lifts these constraints by trading reciprocity for nondegenerate diffusion. As validation, we train a nonlinear resonator network, whose own dynamics supply the policy, against antagonistic temporal modulations with gradients from measured stochastic trajectories alone, without finite differences or a separate adjoint experiment.

papers.title: Energy Partitioning at the Termination Shock
papers.abstract: We show new results of a global 3D magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulation of the Boston University outer heliosphere model where we used a newly developed approach that distributes the non-adiabatic shock heating among the cold protons, electrons, and pickup-ions (PUIs), while maintaining total energy conservation of all ions. In previous simulations (E. S. Bair et al. 2025; B. van der Holst et al. 2026) non-adiabatic shock heating was distributed such that the resulting proton temperature jump at the termination shock (TS) was too high. Using a new methodology the simulation results improved with respect to the solar wind proton temperature jump observed at the TS by Voyager 2. Because we directly control the distribution of non-adiabatic heating at the TS, we have the opportunity to study the scenario of a non-adiabatic physical process heating cold plasma and PUIs in the TS and its effect on the global MHD solution. The results show that having a fraction of up to 8.5\% of the non-adiabatic shock heating going towards thermal solar wind protons at the TS reproduces the jump conditions observed along the V2 trajectory. This fraction depends on the thermal proton and PUI number densities. This information is key to understanding the physical processes that shape the heliosphere. As shown by M. Opher et al. (2020), PUIs significantly change the shape of the heliosphere; for example, the presence of hot PUIs results in a thinner inner heliosheath. Our work provides the architecture of how energy partitioning at shocks in kinetic simulations (J. Giacalone et al. 2021) can be utilized in global MHD models.

papers.title: On a basepoint issue in the tempered dual of $p$-adic $SL(n)$
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero. Let $M$ be a Levi subgroup of $G = \mathrm{SL}(n,F)$. Consider the action on the discrete series of $M$ of the group of unitary unramified characters of $M$ (where a character acts by twisting). Given an orbit $\mathcal{O}$ for that action, let $W_\mathcal{O}$ be the global stabilizer of $\mathcal{O}$ in the Weyl group of $M$. We construct families of orbits $\mathcal{O}$ for which the action of $W_\mathcal{O}$ has no fixed point. More precisely, let $n \geq 8$ be an integer that is not prime and not equal to $9$. We attach families of orbits without fixed points to any divisor $m \geq 2$ of $n$ such that $m \;| \; q-1$ where $q$ is the order of the residue field of $F$. The Levi subgroup $M \subset G$ for the corresponding families has $m$ blocks of size $k\geq 2$ and $2$ blocks of size $m$. The core of the paper is the construction of superculpidal representations of $\mathrm{GL}(m,F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}(k,F)$ satisfying some conditions that we require to construct the families of orbits $\mathcal{O}$ that we expects. In addition, we study the fixed point problem for the dimensions $n$ that we excluded above, i.e., prime or small dimensions. We prove that there is always a fixed point under the action of $W_\mathcal{O}$ in those cases.

papers.title: Composition gradients in sub-Neptunes: K2-18 b and TOI-270 d as case studies
papers.abstract: Structure models of sub-Neptunes commonly assume purely adiabatic interiors with distinct layers of homogeneous composition. We assess how allowing for more complex interiors with composition gradients affects the inferred internal structure and bulk compositions of the sub-Neptunes K2-18 b and TOI-270 d. We compare purely adiabatic models with distinct layers against models that include composition gradients and stable non-convective regions. We present solutions that are consistent with the observed masses, radii, and atmospheric boundary conditions. We find that composition gradients significantly increase the range of viable interior structures: For example, the interior degeneracy remains substantial even for fixed mass and radius, and the maximum hydrogen-helium (H-He) mass fraction can increase significantly: for K2-18 b by a factor of about three at a 1 bar temperature of 300 K and of about ten at 600 K, and generally by more than an order of magnitude for TOI-270 d. Composition gradients further weaken parameter correlations: for K2-18 b and TOI-270 d, the Spearman rank correlation between the H-He and iron abundances drops from $\sim0.7$ to $\sim0.3$, with a similar weakening between the H-He abundance and the rock-to-iron mass ratio. However, other correlations, such as between the H-He abundance and the water-to-rock mass ratio, persist or even strengthen and remain non-negligible. Purely adiabatic models underestimate the range of plausible compositions and overestimate the impact of more precise measurements, atmosphere models, and host-star constraints on a more accurate characterisation. We suggest that interior models of sub-Neptunes should by default include more complex interiors, such as composition gradients and non-convective regions, when using data for interpreting the planetary structure, formation, and evolution.

papers.title: VocalCoachBench: Benchmarking Audio-Language Models on Expert Feedback for Singing
papers.abstract: Recent audio-language models are increasingly evaluated on recognizing, describing, and reasoning about audio, but expert-facing applications require a different capability: producing feedback that identifies problems and suggests corrective actions grounded in the input. We introduce VocalCoachBench, a benchmark for evaluating audio-language models on expert vocal coaching feedback for singing. VocalCoachBench contains 515 recordings annotated by 18 professional vocal trainers, yielding 1,064 expert audio-level reviews and 12,216 atomic coaching claims. It comprises a same-song subset for controlled comparison and a diverse-song subset for segment-grounded feedback across varied songs and recording conditions. To accommodate the open-ended nature of expert feedback, VocalCoachBench separates deterministic structured targets from claim-based assessment of free-form diagnosis and corrective guidance. Human annotation analysis shows that expert agreement varies strongly with label granularity, motivating hierarchical structured metrics and claim-based evaluation of open-ended feedback. Experiments with 12 recent audio-language models reveal a persistent gap: while the strongest models can compare performances and identify broad issue domains in free-form feedback, the best Top-3 macro-F1 only slightly exceeds a label-prior baseline, and strict diagnosis hit rates remain below 8%. To our knowledge, VocalCoachBench provides the first public testbed for evaluating audio-grounded expert feedback for singing, moving audio-language evaluation beyond description toward analytic feedback. Data, code, and audio examples are available at https://hayeonbang.github.io/VocalCoachBench.

papers.title: Prospective Coding Improves Learning in Deep Continuous-Time Recurrent Networks
papers.abstract: Temporal integration gives continuous-time recurrent networks memory, but in deep stacks it also delays bottom-up signals and attenuates top-down errors. We compensate for this delay by making each layer's bottom-up input prospective, and we develop Recursive Quadrature Filters (RQFs), biologically motivated temporal band-pass filters that are a special case of diagonal state-space models (SSMs). Starting from an energy model, we derive the RQF dynamics and show that each RQF is a band-pass filter whose learnable parameters control its tuning frequency and bandwidth. We then make each layer's bottom-up input prospective using a parameter-free two-tap update that leaves the recurrent transition and parallel scan unchanged. We extend this correction to general diagonal SSMs and show that it mitigates depth-dependent gradient attenuation when temporal gradients are truncated, i.e., spatial-only backpropagation. We evaluate the performance of RQFs, S5, and ORGaNICs (a nonlinear gated RNN with built-in attentional modulation and recurrent normalization) trained using full backpropagation through time (BPTT) and spatial-only backpropagation. Under full BPTT, the prospective variants of these models match or outperform their non-prospective controls in every configuration. A non-residual width-32 six-layer RQF achieves 96.09% accuracy on raw-audio Speech Commands with 31.9k parameters; a width-64 six-layer RQF achieves 83.36% on the 16,384-step Path-X task. We also introduce selective RQFs (sRQFs), which make each filter's input gain and, optionally, its bandwidth and tuning frequency input-dependent while retaining the parallel scan. With the input gain alone, the same six-layer model achieves 86.31% on Path-X; with all three input-dependent, a four-layer prospective sRQF solves Selective Copying (99.83%).

papers.title: Limits of Stochastic Semigroups and Block-Triangular Majorisation
papers.abstract: We investigate limits of semigroups of stochastic matrices defined by their invariant distribution. Given probability vectors $q(\beta)$ depending on a parameter $\beta$, we introduce a notion of convergence as $\beta\to\infty$ for the corresponding semigroups of $q(\beta)$-preserving stochastic matrices and investigate the structure of the resulting limit. In general, the limiting semigroup differs from the semigroup preserving the limiting distribution, showing that these two operations do not commute. We develop a general framework for such limiting semigroups and study in detail the case in which the invariant distributions are Gibbs vectors at inverse temperature $\beta$. In that case, the limiting semigroup consists of block-upper-triangular stochastic matrices subject to additional substochasticity constraints. We characterise and enumerate their extremal elements and determine the preorder on probability vectors induced by the action of the semigroup. The resulting notion of Block-Triangular majorisation interpolates between ordinary majorisation and upper triangular (also known as unordered) majorisation. We show that it is completely characterised by a finite family of monotones and analyse the corresponding behaviour of R{\'e}nyi $\alpha$-entropies as $\beta\to\infty$.

papers.title: A SHARP MASS THRESHOLD FOR BOUNDEDNESS IN A CRITICAL QUASILINEAR CHEMOTAXIS MODEL WITH INDIRECT SIGNAL PRODUCTION: THE RADIALLY SYMMETRIC CASE
papers.abstract: A critical quasilinear chemotaxis model with indirect signal production in space dimensions higher than two is studied under radial symmetry. Exploiting the variational structure of the system, the existence of a sharp mass threshold M\textsubscr{c} > 0 is established: all solutions with mass below M\textsubscr{c} are global and bounded, while those with mass above M\textsubscr{c} and sufficiently negative energy are global but blow up in infinite time. Moreover, the value of the critical mass M\textsubscr{c} is related to the best constant of a variant of a Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality.

papers.title: Entanglement dynamics of accelerated atoms with environment-induced interactions
papers.abstract: We investigate the influence of environment-induced interactions on the entanglement dynamics of two uniformly accelerated atoms coupled to a fluctuating massless scalar field with a reflecting boundary. The two atoms are aligned perpendicular to the boundary. The entanglement behavior is influenced by the competition between the environment-induced interatomic and the environment-induced atom-plate interactions, which can be characterized by certain critical values. The maximum of concurrence generated during evolution decreases non-monotonically with the acceleration, which implies that the anti-Unruh phenomenon can exist for some situations even when both environment-induced interatomic and environment-induced atom-plate interactions are considered.

papers.title: Such stuff as magic is made on: compact operator algebra, stabilizer polytope and the structure of reduced density matrices in a Kitaev spin liquid
papers.abstract: Quantum many-body systems exhibit rich and complex behaviour. Magic has recently emerged as a powerful new diagnostic for probing such systems, complementing other key features such as many-body entanglement. Here, starting from an investigation of the onset of magic within subsystems of a larger many-body quantum system, we show that intricate structures emerge which shed important light on the underlying many-body physics. Focusing on the Kitaev honeycomb model, we first identify the temperature below which local subsystems acquire magic. Remarkably, we find that the optimal magic witnesses active at the onset of magic reveal compact operator spaces that continue to capture the local thermal states throughout their subsequent evolution. For the six-site hexagonal marginal, this connection can be made stronger: the same operator space emerges independently from the symmetries of the local marginal and forms the symmetry-resolved plaquette algebra. When these symmetries are realized exactly, the local state lies entirely within this algebra and the reduced robustness of magic is equal to the full robustness of magic. The same reduced description can also be applied to other local quantum resources, which we illustrate using genuine multipartite entanglement. Furthermore, the operator spaces possess a rich algebraic structure in the form of finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebras, with a natural interpretation in terms of bond and bond-cycle operators. Our general methodology therefore show how the onset of local magic can reveal a compact, physically meaningful operator structure underlying the finite-temperature Kitaev spin liquid, and opens up a new avenue towards reduced descriptions of quantum resources in many-body systems.

papers.title: Transient discs around isolated accreting neutron stars
papers.abstract: Mature, isolated neutron stars can accrete from the interstellar medium. Due to turbulence, the accreted gas can have a substantial angular momentum and form a disc around the compact object. In this paper, we perform a population synthesis of isolated neutron stars in the Milky Way that specifically tracks the possibility of disc formation, which typically requires a low spatial velocity of the compact object ($\lesssim 40$ km s$^{-1}$). In general, weak magnetic fields favour disc formation as the magnetosphere occupies a smaller volume. Still, even in the case of fields decaying exponentially over a characteristic timescale of $\sim 1.5$ Gyr, we find that for several realistic models of propeller spin-down, only a small fraction of accretors (down to $\sim 0.02$ %) attain discs. However, disc-accreting isolated neutron stars are relatively numerous among the brightest sources. We estimate that their number can reach a few hundred at X-ray fluxes of $\gtrsim 10^{-14}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$. We speculate that disc-accreting isolated neutron stars can manifest as long-period radio transient sources via electron cyclotron maser emission, predicting spectra and critical conditions for quenching.

papers.title: Linker Functionalization and pH Tuning Enhance Solar-Driven Catalytic CO$_2$ Reduction in MOF-5
papers.abstract: The wide band gap of metal-organic framework (MOF) 5 constrains its use in photocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO$_2$) reduction despite its high porosity and favorable mass-transport properties. Adopting a state-of-the-art first-principles approach, we systematically investigate the effects of volumetric strain, metal-node substitution, linker functionalization, and pH control as knobs to improve the CO$_2$ photocatalytic ability of MOF-5. Strain and metal-node substitution negligibly affect the gap, whereas linker functionalization narrows it into the visible range via in-gap states while preserving reduction-side alignment at pH = 0. The resulting reduction energetics are strongly sensitive to both linker functionalization and pH. Halogenated and hydroxylated frameworks provide access primarily to HCOOH, CO, and HCHO under alkaline conditions, principally with the Mg and Zn nodes, whereas COOH functionalization offers the broadest thermodynamic accessibility across the full CO$_2$ reduction sequence. NH$_2$ retains thermodynamic feasibility for all target reduction pathways but with larger overpotentials, while NO$_2$ generally yields unfavorable reduction energetics. Crucially, within the COOH series, the choice of the metal node tunes the fundamental gap by over 1 eV with only minor changes in the reduction overpotentials, placing Sr- and Ba-based architectures as the most favorable ones for broad product selectivity with visible-light excitation. Linker functionalization substantially reduces the spatial overlap of the frontier states, promoting photoinduced charge separation. Taken together, these results establish linker functionalization and solution pH as complementary design levers for independently tuning light absorption and CO$_2$-reduction energetics in MOF-5, establishing a rational and viable route for designing efficient MOF-based photocatalysts.

papers.title: Sensing Bone-Conducted Speech with Earbuds
papers.abstract: Clear capture of the wearer's own voice (OV) is essential when using earbuds for mobile communication. However, OV capture remains challenging in noisy environments. Bone-conducted (BC) speech, which can be sensed as vibrations of the earbud housing, can be used to improve OV capture. However, neither bandwidth nor spatial characteristics of OV-induced earbud vibrations have been analyzed in detail, despite both characteristics being relevant, e.g., for sensor choice and placement. This study investigates both characteristics, based on measurements with two earbud models. Spectrally, results indicate that OV-induced earbud vibrations exhibit a low-pass characteristic, with a steep roll-off of -93 dB per decade above 400 Hz. Thus, sensors with comparatively low noise floors are required to sense the vibrations above \SI{1}{\kilo\hertz}. Spatially, results indicate that the earbuds mainly vibrate in and out of the ear canal entrance, with high consistency between subjects and fits. Simulations confirm that this enables capture of the high-power vibrations below 400 Hz by a single-axis sensor with less than 1.5 dB mean attenuation.

papers.title: Orthogonal polynomials which are eigenfunctions of a partial differential operator
papers.abstract: We study orthogonal polynomials of $d = d_1+d_2$ variables with respect to a wrapped product weight function $\Wb(\bm x,\bm y) = W_1(\bm x/\rho(\bm y)) W_2(\bm y)$ for $(\bm x, \bm y) \in \mathbb{R}^{d_1} \times \mathbb{R}^{d_2}$, where $\rho$ is either linear or the square root of a nonnegative quadratic polynomial, and identify all such polynomials that are eigenfunctions of a second-order linear differential operator. For $d =2$, it is known that there are primarily, up to affine transformations, five families of such polynomials, which are products or wrapped products of classical orthogonal polynomials of one variable; all five families have their counterparts in higher dimensions, but no characterization is known in dimension three or higher. Our study explores viable wrapped product families, finds explicit second-order differential operators for two new families of orthogonal polynomials in $d= d_1+d_2$ variables that have not been studied before when either $d_1>1$ or $d_2 > 1$, and provides, in particular, a complete list of such operators among all wrapped product orthogonal polynomials when $d = 3$. The list also includes four families that are eigenfunctions of a fourth-order differential operator, whereas no second-order operator is available. Moreover, orthogonal polynomials on the corresponding wrapped quadratic surfaces that are eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator on the surface are also studied.

papers.title: Amortized Opacity Marginalization Improves C/O Interval Calibration for Brown-Dwarf Retrievals
papers.abstract: Molecular line lists disagree at a level that measurably shifts retrieved C/O, so retrievals conditioned on a single list omit a dominant systematic from their error bars. Classical marginalization re-runs a full retrieval under K opacity realizations per object. We move that cost into simulation: while generating the training set we randomize opacities (smooth multiplicative Fourier fields in log(nu) plus a discrete line-list mixture, under a deliberately broad prior informed by measured inter-list differences), so a neural posterior estimator learns an already-marginalized posterior. On perturbed held-out spectra (n=2048) a standard NPE covers nominal 90% C/O intervals 43.3% of the time against 82.4% for a compute-matched marginalized network; three-seed control ensembles reach 93.2% on clean data but 61.4% under perturbation, against 89.4% marginalized, isolating the deficit as opacity-induced (TARP joint expected-coverage deviation 0.005 against 0.035 for a single control network). An axis ablation traces the gain to the continuous field (45.4% for the discrete swaps alone, 79.3% for the field alone). In simulation, real JWST bad-pixel masks with median filling cut the marginalized ensemble's C/O coverage from 0.894 to 0.683; an ensemble retrained with mask augmentation holds 0.918 under the full deployment preprocessing (n=1024). We apply the networks to one pipeline-combined JWST/NIRSpec G395H spectrum each of 14 late-T and Y dwarfs. The recommended mask-augmented ensemble returns C/O medians between 0.24 and 0.62 and contains the Hood et al. (2024) value of 0.53 for the T8 benchmark 2MASS J0415-0935, which every fixed-opacity control network excludes. With 90% intervals spanning about 0.43 of the prior width, this is a consistency check, not a validation.

papers.title: Accelerated primal-dual dynamical systems for convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose accelerated inertial primal-dual dynamics for convex optimization problems with nonlinear convex inequality constraints. The proposed dynamics combine Nesterov accelerated vanishing damping $\alpha/t$, a projected augmented-Lagrangian multiplier, and tangent extrapolation of the constraint mapping. Without assuming strong convexity, we establish global well-posedness and simultaneous $\mathcal O(t^{-2})$ decay rates for the constraint violation and the objective residual when $\alpha\geq3$ and the extrapolation parameter satisfies a suitable compatibility condition. Under stricter parameter conditions, with $\alpha>3$, we further prove that the primal-dual trajectory converges to a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker pair, both residuals decay as $o(t^{-2})$. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Coding for Multiple Reverse-Complement and Palindromic Duplications
papers.abstract: Reverse-complement (RC) and palindromic (PAL) duplications insert a reversed copy of a length-$k$ block immediately after the block; an RC duplication also applies a fixed involutive complement to the inserted symbols. We study $q$-ary codes correcting $t$ such operations applied in sequence, where later operations may copy inserted symbols. For fixed $q\geq2$ and $k,t\geq1$, we prove that every length-$n$ code $C$ for either channel has redundancy $n-\log_q|C|\geq t\log_q n-O_{q,k,t}(1)$; for fixed $q,k$ and $1\leq t=t(n)=o(n)$ the lower bound is $t\log_q(n/t)-O_{q,k}(t)$. For fixed $k$, known codes for one length-$k$ insertion burst attain redundancy $\log_q n+O_{q,k}(1)$ for a single duplication of either type. For every even $k$ and any involutive complement, we show that the two channels are equivalent for every number of errors: the bijection complementing every other coordinate turns each RC duplication into a PAL duplication. This bijection therefore converts any $t$-error-correcting RC code into a PAL code of the same size, and conversely, with linear-time transfer of encoders and decoders. For every even $k$, we also determine the maximum number of descendants of one word under exactly two errors; by the bijection, it is the same for both channels. For fixed even $k$, a direct count using this maximum proves the existence of two-error-correcting PAL and RC codes with redundancy at most $4\log_q n+O_{q,k}(1)$. A known existence bound for two deletion bursts transfers to insertions with the same leading term as ours and a larger additive constant. For two errors, the converse gives $2\log_q n-O_{q,k}(1)$, a factor of two below these existence bounds.

papers.title: Dual-polarized, mid-infrared nonreciprocal absorption
papers.abstract: The emission and absorption of thermal radiation are usually coupled via reciprocity and Kirchhoff's law, stated as the equality of spectral directional emissivity and absorptivity. Magneto-optical materials have recently been identified as a promising route to lifting the constraint of reciprocity for thermal emission and absorption, with multiple experimental demonstrations using doped InAs, which is described by an antisymmetric, nonreciprocal dielectric tensor under an applied magnetic field. However, these demonstrations have been limited to p-polarized light in the Voigt configuration, whereas thermal radiation from a blackbody is unpolarized and thus comprised of both s- and p-polarized light. This means existing nonreciprocal emitter and absorber designs underutilize available power by 50%. Here, we report a photonic crystal slab-based structure that exhibits nonreciprocal absorption for both s- and p-polarizations in the mid-infrared spectral range. The structure operates from 11-20 $\mu$m and consists of an a-Si photonic crystal slab on top of a doped InAs substrate. The photonic crystal slab supports eigenmodes that couple to both s- and p-polarized plane waves, resulting in absorption peaks that, because of the applied magnetic field, spectrally shift in opposite directions for forward- and backward-propagating light$\unicode{8212}$a signature of nonreciprocity in planar, subwavelength systems. We fabricate the designed structure, then experimentally demonstrate dual-polarized nonreciprocal absorption by measuring its room-temperature absorptance using magnetic-field-integrated absorptance spectroscopy. Our design is a step toward the complete control of light as heat, which could improve photonic energy conversion, thermal management, and mid-infrared optical isolation and circulation.

papers.title: Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow
papers.abstract: We prove uniqueness of finite-time geometric endpoints for the M\"obius-invariant Willmore flow in $\mathbb{S}^3$ under uniform quantitative nonumbilicity. The multiplicity-counting varifolds converge, without reparametrization or M\"obius renormalization, to a unique integral two-varifold. An intrinsic transport estimate gives quantitative total-variation convergence of the induced area measures on the fixed domain and bounded-Lipschitz Cauchy control of their pushforwards. Together with Allard compactness and rectifiability, this upgrades subsequential compactness to full-trajectory varifold convergence. The limit has generalized Euclidean mean curvature in $L^2$ with the natural endpoint lower-semicontinuity bound. For finite maximal trajectories with initial energy at most $8\pi$, Jakob's subsequential alternative becomes sequence independent: the limit is zero, or it has unit density and embedded Lipschitz support of genus zero or one. For Hopf-torus trajectories under the same energy bound, nonumbilicity is automatic and the anchored constant-speed profiles converge weakly in $W^{2,2}$ and strongly in $W^{1,2}$ and $C^{1,\alpha}$ for every $\alpha<\frac{1}{2}$. At infinite time, the same method yields a unique limit under an additional finite-dissipation-length condition.

papers.title: Proposing GRENDEL: GalleRy ExperimeNt for Decays of Exotic LLPs at the LHC
papers.abstract: Long-lived particles are a generic prediction of Standard Model extensions that address the hierarchy problem, the origin of neutrino masses, the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, and the nature of dark matter. Despite the breadth of theoretical motivation, neutral long-lived particles in the GeV-scale mass range remain difficult to probe at the LHC main detectors, where trigger limitations and challenging backgrounds curtail sensitivity over a wide range of lifetimes. We propose GRENDEL (GalleRy ExperimeNt for Decays of Exotic LLPs), a dedicated detector to be installed in the PX56 drainage gallery at CMS Point~5. The GRENDEL detector will exploit the substantial rock and concrete between the detector and the LHC interaction point as passive shielding in addition to employing active background rejection. Located approximately 24\,m above the interaction point and running largely transverse to the beam, GRENDEL will span around 110\,m and cover the central region $|\eta| < 0.5$. The detector will make use of extruded scintillator bars to achieve competitive sensitivity with other proposed detectors while requiring minimal infrastructure, and without the need for civil engineering. We present the physics case, detector concept, and projected sensitivities to heavy neutral leptons, dark scalars, and axion-like particles covering the $0.2$--$60$\,GeV mass range, for a data sample corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $3\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$ at the High-Luminosity LHC. The benchmarks span the neutrino, scalar, and axion portals, with production through exotic Higgs boson decays, $B$- and $D$-meson decays, and $W/Z$ decays.

papers.title: The Minimal Persona: Rarer and Shared Labels Both Skew Allocation Among AI Agents
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents built on large language models increasingly work in teams, where one agent divides tasks or resources among others that the software marks with a team, a role or a similar label. A model that simply up-weights any recipient sharing a string with its own context would favor same-label peers, so a shared-label tilt alone says little about groups. Borrowing the minimal-group paradigm of social psychology, we had six language models divide 100 points among 19 peers that differed only in carrying one of two invented words, in groups of unequal size (32,400 decisions). Varying group size separates two effects. In five of the six models, at the most unequal split, a recipient with the rarer label received 1.3 to 3.3 times the points of one with the common label even when the decider was not told its own label: a rarity effect that involves no match to the decider. In four of them it accounts for 35% to 55% of the extra favoritism that agents in the smaller group show their own group, and for more in the fifth. Telling the decider its label adds an own-group effect, positive in every model and in five of the six indistinguishable from label matching. With the labels hidden, neither appears. Because the labels mean nothing, bias tests built on lists of named social groups are not designed to detect either effect.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End AI Weather Forecasting: Disentangling Observation and Model Contributions
papers.abstract: End-to-end weather forecasting systems produce skillful global gridded and station forecasts directly from raw Earth observations, replacing the numerical weather prediction pipeline, including data assimilation, at a fraction of its cost. These systems are deterministic and issue no uncertainty. Here we render the Aardvark Weather model probabilistic by attaching one stochastic mechanism to each component: learned, input-dependent noise at the observation encoder, aimed at the uncertainty inherited from the observing system, and Monte Carlo dropout in the processor, aimed at the uncertainty of the learned dynamics. The resulting nested ensemble attributes forecast spread to the two sources through a law-of-total-variance decomposition, cross-checked by withholding observation streams. Probabilistic finetuning significantly improves the mean forecast, by 11% on average across variables and lead times. The ensemble is close to calibrated against ERA5 through the medium range, is at least as accurate as the deterministic model at weather stations while beating it in relative economic value at every lead time, and remains considerably behind the operational ECMWF IFS ensemble. The encoder branch behaves as observation-driven uncertainty. Component-attributed uncertainty makes end-to-end forecasts more transparent, a step toward observation-driven digital twins of the atmosphere.

papers.title: Constraining Baryonic Feedback at $z\sim 1$ with the H$\alpha$ Luminosity Function
papers.abstract: Baryonic feedback remains one of the primary uncertainties in galaxy formation models because of its impact on the interstellar medium (ISM) and star formation. We investigate its effect on the H$\alpha$ luminosity function (LF) using the Illustris and IllustrisTNG simulations. We incorporate direction- and metallicity-dependent dust attenuation, thermal sputtering and a physically motivated treatment of the propagation of Lyman-series photons. We model three sources of H$\alpha$ emission: star-forming H II regions, collisional excitation and recombination in the diffuse ISM, and AGN-induced photo-excitation of diffuse gas. The models are calibrated against observed H$\alpha$ LF at $z\sim1-1.5$ using a single free parameter relating the star formation rate to the H II-region H$\alpha$ luminosity. We find that, for $L_{\text{H}\alpha}\geq 10^{41}\ \rm{erg \ s^{-1}}$, emission from diffuse gas contributes $\sim 5\%-15\%$ of the total H$\alpha$ luminosity in both simulation sets. AGN photo-excitation produces only a modest enhancement of the bright end of the LF, although it dominates the H$\alpha$ emission of Illustris galaxies with $L_{\text{H}\alpha}\gtrsim \times10^{43}\ \rm{erg \ s^{-1}}$. The low-feedback IllustrisTNG simulations provide a good fit to the observed LF for all emission models considered, whereas the high-feedback Illustris predictions are difficult to reconcile with both the bright and faint end of the LF. This tension between H$\alpha$ LF and stacked kSZ measurements highlights the combined power of these probes for constraining the interplay between baryonic feedback, gas properties, and the physics governing emission-line galaxies.

papers.title: On-shell renormalization in NREFT: a simplified description of resonances, bound states, and coupled channel effects
papers.abstract: We discuss several issues regarding the modern generalization of Weinberg's compositeness criterion. In particular, we demonstrate that the on-shell renormalization in NREFT reproduces Weinberg's result and provides a simple description of resonances, bound states, and coupled channel effects. Additionally, we present the complete propagator, including the charged channel for the near-threshold p-wave states.

papers.title: Finite-Width Dissolution of Radial Spectroscopy in Single-Top Mesonic Correlations
papers.abstract: Within the heavy-mass expansion, the pole width of a system containing one unstable heavy constituent inherits the constituent width up to $\mathcal O(\Lambda_{\rm kin}^2/m_Q^2)$ corrections, while radial splittings remain $\mathcal O(\Lambda_{\rm rad})$. The top quark is an extreme realization of this hierarchy. We implement the complex top pole mass in an instantaneous Bethe--Salpeter framework, where a biorthogonal Hellmann--Feynman relation realizes width inheritance at the operator level and an artificial heavy-mass scan confirms the predicted $m_Q^{-2}$ suppression. The low-pole source-projected response has a single broad maximum at the physical top width in the $t\bar b$, $t\bar c$, and $t\bar u$ channels. Full width-dependent non-Hermitian re-diagonalization and a direct full-matrix resolvent evaluation confirm the progressive dissolution of the small-width radial maxima. Thus stable-top eigenvalues survive as reference poles but not as a resolvable multi-peak spectrum; they may instead leave qualitative, process-dependent $Wb\bar q$ signatures, such as a broad threshold enhancement or modified color flow.

papers.title: Bound state of a He-3 atom at free He-4 surfaces
papers.abstract: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations confirm the existence of a bound state of a single He-3 atom at a free superfluid He-4 surface in three dimensions, localized within a ~10-A thick low-density He-4 surface layer, with a binding energy of approximately 5 K with respect to vacuum. As the temperature is raised above ~ 1 K the He-3 atom leaves the surface to dissolve into the superfluid. The situation is entirely different in two dimensions, as the He-3 atom is excluded from the superfluid and no surface bound state exists. Results are also presented for the a He-3 atom binding to nanoscale size He-4 clusters adsorbed on weak substrates, a physical system that may allow for the observation of some of the physics predicted for extended surfaces. It is shown that a He-3 bound state localized at the perimeter of sufficiently small (a few tens of atoms) clusters exists not just on Cs, as previously reported, but on all alkali substrates.

papers.title: Asymptotic Bounds for Online Ramsey Numbers of Stars versus Long Paths and Cycles
papers.abstract: The online Ramsey game for graphs $G$ and $H$ is played on the infinite complete graph $K_\mathbb{N}$. In each round, Builder chooses an edge, and Painter colors it red or blue. The online Ramsey number $\tilde{r}(G,H)$ is the smallest integer $t$ for which Builder has a strategy guaranteeing a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$ within $t$ rounds. For every fixed integer $k\ge4$, the best-known asymptotic lower bounds for $\tilde{r}(K_{1,k},P_n)$ and $\tilde{r}(K_{1,k},C_n)$ are $\left(\frac{k+3}{4}+o(1)\right)n$ as $n\to\infty$. We improve the corresponding asymptotic upper bounds from $\left(k+o(1)\right)n$ to $\left(\frac{k+3}{3}+o(1)\right)n$ as $n\to\infty$.

papers.title: The Higher-Dimensional Nitsche Conjecture: Sharp Bounds and Rigidity
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge3$ and let $h:\A(r,1)\to\A(R,1)\subset\mathbb R^n$ be an onto homeomorphism with harmonic coordinate functions. We prove the sharp Nitsche bound \[ R\le R_{n,+}(r):=\frac{nr}{n-1+r^n}, \] and, when $h$ interchanges the two ends, the strictly stronger sharp bound \[ R\le R_{n,-}(r):=\frac{nr^{n-1}}{1+(n-1)r^n}. \] In each case, equality holds only for the corresponding radial harmonic homeomorphism, up to an orthogonal transformation. Both bounds and their equality cases extend to bounded harmonic maps in every dimension $n\ge2$. This requires nonzero degree of $h/|h|$ on interior spheres, $|h|\ge R$, and the corresponding $L^2$ limits of the modulus at the two ends. In the plane, we also prove the nonzero-winding-number conjecture of Iwaniec--Kovalev--Onninen [\emph{J. Amer. Math. Soc.} \textbf{24} (2011), 345--373], without endpoint modulus conditions. We prove a sharp $L^1$ contraction theorem for vector measures associated with spherical couplings. The first marginal is uniform, while the second is unrestricted. For bounded nonnegative nondecreasing zonal kernels, the optimal constant is the degree-one multiplier. If the kernel is also strictly increasing, equality holds exactly for couplings supported on orthogonal graphs. This theorem is the main tool in the proofs of the annular bounds and their rigidity.

papers.title: Reservoir-Engineered Josephson Diode in a Dark Andreev Channel
papers.abstract: We propose a reservoir-engineered Josephson diode in a double-dot junction with symmetric coherent couplings. A relative phase in the coupling to a common loss reservoir selects a rapidly decaying bright orbital and an orthogonal dark Andreev channel. In the quantum Zeno regime, virtual bright-sector transitions set the dark-channel occupation while preserving its coherent supercurrent. For junctions in the infinite-gap Zeno regime, the steady-state current factorizes as $I_{\rm ss}=I_A P_\gamma$: a reciprocal spectral current $I_A$ is reweighted by the reservoir-selected occupation imbalance $P_\gamma$, which generates rectification. The resulting nonreciprocal current remains finite as reservoir leakage decreases with increasing loss strength. Furthermore, local Coulomb repulsion tunes a dark-pair resonance that enables near-ideal rectification, with induced two-particle loss essential to the quantitative description of the steady current. Keldysh-Lindblad calculations confirm that the results remain robust at finite loss strength and superconducting gap.

papers.title: Surf_2_Volume: A Python Toolbox for Cortical Ribbon Based CIFTI to NIfTI Conversion
papers.abstract: Many neuroimaging workflows require NIfTI label volumes, whereas cortical parcellations are increasingly distributed in CIFTI surface space. Existing conversion tools offer several mapping settings. In nearest vertex mapping, a small distance can leave cortical voxels unlabeled, whereas a larger distance can extend labels beyond the intended cortical region. Choosing among settings is difficult when no paired volume atlas is available. We present Surf_2_Volume, a Python toolbox that projects discrete cortical labels within an adjustable cortical ribbon. Users can specify the ribbon threshold directly or use an optional procedure that ranks candidate thresholds using information from the source atlas. This procedure ranks 12 thresholds by differences between each label's proportion of source cortical vertices and its proportion of output voxels, without using a published volume atlas for selection. We evaluated four configurations from two atlas families: Yeo2011 parcellations with 7 and 17 networks, represented by 51 and 114 spatial components, and Schaefer2018 100-parcel atlases with 7 and 17 network assignments. All four selected sets included threshold 0.05, which had the highest macro-Dice and macro-Jaccard among the tested package thresholds. Eleven of the 12 selected outputs had higher macro-Dice than the best tested Connectome Workbench mapping for their atlas. In 24 HCP participants, all 12 selected outputs had higher participant-level mean parcel time-series concordance than every tested Workbench mapping (all within-atlas FDR-adjusted p < 0.001). Surf_2_Volume provides a reproducible way to generate and select volume atlas candidates when only a surface parcellation is available, while retaining alternatives for different coverage and signal-extraction needs.

papers.title: Quantum estimation theory with quantum noise control
papers.abstract: Quantum estimation theory serves as one of fundamental backbones of quantum Shannon information theory and was mathematically systematized by pioneers of quantum information science. Although its applied research saw limited progress for a long period, the 21st century has witnessed active discussions and numerous fruitful proposals regarding its applications. Notably, the contributions of Monras and Paris represent one of the most remarkable achievements addressing the realization problem of estimation bounds. This paper aims to demonstrate a practical direction for extending their original ideas. Next-generation quantum information mechanisms urgently demand guarantees of quantum advantage unattainable by classical theory, alongside strict real-time processing without delays. By leveraging the concept of generalized heterodyne detection proposed nearly half a century ago, we demonstrate that a scheme based on their results can effectively meet the stringent requirements of near-future information technologies.

papers.title: Hadamard Flattening and Gaussian Pooling Sketch for Least Squares with Coordinate-wise Guarantee
papers.abstract: Randomized sketch-and-solve algorithms accelerate overconstrained $\ell_2$ regression by replacing the input with a much smaller, randomly projected problem. While standard subspace embeddings nearly preserve the regression cost, coordinate-wise accuracy is more delicate: rather than the objective value, we want the solution vector itself to be close to the optimum in $\ell_\infty$ norm. Specifically, we seek $x'\in\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\|x'-x^\star\|_\infty\leq\frac{\epsilon}{\sqrt d}\|Ax^\star-b\|_2\|A^\dagger\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, where $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$ is the design matrix, $b\in\mathbb{R}^n$ the label vector, $x^\star$ the optimal solution and $A^\dagger$ the pseudo-inverse of $A$. Price, Song and Woodruff introduced this problem and claimed that the subsampled randomized Hadamard transform (SRHT) with $O(\epsilon^{-2}d^{1+\Theta(\sqrt{\log\log n/\log d})})$ rows achieves this guarantee; we point out a gap in the proof.
