For $P$ of even degree we prove that $\lambda(P)$ meets every residue class modulo every integer if and only if $P$ has an irrational non-constant coefficient. The same holds for every polynomial $P(x)=ax^n+c$ with $n\ge2$, and for every nonlinear $P$ with $P(x)-P(0)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$. For linear $P$, both properties are characterized completely, and the two notions differ.

papers.title: The finite volume method on Sierpi\'nski simplices
papers.abstract: In the sequel, we extend the Strichartz average approach for the Laplacian, which uses average values of a function over basic sets, rather than pointwise ones as classically done in the literature, and goes back to the seminal work of~S.~Kusuoka and~X.~Y.~Zhou, to Sierpi\'{n}ski Simplices. To our knowledge, the finite volume method had not been applied before to fractals themselves, with their intrinsic Laplacian. We build the finite volume scheme for the heat equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions, give its consistency error, a stability condition of Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy type, obtained by means of an inclusion between the spectrum of the finite volume matrix and the one of the graph Laplacian, and prove the convergence of the scheme. Numerical results are given in the case of the Sierpi\'{n}ski Gasket and Tetrahedron, and compared with the finite difference method.

papers.title: Cavitation near the oscillating piezoelectric plate in water
papers.abstract: Gas and vapor bubbles at a wall can reduce the skin friction of a liquid flow. We estimate whether an oscillating piezoelectric plate mounted flush with the wall can create such a near-wall bubble layer by acoustic cavitation. Once the cavitation threshold is reached, the liquid can no longer follow the receding plate, and the excess plate displacement is accommodated by cavitation bubbles forming at the wall; this kinematic argument gives the bubble volume generated per stroke and its energy cost. Homogeneous cavitation in pure water (about -30 MPa) requires pressure amplitudes far beyond those of flat piezoelectric plates and produces submicron bubbles that collapse within nanoseconds. Heterogeneous cavitation on wall and gas nuclei (-0.1 to -1 MPa) is within reach of piezoceramics and concentrates the void on fewer, larger wal-attached bubbles, which survive between strokes if they exceed a few micrometres at 5 MHz. The acoustic power needed to sustain a bubble layer in a turbulent boundary layer at 10 m/s is about 20 kW/m2 for heterogeneous and about 0.4 MW/m2 for homogeneous cavitation.

papers.title: A weighted edge-count two-sample test for multivariate and object data
papers.abstract: Two-sample tests for multivariate data and non-Euclidean data are widely used in many fields. Parametric tests are mostly restrained to certain types of data that meets the assumptions of the parametric models. In this paper, we study a nonparametric testing procedure that utilizes graphs representing the similarity among observations. It can be applied to any data types as long as an informative similarity measure on the sample space can be defined. The classic test based on a similarity graph has a problem when the two sample sizes are different. We solve the problem by applying appropriate weights to different components of the classic test statistic. The new test exhibits substantial power gains in simulation studies. Its asymptotic permutation null distribution is derived and shown to work well under finite samples, facilitating its application to large datasets. The new test is illustrated through an analysis on a real dataset of network data.

papers.title: Maximal Non-commuting Sets in Certain Unipotent Upper-triangular Linear Groups
papers.abstract:
Let $\omega(G)$ be the maximum size of a set of pairwise non-commuting elements of a group $G$. We determine $\omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))$, where $UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q)$ is the group of $4	imes 4$ unipotent upper-triangular matrices over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, in terms of a classical invariant of finite geometry: we prove that \[ \omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3-q+1+
u(q), \] where $
u(q)$ is the largest size of a partial ovoid of the symplectic generalized quadrangle $\mathrm{W}(3,q)$ disjoint from a fixed line. We show that $
u(q)=q^2$ for even $q$ and $
u(q)=\mu(q)$ for odd $q$, where $\mu(q)$ is the largest size of a partial ovoid of $\mathrm{W}(3,q)$. Consequently $\omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3+q^2-q+1$ for even $q$, while for odd $q$ we obtain $q^3+2q-1\le \omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))\le q^3+q^2-2q+2$; the upper bound rests on a self-contained proof of the inequality $\mu(q)\le q^2-q+1$. In particular $\omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))$ is not a polynomial in $q$, not even for large $q$. This corrects Theorem~$A$ of the published version of this paper, where the value $q^3+q+1+\omega(\mathcal{M})$ was claimed. We also study the non-commuting structures $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ introduced there: we prove that $\omega(\mathcal{M})=q(q-1)$ for even $q$, that $\omega(\mathcal{Q})=\mu(q)-1$ for all $q$, and that for odd $q$ a non-commuting set in $\mathcal{Q}$ consisting of almost $m$ lines exists only for $m\le 5$. Exact values for small $q$ and a list of open problems and conjectures are included. Consequently for odd $q$ \[ \omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3-q+2+\omega(\mathcal{Q}). \]

papers.title: Estimates for the Number of Solutions of Algebraic Diophantine Equations: From the Circle Method to the Manin Conjecture
papers.abstract: This work continues the research of the author on estimates for the number of solutions of algebraic diophantine equations by means of the circle method and develops this line in the geometric direction, towards counting integral points on log Fano varieties. It consists of two parts. Part 1 is the corrected version of the previous work. For diagonal equations $c_1x^{k_1} +...+c_sx^{k_s} = n$ with natural coefficients, upper asymptotic estimates for the number of natural solutions in the range $s \leq 2^k$, where the classical asymptotics is not applicable, are obtained by the circle method and the Hua lemma. The estimates are refined for $s = 2,3,4$ and various $k_i$; in the range $s > 2^k$ they agree with the classical ones. Part 2 develops the same line: from counting solutions of equations to counting integral points on log Fano varieties, where the circle method fails because of insuf ficient dimension. In the log case, the product in the Peyre constant diverges as a harmonic series. A method of analytic compensation is introduced that cancels the divergent term and returns the problem to the range of applicability of the standard scheme. The main result is a method for computing the Peyre log constant with guar anteed accuracy and certified intervals for the number of integral points whenever an estimate of the remainder of the asymptotics is known. The log constant is computable unconditionally, without the Manin conjecture; the conjecture is needed only to interpret it as the leading term of the asymptotics. An experimental verification for the algebraic torus and the Fermat cubic surface is presented.

papers.title: Trees in Random Sparse Graphs with a Given Degree Sequence
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ be the set of graphs $G(V,\, E)$ with $\left|V\right|=n$, and the degree sequence equal to $D=(d_{1},\, d_{2},\,\dots,\, d_{n})$. In addition, for $\frac{1}{2}<a<1$, we define the set of graphs with an almost given degree sequence $D$ as follows, \[ \mathbb{G}_{a}^{D}:=\cup\,\mathbb{G}^{\bar{D}}, \] where the union is over all degree sequences $\bar{D}$ such that, for $1\leq i\leq n$, we have $\left|d_{i}-\bar{d}_{i}\right|<d_{i}^{a}$. Now, if we chose random graphs $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ and $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{a}}\left(D\right)$ uniformly out of the sets $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ and $\mathbb{G}_{a}^{D}$, respectively, what do they look like? This has been studied when $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ is a dense graph, i.e. $\left|E\right|=\Theta(n^{2})$, in the sense of graphons, or when $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ is very sparse, i.e. $d_{n}^{2}=o(\left|E\right|)$. In the case of sparse graphs with an almost given degree sequence, we investigate this question, and give the finite tree subgraph structure of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{a}}\left(D\right)$ under some mild conditions. For the random graph $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ with a given degree sequence, we re-derive the finite tree structure in dense and very sparse cases to give a continuous picture. Moreover, for a pair of vectors $\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)\in\mathbb{Z}^{n_{1}}\times\mathbb{Z}^{n_{2}}$, we let $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{b}}\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$ be the random bipartite graph that is chosen uniformly out of the set $\mathbb{G}^{D_{1},D_{2}}$, where $\mathbb{G}^{D_{1},D_{2}}$ is the set of all bipartite graphs with the degree sequence $\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$. We are able to show the result for $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{b}}\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$ without any further conditions.

papers.title: On some formality criteria for DG-Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We give some formality criteria for a differential graded Lie algebra to be formal. For instance, we show that a DG-Lie algebra L is formal if and only if the natural spectral sequence computing the Chevalley-Eilenberg cohomology H(L,L) degenerates at second page.

papers.title: Emerging of massive gauge particles in inhomogeneous local gauge transformations
papers.abstract: A generalized theory of gauge transformations is presented on the basis of the covariant Hamiltonian formalism of field theory, for which the covariant canonical field equations are equivalent to the Euler-Lagrange field equations. Similar to the canonical transformation theory of point dynamics, the canonical transformation rules for fields are derived from generating functions. Thus---in contrast to the usual Lagrangian description---the covariant canonical transformation formalism automatically ensures the mappings to preserve the action principle, and hence to be {\em physical}. On that basis, we work out the theory of inhomogeneous local gauge transformations that generalizes the conventional local SU(N) gauge transformation theory. It is shown that massive gauge bosons naturally emerge in this description, which thus could supersede the Higgs mechanism.

papers.title: Sharp double logarithmic $L^\infty$ bounds for second-order Sobolev functions in dimension four
papers.abstract: Although $W^{2,2}(\mathbb{R}^{4})$ does not embed into $L^\infty$, we prove that radial symmetry allows the $L^\infty$ norm to be controlled by the homogeneous Sobolev seminorm $\dot H^2$, at the cost of a logarithmic correction involving a stronger H\"older-type norm. Our main result is a sharp double-logarithmic inequality with optimal leading constant $1/(8\pi^2\alpha)$. We also establish a single-logarithmic estimate and prove the sharpness of its threshold. The optimal lower bound is derived by analysing a biharmonic obstacle problem with H\"older-type obstacle. A tailored penalization argument yields existence, uniqueness, and regularity of the minimizer, while an explicit transcendental equation for the free-boundary radius determines the sharp constant through its asymptotic behavior. These results provide fourth-order, four-dimensional analogues of the two-dimensional first-order inequalities of Ibrahim--Majdoub--Masmoudi (\textit{Proc.\ Amer.\ Math.\ Soc.}, 2007), with potential applications to fourth-order semilinear evolution equations with exponential nonlinearities.

papers.title: Energy of test objects on black hole spacetimes: A brief review
papers.abstract: In this paper, we review the issue of defining energy for test particles on a background stationary spacetime. We revisit the different notions of energy as defined by different observers. As is well known, the existence of a time-like isometry allows for the notion of total conserved energy to be well defined. We use this well known quantity to show that a gravitational potential energy can be consistently defined. As examples, we study the case of the exterior regions of an asymptotically flat black hole and of the $\Lambda>0$ Schwarzschild de Sitter case, where an asymptotic region is not available. We then consider the situation in which the test particle is absorbed by the black hole, and analyze the energetics in detail. In particular, we show that the notion of horizon energy as defined by the isolated horizons formalism provides a satisfactory notion of energy compatible with the particle's total conserved energy. With these choices, there is a global conservation of energy. Finally, we comment on a recent proposal to define energy of the black hole as seen by a nearby observer at rest, for which this feature is lost.

papers.title: Triangle Tiling: The case $3\alpha + 2\beta = \pi$
papers.abstract: An $N$-tiling of triangle $ABC$ by triangle $T$ (the ``tile'') is a way of writing $ABC$ as a union of $N$ copies of $T$ overlapping only at their boundaries. Let the tile $T$ have angles $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$, and sides $(a,b,c)$. This paper takes up the case when $3\alpha + 2\beta = \pi$. Then there are (as was already known) exactly five possible shapes of $ABC$ not similar to $T$: either $ABC$ is isosceles with base angles $\alpha$, $\beta$, or $\alpha+\beta$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2\alpha, \alpha, 2\beta)$. We prove that the tile is rational (the ratios of its sides are rational). We then exhibit several families of previously unknown tilings. We also exhibit, for each shape, a Diophantine equation in $N$ and the parameters of the tile that must have a solution whenever there is a tiling of some triangle of that shape. By means of these Diophantine equations, some conclusions about the possible values of $N$ are drawn. We prove, for example, that there is no $N$-tiling with $N$ prime when $3\alpha + 2\beta = \pi$, for three of the five shapes; that question remains open for the shape $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$ and for isosceles triangles with base angles $\beta$. These equations also imply that for each $N$, there is a finite set of possibilities for the tile $(a,b,c)$ and the triangle $ABC$. (Usually, but not always, there is just one possible tile.) For each of the five shapes, we give a construction method that works under certain sufficient conditions, but there remain values of $N$ that satisfy our necessary conditions and for which we do not know whether a tiling exists. All results have been formalized in Lean.

papers.title: The Douglas property for multiplier algebras of operators
papers.abstract: For a collection of reproducing kernels k which includes those for the Hardy space of the polydisk and ball and for the Bergman space, k is a complete Pick kernel if and only if the multiplier algebra of the Hilbert space H^2(k) associated to k has the Douglas property. Consequences for solving the operator equation AX=Y are examined.

papers.title: A Totient Function Inequality
papers.abstract: An unconditional inequality of the totient function is contributed to the literature. This result is associated with various problems about the distribution of prime numbers.

papers.title: Topologically transitive semigroup actions of real linear fractional transformations
papers.abstract: Let $F_I=\{f:I\to I \mid f(x)=(Ax+B)/(Cx+D),\ AD-BC\neq 0\}$, where $I$ is a proper closed subinterval of $\mathbb{R}$. We describe all pairs $f,g\in F_I$ for which the action of the semigroup $\langle f,g \rangle$ generated by $f$ and $g$ is topologically transitive on $I$. It turns out that for such pairs topological transitivity, hypercyclicity, and density of every interior orbit are equivalent. Using the Hilbert metric of $I$ we show that no subsemigroup of $F_I$, with any number of generators, acts in a weakly topologically mixing way on $I$. We classify the pairs of affine maps of $\mathbb{R}$ whose semigroup action is topologically transitive, weakly topologically mixing, or hypercyclic, and we show that such an action is never $3$-transitive. In contrast, there are pairs of real linear fractional transformations whose semigroup action on $\mathbb{R}$ is topologically $3$-transitive, while no semigroup of linear fractional transformations is $4$-transitive.
